Modifiers can be chained: they are applied from left to right, each one receiving the result of the previous one.  {{ $page.post_date|feggDate:'Y/m/d' }} {{ $page.text|lineStrimWidth:80|br }}   Any PHP function works as a modifier: {{ $x|name:arg1:arg2 }} calls name($x, arg1, arg2).Arguments are PHP expressions: quote strings ('Y/m/d'), and use template variables freely (feggDate:$format). A : or | inside a quoted string is part of the string.The result is HTML-escaped like any output, unless noescape is in the chain.Modifiers only run when the variable is set: {{ $missing|feggDefault:'-' }} outputs nothing, so use {{ if }} for defaults. Arrays are passed to modifiers ({{ $tags|feggImplode:', ' }}); when the result is still an array, nothing is output.An unknown modifier is reported by fegg-cli template:lint (see Lint and errors).

searchDocs.title: noescape​
searchDocs.content: Outputs the value without HTML escaping. Use it only for trusted HTML (CMS rich text written by administrators, messages from your own config). See Security and the example in Variable.

searchDocs.title: br​
searchDocs.content: Escapes the value, then converts newlines to <br /> (nl2br).  Controller $this->page['foo'] = "First line.\nSecond line.";   Template {{ $page.foo|br }}   Output First line.<br /> Second line.

searchDocs.title: replace​
searchDocs.content: replace:'pattern':'replacement' replaces with mb_ereg_replace(). The pattern is a regular expression, so escape special characters ('\.').  Template {{ $page.tel|replace:'-':'' }}

searchDocs.title: Fegg modifiers​
searchDocs.content: Defined in htdocs/_fegg/core/functions/modifier.php.  Modifier	DescriptionfeggDate:'Y/m/d'	Formats a date string or a Unix timestamp with the date() format. Also accepts x / X (Japanese day of the week: 火 / 火曜日) and V / v (Japanese era and year: 令和 / 7). Outputs nothing for an empty or invalid date feggImplode:', '	Joins an array with the glue feggDefault:'-'	The replacement when the value is an empty string or an empty array. Does not apply to unset variables feggCheck:'value':'yes':'no'	'yes' when the value is identical (===) to 'value', otherwise 'no' feggReplace:'a':'b'	str_replace('a', 'b', $value) feggPregReplace:'/a/':'b'	preg_replace('/a/', 'b', $value). An optional third argument is the maximum number of replacements feggUrlParam:$params	Appends query parameters (an array or a string) to a URL, with ? or & feggUrl	A URL safe for href / src: any scheme other than http, https, mailto and tel (javascript:, data: …) becomes # feggJs	The value as a JavaScript literal (string, number, array, object, null) with <, >, &, ' and " encoded. Do not put quotes around it. See Security feggYoutube	A YouTube video as the editor embeds it (<div data-youtube-video class="fegg-video"><iframe src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/…">), nothing for another value. Arguments: ratio ('16-9', '9-16'), alignment ('center', 'right'), width in %. Print it with noescape. See Embed feggMap	A Google map as the editor embeds it, from the <iframe> Google Maps gives or its URL; nothing for another value. Arguments: ratio ('4-3', '16-9', '1-1'), alignment, width in %. Print it with noescape. See Embed  Controller $this->page['post_date'] = '2025-04-01 10:00:00'; $this->page['category'] = '1'; $this->page['data']['link'] = 'javascript:alert(1)'; $this->page['query'] = array('category' => 2, 'p' => 3); $this->setSiteinfo('prefix', '/news/');   Template {{ $page.post_date|feggDate:'Y年n月j日(x)' }} <li class="c-tab{{ $page.category|feggCheck:'1':' is-active':'' }}"> <a href="{{ $page.data.link|feggUrl }}">Link</a> <a href="{{ $site.prefix|feggUrlParam:$page.query }}">Search</a>   Output 2025年4月1日(火) <li class="c-tab is-active"> <a href="#">Link</a> <a href="/news/?category=2&amp;p=3">Search</a>

searchDocs.title: Joining an array​
searchDocs.content: Template {{ $page.tags|feggImplode:', ' }}

searchDocs.title: CMS modifiers​
searchDocs.content: Defined in htdocs/_fegg/core/functions/cms-modifier.php and model.php.  Modifier	DescriptiongetImageUrl	URL of a CMS image from its ID getImageUrl:320	Resized to a width of 320px getImageUrl:780:360	Resized to 780 × 360px. A third argument changes the crop mode in the file name (default 'i') getImageUrlFromDB, getImageUrlFromDB:320, getImageUrlFromDB:780:360	URL that generates the image on every request (/cms/image/get/...) getFileUrl	URL of a CMS file from its ID getFileRawUrl	Direct URL of the stored file (looks the file up in cms_file) byteConvert	A byte count as a readable size: 1536 → 1.5 KB lineStrimWidth:40	Removes tags and newlines, then shortens the text to a display width of 40, adding …. A second argument replaces … url2link	Turns URLs in text into <a> links. The result is HTML: see the warning below feggCategoryLabel:'news'	Label of a category ID, from the list news of site/config/category_info.php  Template <img src="{{ $page.data.image_id|getImageUrl:780:360 }}" alt=""> <a href="{{ $page.data.file_id|getFileUrl }}">Download</a> <span class="c-label">{{ $post.category|feggCategoryLabel:'news' }}</span> <p>{{ $post.body|lineStrimWidth:80 }}</p>   warning url2link returns HTML and does not escape the rest of the text, so it needs noescape. Use it only on trusted text (written by administrators in the CMS), never on user input.

searchDocs.title: Project modifiers​
searchDocs.content: Put your own modifiers in htdocs/_fegg/site/functions/*.php. These files are loaded automatically after the core's. Every file under htdocs/_fegg/ starts with the direct-access guard.  htdocs/_fegg/site/functions/modifier.php <?php defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; function priceFormat($value) { return number_format((int) $value) . ' yen'; }   Template {{ $page.price|priceFormat }}   The skeleton defines isNew($date, $gap = 2): true when the date is less than $gap days old. Use it in a condition: {{ if isNew($post.post_date) }}NEW{{ end }}.

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: {{ if condition }} {{ else if condition }} {{ else }} {{ end }}   Outputs a part of the template only when a condition is true. The condition is a PHP expression: comparison and logical operators (===, >, &&, ||, ! …) and PHP functions (is_array, count …) work, with template variables written as usual ($page.foo).  {{ if $var }} with a single variable checks isset($var) && $var: it is false when the variable is not set.In any other expression, a variable that is not set reads as null without a warning, so {{ if $page.count > 0 }} is safe when count is missing.{{ elseif }} (without a space) is accepted as well as {{ else if }}.{{ end }} closes the block. {{ else }} or {{ else if }} outside an if, a missing {{ end }} or an extra one is an error reported with its line (see Lint and errors).

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Template {{ if $page.foo === 'bar' }} foo is bar {{ else if $page.foo === 'baz' }} foo is baz {{ else }} foo is neither bar nor baz {{ end }}

searchDocs.title: Checking whether a value is set​
searchDocs.content: Template {{ if $page.image_id }} <img src="{{ $page.image_id|getImageUrl }}" alt=""> {{ end }} {{ if !isset($page.data) || count($page.data) === 0 }} <p>No news yet.</p> {{ end }}

searchDocs.title: Using a function​
searchDocs.content: Template {{ if isNew($post.post_date) }}<span class="c-label">NEW</span>{{ end }}   isNew() is defined by the skeleton in htdocs/_fegg/site/functions/modifier.php. Functions defined there can be called in any expression.

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: {{ hidden }}   Prints an <input type="hidden"> for every value set with setHidden() in the controller.  Put it inside the <form>. It is typically used to carry an ID or a one-time ticket from the input screen to the confirmation and save steps.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $this->setHidden('internal_id', 12);   Template <form method="post" action="{{ base }}/contact/confirm/"> {{ hidden }} <button type="submit">Send</button> </form>   Output <form method="post" action="/contact/confirm/"> <input type="hidden" name="internal_id" value="12"> <button type="submit">Send</button> </form>

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: {{ include '/path/to/template' }}   Renders another template at this place, with the same variables. Variables the included template assigns do not come back to the including one.  {{ include head '/path/to/template' }} {{ head }} {{ include foot '/path/to/template' }} {{ foot }}   {{ include head }} and {{ include foot }} do not output anything where they are written. They queue a template that is rendered later where the layout writes {{ head }} (in <head>) or {{ foot }} (before </body>). A page uses them to add its own CSS or JavaScript to the shared layout. When several templates queue partials (a page and the layouts it transcludes), the partials of the outer layouts come first.  {{ include html '/parts/banner.html' }}   {{ include html }} includes a file under the document root (htdocs/) with PHP's include. The path starts with / and has its extension. It is not a template: {{ }} tags in it are not compiled.

searchDocs.title: Paths​
searchDocs.content: Template paths have no .tpl extension.A path starting with / is relative to the template root: the tpl/ of the site the URL belongs to (for /cms/..., site/template/cms/tpl/), then core/template/. Prefer it: it works the same from any directory.A path without / is relative to the directory of the template that contains the tag (./parts/card, ../include/head/news). For include head / include foot, it stays relative to the template that queued it.  {{ transclude '/template/siteframe' }} site/template/main/tpl/template/siteframe.tpl {{ transclude '/cms/frame/siteframe' }} site/template/cms/tpl/frame/siteframe.tpl, else core/template/cms/frame/siteframe.tpl {{ include head '/include/head/about' }} site/template/main/tpl/include/head/about.tpl {{ include './parts/card' }} parts/card.tpl next to this template   A missing target throws Fegg\Template\TemplateException (HTTP 500). ./fegg-cli template:lint reports missing targets before you deploy (see Lint and errors).

searchDocs.title: include​
searchDocs.content: site/template/main/tpl/parts/card.tpl <div class="c-card">{{ $page.title }}</div>   site/template/main/tpl/news/detail.tpl <p>Before</p> {{ include '/parts/card' }}   Output <p>Before</p> <div class="c-card">Hello</div>

searchDocs.title: include head / include foot​
searchDocs.content: site/template/main/tpl/include/head/about.tpl <link rel="stylesheet" href="{{ $site.assets }}/css/about.css">   site/template/main/tpl/include/foot/about.tpl <script src="{{ $site.assets }}/js/about.js"></script>   site/template/main/tpl/about.tpl {{ transclude '/template/siteframe' }} {{ include head '/include/head/about' }} {{ include foot '/include/foot/about' }} {{ section contents }} <p>About us</p> {{ end section contents }}   site/template/main/tpl/template/siteframe.tpl <!DOCTYPE html> <html lang="ja"> <head> <meta charset="UTF-8"> <title>{{ $site.title }}</title> {{ head }} </head> <body> {{ section contents }} {{ end section contents }} {{ foot }} </body> </html>   Output <!DOCTYPE html> <html lang="ja"> <head> <meta charset="UTF-8"> <title>Example Inc.</title> <link rel="stylesheet" href="/_fegg/site/template/main/css/about.css"> </head> <body> <p>About us</p> <script src="/_fegg/site/template/main/js/about.js"></script> </body> </html>   note Write {{ include head }} and {{ include foot }} at the top level of the template, not inside a {{ section }} (see Transclude).

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: {-{ ... }-} {--{ ... }--}   Fegg treats every {{ ... }} as a tag. To output literal double braces, for example a Vue or Handlebars template inside the page, or copy that contains them, write {-{ for {{ and }-} for }}. The text between them is not compiled.  {-{ also removes the spaces directly before it, and }-} the spaces directly after it (a {-{ x }-} b outputs a{{ x }}b). {--{ and }--} work the same but remove all whitespace there, newlines included.  Single braces ({, }) in HTML, CSS and JavaScript need nothing special.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Template <div id="app"> <p>{-{ message }-}</p> </div> <script> Vue.createApp({ data() { return { message: 'Hello' }; } }).mount('#app'); </script>   Output <div id="app"> <p>{{ message }}</p> </div> <script> Vue.createApp({ data() { return { message: 'Hello' }; } }).mount('#app'); </script>

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: {{ options source=$list selected=$currentValue }}   Prints one <option> for each element of source: the array key is the value attribute and the array value is the label. Both are HTML-escaped.  The option whose key equals selected (compared as strings) gets the selected attribute. selected is optional. Nothing is printed when source is empty.  Write the arguments without spaces inside them (source=$page.categories, not an expression). For a multiple select, use checked/selected in a foreach instead.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $this->page['categories'] = array( '1' => 'News', '2' => 'Events & Seminars', );   Template <select name="category"> <option value="">All</option> {{ options source=$page.categories selected=$in.category }} </select>   Output (request ?category=2) <select name="category"> <option value="">All</option> <option value='1'>News</option><option value='2' selected>Events &amp; Seminars</option> </select>

searchDocs.title: foreach​
searchDocs.content: {{ foreach $array as $key => $value }} {{ end foreach }} {{ foreach $array as $value }} {{ end }}   Repeats the block for every element of an array, like PHP's foreach. The key is optional. The block is closed by {{ end foreach }} or simply {{ end }}.  When the array is not set, the block is skipped without a warning.$foreachIndex counts the iterations from 0. In nested loops, the inner loop has its own $foreachIndex and the outer value is restored when the inner loop ends. After a loop, $foreachIndex holds the number of iterations.The key and value variables live in the same namespace as $page, $site …: {{ foreach $list as $page }} overwrites $page. Pick other names.

searchDocs.title: loop​
searchDocs.content: {{ loop $i = 1 to 10 }} {{ end }}   Counts from the first bound to the second, both included: {{ loop $i = 1 to 10 }} is for ($i = 1; $i <= 10; $i++). Each bound is a number or a variable ($page.pager.last_page), not an expression. A bound that is not set reads as null. Close the block with {{ end }}.

searchDocs.title: foreach​
searchDocs.content: Controller $this->page['list'] = array('foo' => 'bar', 'baz' => 'qux');   Template <ul> {{ foreach $page.list as $key => $value }} <li>{{ $foreachIndex }} : {{ $key }} => {{ $value }}</li> {{ end foreach }} </ul>   Output <ul> <li>0 : foo => bar</li> <li>1 : baz => qux</li> </ul>

searchDocs.title: Nested foreach​
searchDocs.content: Controller $this->page['rows'] = array(array('a', 'b'), array('c', 'd', 'e'));   Template {{ foreach $page.rows as $row }}[{{ foreach $row as $cell }}{{ $cell }}{{ end }}:{{ $foreachIndex }}]{{ end }}   Output [ab:0][cde:1]

searchDocs.title: loop​
searchDocs.content: Controller $this->page['max'] = 5;   Template <ul> {{ loop $i = 1 to $page.max }} <li>{{ $i }}</li> {{ end }} </ul>   Output <ul> <li>1</li> <li>2</li> <li>3</li> <li>4</li> <li>5</li> </ul>

searchDocs.title: Escaping by context​
searchDocs.content: {{ $x }} escapes the value with htmlspecialchars (ENT_QUOTES). That is right for HTML text and for quoted attribute values, but not enough in URLs and JavaScript. Use the modifier that matches the place:  Where the value goes	WriteHTML text, quoted attribute values	{{ $x }} <textarea>	{{ $x }} (the browser shows the original text) href / src / action / formaction taking a URL from data	href="{{ $x|feggUrl }}" Inside <script>	var x = {{ $x|feggJs|noescape }}; (no quotes around it) Event attributes (onclick …)	onclick="go({{ $x|feggJs }})" (no quotes around it, keep the escaping) Trusted HTML (CMS rich text saved through HtmlSanitizer::clean(), messages from your config)	{{ $x|noescape }} A YouTube URL or a Google map from a CMS field	{{ $x|feggYoutube|noescape }}, {{ $x|feggMap|noescape }} (the modifier checks and escapes the URL)  Always quote attribute values (class="{{ $x }}", not class={{ $x }}).  ./fegg-cli template:lint reports outputs in <script>, event attributes and URLs that lack the right modifier (see Lint and errors).

searchDocs.title: URLs: feggUrl​
searchDocs.content: HTML escaping does not stop a javascript: URL. feggUrl returns # for any URL whose scheme is not http, https, mailto or tel (also when the scheme is disguised with spaces or control characters). Relative URLs are kept.  Template <a href="{{ $page.data.link|feggUrl }}">{{ $page.data.link_label }}</a>   URLs built by the CMS modifiers (getImageUrl, getImageUrlFromDB, getFileUrl, getFileRawUrl) and values from $site (your configuration) do not need it.

searchDocs.title: JavaScript: feggJs​
searchDocs.content: feggJs turns any value (string, number, array, object, null) into a JavaScript literal and encodes <, >, &, ' and ", so the value can neither end the string nor close the <script> element. It writes the quotes itself: do not add your own.  Inside a script element: add noescape <script> var title = {{ $page.title|feggJs|noescape }}; </script>   In an event attribute: keep the escaping <button type="button" onclick="showItem({{ $item.id|feggJs }})">Show</button>   In an attribute, the browser decodes the HTML escaping before it runs the JavaScript, so the normal {{ }} escaping must stay: never add noescape there.  tip Arrays and objects work too, so a whole data set can go to a script in one line: Template <script> var items = {{ $page.items|feggJs|noescape }}; // [{"id":1,"title":"..."}, ...] </script>

searchDocs.title: noescape​
searchDocs.content: noescape outputs the value as it is. Use it only for HTML you trust: CMS rich text written by administrators and cleaned with Fegg\Cms\HtmlSanitizer::clean() when it was saved (see CMS screens and the editor), validation messages from your config, the result of feggJs inside <script>, or the result of feggYoutube / feggMap. Never use it on $in (request parameters) or anything a visitor can type.

searchDocs.title: Templates are code​
searchDocs.content: {{ code }}, conditions, {{ assign }} and modifiers run arbitrary PHP. Treat templates like PHP files:  Only developers may edit templates. Never let site users upload or edit .tpl files.Never build a template name, an include path or a modifier name from user input.A controller that picks the template from its URL arguments implements Fegg\Http\RouteOnly, so only site/config/route.php reaches it (see Route-only controllers).

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: {{ base }} {{ base_url }} {{ current_url }}   Tag	Output	Example{{ base }}	URL path of the site root, without a trailing slash. Empty when the site is at the document root	(empty), /sub {{ base_url }}	Scheme, host (and port) plus {{ base }}: the absolute URL of the site root	https://example.com, https://example.com/sub {{ current_url }}	Absolute URL of the current request, including the query string	https://example.com/news/?p=2  All three are HTML-escaped.  Start every link with {{ base }}/, so the site keeps working when it is installed in a subdirectory. Write the site's CSS, JS and images with {{ $site.assets }}/, which already contains {{ base }} (see Sites). Use {{ base_url }} and {{ current_url }} where an absolute URL is required (canonical, OGP).

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Template <link rel="stylesheet" href="{{ $site.assets }}/css/style.css"> <a href="{{ base }}/news/">News</a> <img src="{{ $site.assets }}/img/common/pc/logo.png" alt=""> <link rel="canonical" href="{{ current_url }}"> <meta property="og:image" content="{{ base_url }}/_fegg/site/template/main/img/ogp.png">   Output (site at https://example.com/, page /news/?p=2) <link rel="stylesheet" href="/_fegg/site/template/main/css/style.css"> <a href="/news/">News</a> <img src="/_fegg/site/template/main/img/common/pc/logo.png" alt=""> <link rel="canonical" href="https://example.com/news/?p=2"> <meta property="og:image" content="https://example.com/_fegg/site/template/main/img/ogp.png">

searchDocs.title: URL and Controller class​
searchDocs.content: Fegg maps URL segments to a controller class, a method and its arguments:  https://example.com/class/method/param1/param2/   Controller class (site/controller/Class.php, first letter in upper case)Method of the controller classArguments for the method  When the method segment is empty, index() is called. When no segment names a controller, the Index controller of that directory is used.  Sub directories of site/controller/ are part of the URL and of the namespace:  URL	File	Called/	site/controller/Index.php	Site\Controller\Index::index() /news/	site/controller/News.php	Site\Controller\News::index() /news/detail/12/	site/controller/News.php	Site\Controller\News::detail('12') /cms/news/edit/3/	site/controller/Cms/News.php	Site\Controller\Cms\News::edit('3') /cms/media/	core/controller/Cms/Media.php (no site class)	Fegg\Controller\Cms\Media::index()  The site (Site\Controller\...) is searched first, then the core (Fegg\Controller\...). A site class with the same name replaces the core's CMS screen (see Controller).Segments are walked from the left; the first one that names a controller file wins over a directory with the same name.Controller and directory names must be valid PHP class names (letters, digits, _). For URLs like /about-us/, use a route.Abstract classes (the base Controller classes) are never called from a URL.Only the controller's own actions can be called; any other method is a 404 (see Which methods are actions).If no controller or no method matches, the NotFound controller renders the 404 page.  Arguments are always strings.

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: {{ $var }} {{ $var.key.sub }} {{ $var|modifier }}   {{ $var }} outputs a variable. Array elements are separated with a period: $var.key.sub is $var['key']['sub']. Numeric keys and keys that are PHP keywords work too ($rows.0.name, $item.new, $site.default). Square brackets take an expression as the key: $page.data[$id], $map[$key].name.  Values from the controller are set in $this->page and read as $page in the template. The other variables available in a page are listed in Application::fetchPage.  The output is escaped with htmlspecialchars (ENT_QUOTES), which is right for HTML text and quoted attribute values. Other places (URLs, JavaScript) need a modifier: see Security. To output trusted HTML as it is, use the noescape modifier (see Modifiers).  Nothing is output (and no error is raised) when the variable is not set, or when it is an array and no modifier is applied. Modifiers receive arrays, so {{ $tags|feggImplode:', ' }} and {{ $items|feggJs|noescape }} work; a chain whose result is still an array outputs nothing.  Inside a tag, $a.b is always array access. To concatenate strings in an expression (if, assign …), write the PHP operator with spaces: $a . $b.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $this->page['title'] = 'Hello'; $this->page['rows'] = array( array('name' => 'first'), ); $this->displayPage('template');   Template {{ $page.title }} {{ $page.rows.0.name }} {{ $page.missing }}   Output Hello first

searchDocs.title: Escaping and noescape​
searchDocs.content: Controller $this->page['foo'] = '<p>bar</p>';   Template {{ $page.foo }} {{ $page.foo|noescape }}   Output &lt;p&gt;bar&lt;/p&gt; <p>bar</p>   Use noescape only for HTML you trust (see Security).

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: {{ transclude '/path/to/layout' }} {{ section name }} {{ end section name }}   {{ transclude }} makes the template inherit a layout (the parent template). The parent declares named {{ section }} blocks; the child fills them, and the parent prints each one where it is declared.  In the parent, a section is a placeholder. Its content is the default, printed when the child does not define the section.In the child, a section defines the content. The section name must match the parent's.Inheritance works through any number of levels: a child can fill a section declared by its parent or by any layout further up.A template has one {{ transclude }}. Paths follow the include rules: prefer /-rooted paths such as '/template/siteframe'. A missing parent throws Fegg\Template\TemplateException with the line of the tag.Close a section with {{ end section name }} (recommended) or {{ end section }}.  Things to know:  Text outside any {{ section }} in a child template is output before the parent layout. Keep everything inside sections (fegg-cli template:lint warns about stray text).A section runs as a function. {{ assign }}, {{ include head }} and {{ include foot }} written inside it only affect that section. Put them at the top level of the template, next to {{ transclude }}.A section the parent does not declare is printed where the child defines it.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: site/template/main/tpl/template/siteframe.tpl <!DOCTYPE html> <html lang="ja"> <head> <meta charset="UTF-8"> <title>{{ $site.title }}</title> </head> <body> <main> {{ section contents }} <p>Default content</p> {{ end section contents }} </main> </body> </html>   site/template/main/tpl/index.tpl {{ transclude '/template/siteframe' }} {{ section contents }} <p>This is the index content.</p> {{ end section contents }}   Output <!DOCTYPE html> <html lang="ja"> <head> <meta charset="UTF-8"> <title>Example Inc.</title> </head> <body> <main> <p>This is the index content.</p> </main> </body> </html>

searchDocs.title: Multiple levels​
searchDocs.content: site/template/main/tpl/base.tpl <html> <body> {{ section header }}<header>Default header</header>{{ end section header }} {{ section body }}{{ end section body }} </body> </html>   site/template/main/tpl/layout/two_columns.tpl {{ transclude '/base' }} {{ section body }} <div class="l-columns"> <aside>Menu</aside> <div class="l-columns__main"> {{ section main }}{{ end section main }} </div> </div> {{ end section body }}   site/template/main/tpl/news/detail.tpl {{ transclude '/layout/two_columns' }} {{ section header }}<header>News</header>{{ end section header }} {{ section main }} <p>This is the news content.</p> {{ end section main }}   Output (whitespace simplified) <html> <body> <header>News</header> <div class="l-columns"> <aside>Menu</aside> <div class="l-columns__main"> <p>This is the news content.</p> </div> </div> </body> </html>   news/detail fills header, which is declared two levels up in base, and main, which is declared by its direct parent.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: URL https://example.com/post/edit/1/   htdocs/_fegg/site/controller/Post.php <?php namespace Site\Controller; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; class Post extends Controller { public function edit($id) { echo $id; // Result: 1 } }

searchDocs.title: Trailing slash​
searchDocs.content: URLs without an extension are normalised to end with /. A GET or HEAD request to /news/detail/1 is redirected (301) to /news/detail/1/, keeping the query string (/news?p=2 → /news/?p=2). Other methods (POST, ...) are handled in place without a redirect. URLs with an extension (/news/post_1.html) are not changed.  Write links in templates with the trailing slash to avoid the extra redirect.

searchDocs.title: Routing​
searchDocs.content: To use URLs that do not follow the class/method structure, add routes to htdocs/_fegg/site/config/route.php:  $route['from'] = 'to';   The key is the URL (without the leading /) and the value is the class/method/arguments path it is mapped to.  Routes without wildcards are checked first. Then the routes are tried in the order they are written, and the first match wins. Put specific routes above general ones.A route without an extension matches the URL with or without a trailing slash ('contact/' matches /contact and /contact/).When no route matches, the URL itself is used as the path.

searchDocs.title: Wildcards​
searchDocs.content: Wildcard	Matches:num	Digits only ([0-9]+) :any	One segment: any characters except /  Refer to the matched values with $1, $2, ... in the value.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: htdocs/_fegg/site/config/route.php <?php defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; // Handle index.html (in the skeleton by default) $route[':any/index.html'] = '$1/index'; // https://example.com/news/index.html -> Site\Controller\News::index() $route['news/post_:num.html'] = 'news/detail/$1'; // https://example.com/news/post_1.html -> Site\Controller\News::detail('1') $route['item/:any/'] = 'product/item_lookup/$1'; // https://example.com/item/foobar/ -> Site\Controller\Product::item_lookup('foobar') $route['contact/'] = 'contact/index'; $route['contact/confirm.html'] = 'contact/confirm'; // https://example.com/contact/confirm.html -> Site\Controller\Contact::confirm()

searchDocs.title: Static pages​
searchDocs.content: Pages that have no data of their own do not need a controller. Route them to the skeleton's Site\Controller\Page, which renders the template named in the route:  htdocs/_fegg/site/config/route.php $route['about/'] = 'page/render/about'; // site/template/main/tpl/about.tpl $route['guide/:any.html'] = 'page/render/guide/$1'; // site/template/main/tpl/guide/*.tpl $route['recruit/jobs/'] = 'page/render/jobs'; // site/template/recruit/tpl/jobs.tpl   The template is read from the tpl/ of the site the URL belongs to (see Sites).  Page::render() joins its arguments into the template path. If the template does not exist, it redirects to the top page.

searchDocs.title: Route-only controllers​
searchDocs.content: Page implements the marker interface Fegg\Http\RouteOnly. A controller that implements it is only called through a route in route.php. The default /class/method/arguments mapping skips it, so /page/render/about/ typed in the browser is a 404. This way a visitor cannot choose which template Page renders; only the routes you write can.  Use RouteOnly for your own controllers whose arguments must not come straight from the URL:  htdocs/_fegg/site/controller/Landing.php <?php namespace Site\Controller; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; use Fegg\Http\RouteOnly; class Landing extends Controller implements RouteOnly { public function show($campaign) { $this->page['campaign'] = $campaign; $this->displayPage('landing/' . $campaign); } }   htdocs/_fegg/site/config/route.php $route['campaign/spring/'] = 'landing/show/spring';

searchDocs.title: Namespaces​
searchDocs.content: Classes are loaded by the core's own autoloader (core/bootstrap/autoload.php). Composer is not required; in the skeleton it is only used for the test suite.  Namespace	DirectoryFegg\	core/src/ Fegg\Controller\	core/controller/ Fegg\Command\	core/bin/ Site\	site/src/ Site\Controller\	site/controller/  Sub directories are namespaces: site/src/Shop/Cart.php is Site\Shop\Cart, site/controller/Cms/News.php is Site\Controller\Cms\News.  Every PHP file under htdocs/_fegg/ must start with defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit;. It stops the file from doing anything when it is requested directly from a URL.

searchDocs.title: Overriding the core​
searchDocs.content: The site is searched first, then the core. This works like a WordPress child theme.  What	How	ExampleTemplates	Put a file in site/template/cms/tpl/ at the path it has under core/template/cms/	site/template/cms/tpl/login.tpl is used instead of core/template/cms/login.tpl Config files	Put a file with the same name in site/config/	site/config/validation_error_message.php replaces the core's messages Settings	Write only the keys you want to change in site/config/settings.php	$settings['developer_ip'] = array(...); CMS screens	Put a class that extends the core controller in site/controller/, with only the methods you change	See Controller CMS menu	Add one block to site/config/cms_menu.php	When you add a post type DB tables	Put a YAML file in site/config/database/ (a file with the same name wins over the core's)	cms_news.yaml

searchDocs.title: Entry files and layout​
searchDocs.content: htdocs/index.php and fegg-cli belong to the project. They only define three paths and then load the core:  htdocs/index.php <?php define('FEGG_HTML_DIR', __DIR__); // document root define('FEGG_CORE_DIR', __DIR__ . '/_fegg/core'); // core define('FEGG_SITE_DIR', __DIR__ . '/_fegg/site'); // site require FEGG_CORE_DIR . '/bootstrap/web.php';   fegg-cli defines the same three constants and requires core/bootstrap/cli.php. Always keep the paths in the two files consistent. Templates for both are in core/dist/.  Layout	Entry fileStandard: htdocs/_fegg/ (always inside the document root: the CMS's CSS and JS are served from _fegg/assets/)	core/dist/index.php.dist The document root has a different name (public_html, etc.)	Keep the standard one. Only fix FEGG_HTML_DIR in fegg-cli Installed in a subdirectory (https://example.com/sub/)	Keep the standard one. The URL base is detected from SCRIPT_NAME

searchDocs.title: Protecting _fegg/​
searchDocs.content: In the standard layout _fegg/ is inside the document root. It is protected in layers:  htdocs/_fegg/.htaccess denies all requests. _fegg/assets/.htaccess and the .htaccess of each site folder (site/template/<site>/) let only CSS, JS, images and fonts through; site/up_dir/.htaccess only the file types that can be uploaded (see Upload).htdocs/.htaccess returns 403 for /_fegg/ (except the CSS, JS, images and fonts of _fegg/assets/ and of each site folder's css/ js/ img/ font/, and the files of _fegg/site/up_dir/), dotfiles and hidden directories (.git/; .well-known/ stays reachable), and denies .db, .sqlite, .yaml, .tpl, .log, .md, .json and .dist files.Every PHP file under _fegg/ and every compiled template starts with the guard line (see Namespaces).fegg-cli doctor https://example.com checks over HTTP that nothing under _fegg/ (a site's SCSS sources included) and no database file can be read (see fegg-cli). Run it from your local machine after every upload: many FTP clients skip .htaccess. The CMS dashboard also warns about problems it can detect from the files, such as a missing .htaccess.If the server allows it, put the SQLite database outside the document root (see Settings).  On nginx, where .htaccess is not used, add equivalent rules:  # The CMS's files (_fegg/assets/) and each site's (_fegg/site/template/<site>/{css,js,img,font}/) first # (nginx uses the first regex that matches) location ~* ^/_fegg/(assets|site/template/[a-z0-9-]+/(css|js|img|font))/[^?]+\.(css|js|map|png|jpe?g|gif|svg|webp|woff2?|ico)$ { } # The uploaded files (_fegg/site/up_dir/): the uploaded file types only, never scripts; a missing image # size and /file/<id>/ go to PHP. ^~ keeps the regex locations below (and the PHP handler) out location ^~ /_fegg/site/up_dir/ { location ~* \.(jpe?g|png|gif|webp|pdf|docx?|docm|dotx|dotm|xlsx?|xlsm|xltx|xltm|xlsb|xlam|pptx?|pptm|ppsx|ppsm|potx|potm|ppam|sldx|sldm|thmx|one|zip|txt|csv)$ { try_files $uri /index.php?$query_string; } location ~ /\. { deny all; } location ~* \.[a-z0-9]+$ { deny all; } rewrite ^ /index.php last; } location ~ (^|/)_fegg(/|$) { deny all; } location ~ /\.(?!well-known/) { deny all; } location ~* \.(tpl|db|sqlite|ya?ml|log|md|json|dist)$ { deny all; }

searchDocs.title: 1. List what the old project has of its own​
searchDocs.content: Find the skeleton version the project started from (version in package.json, or @version in fegg/Application.php). Check out the skeleton at that tag, copy the project's core files over it (fegg/, code/lib/, code/application/cms/, code/template/cms/, htdocs/cms/, htdocs/index.php, htdocs/.htaccess) and look at git diff. Write down:  Changes to the core: Fegg 5 rewrote most of the core, so decide for each whether the project still needs it. What is still needed is written again as an override in site/ (see Controller).The project's own code: controllers (public pages and post types), project libraries in code/lib/, code/lib/Modifire.php, processing added to MyApplication.The project's own files: templates, htdocs/data/ (SCSS, JS, images), table definitions, config values, code/data/, uploads.

searchDocs.title: 2. Start from the Fegg 5 skeleton​
searchDocs.content: Replace the branch's contents with the Fegg 5 skeleton (everything except .git) and rename it as for any new project (the package name in package.json, the local URL in e2e/playwright.config.ts).Copy site/config/env.php.dist to site/config/env.php on each development or staging server and set 'FEGG_ENV' => 'development': without it the site runs as production and shows no error details (see Settings).Set the values the project changed in the old fegg/settings.php (developer_ip, run_mode, maintenance_page_url, Basic authentication, languages) in site/config/settings.php.Add the project's own rules of the old htdocs/.htaccess (redirects, headers) to the new one. If the project changed the paths in index.php, set the three constants (FEGG_HTML_DIR, FEGG_CORE_DIR, FEGG_SITE_DIR) to match (see Directory structure).

searchDocs.title: 3. Bring over the files that carry over​
searchDocs.content: v3 / v4	Fegg 5htdocs/data/ (SCSS, JS, images)	htdocs/_fegg/site/template/main/ (scss/, js/, img/; npm run build:scss) htdocs/cms/scss/unique.scss (the project's CMS styles)	htdocs/_fegg/site/template/cms/scss/unique.scss code/template/ except cms/	htdocs/_fegg/site/template/main/tpl/ (check with ./fegg-cli template:lint) code/template/cms/<post type>/	htdocs/_fegg/site/template/cms/tpl/<post type>/ code/config/database/ (project tables)	htdocs/_fegg/site/config/database/ Project values in code/config/	Merged into the skeleton's files in htdocs/_fegg/site/config/ code/data/	htdocs/_fegg/site/data/ htdocs/up_dir/	htdocs/_fegg/site/up_dir/ (served at /_fegg/site/up_dir/) The post types in the old CMS menu	htdocs/_fegg/site/config/cms_menu.php, one block each  fegg/, the core's libraries in code/lib/, the core's CMS screens and templates, bin/ and htdocs/cms/ are not brought over: the skeleton has their Fegg 5 versions.  Template paths are relative to main/tpl/ (see Sites). In the templates, replace {{ base }}/data/ with {{ $site.assets }}/ ({{ $site.assets }}/css/style.css, {{ $site.assets }}/img/...).  The uploaded files' URL becomes /_fegg/site/up_dir/.... Rich text saved in the database still links to /up_dir/: replace it in every column that holds rich text, for example:  UPDATE cms_news SET content = REPLACE(content, '/up_dir/', '/_fegg/site/up_dir/');   The database is used as it is: point the project at a copy of the production database and run ./fegg-cli migration, which only adds the new core tables (such as rate_limit).

searchDocs.title: 4. Rewrite the PHP​
searchDocs.content: Write each controller again as a namespaced class in htdocs/_fegg/site/controller/, replace the Fegg 4 classes with their Fegg 5 names, and add $this->requirePost() to every CMS action that changes data. Then go through the behaviour changes: Fegg 5 fails loudly where Fegg 4 was silent.  📄️Rewriting the PHP Write each controller again as a namespaced class in htdocs/_fegg/site/controller/ (cms/ becomes Cms/). The skeleton's Cms/News.php and Cms/Lab.php are the models for post types. 📄️Behaviour changes Fegg 5 fails loudly where Fegg 4 was silent. The full list is in the 5.0.0 section of htdocs/_fegg/core/UPGRADE.md. The ones most likely to affect code brought over:

searchDocs.title: 5. Check​
searchDocs.content: ./fegg-cli template:lint prints OK php -l reports no syntax errors for the PHP files under htdocs/_fegg (excluding vendor/ and data/) ./fegg-cli migration against a copy of the production database only adds new core tables such as rate_limit (no project table definition is missing, and every YAML file is read: an error names the file and the line) ./fegg-cli core:status prints No changes to core files. The browser console of every CMS screen shows no errors ($ is not defined means a template still uses jQuery), and dates (with the time), rich text and gallery ordering are saved Public pages, the contact form (through to sending), CMS login, create / edit / delete for each post type, and media and image uploads work, with the data and uploads of the old site Every post type appears in the CMS side menu and on the dashboard Every saving action in site/controller/Cms/ calls $this->requirePost(): opening its URL in the browser (a GET, e.g. /cms/news/update/) answers 405 No page links to an action named like a method of Fegg\Application (mail, in, redirect ...) or defined only in a base controller (both are 404 now) The PHP error log has no warnings After deploying, ./fegg-cli doctor https://<production URL> prints OK (/_fegg/assets/js/base.js is served; the rest of /_fegg/, the sites' SCSS sources included, is not) and the CMS dashboard shows no protection warnings  To roll back, redeploy the old branch. The table definitions are compatible, so the same database works with both.

searchDocs.title: migration​
searchDocs.content: ./fegg-cli migration   Compares the table definitions in the YAML files with the database (SQLite, or MySQL / MariaDB) and applies the difference (adds tables, columns and indexes).  The core's files (core/config/database/: cms_user, cms_file, cms_image, rate_limit) are read first, then the project's (site/config/database/). A project file with the same name replaces the core's file. With the CMS turned off ($settings['cms'] = false, see Settings) cms_user, cms_file and cms_image are neither created nor dropped, and no first CMS user is created.Starts with one line naming the environment, its file and the database, e.g. Environment: staging (site/config/env/staging.php, /var/www/vhosts/*/p[0-9]*) / DB: sqlite:... (see Environments and secrets).Prints Fegg-cli migration diff : Not changed when the database already matches, Fegg-cli migration diff : Finished migration after applying changes.Then creates the first CMS user when FEGG_CMS_INITIAL_LOGIN is set and cms_user has no users at all, with FEGG_CMS_INITIAL_PASSWORD_HASH (or FEGG_CMS_INITIAL_PASSWORD) and FEGG_CMS_INITIAL_NAME. An existing user is never changed and a deleted one is not created again, so this is safe on every deploy. Without a usable password it exits with 1 after the migration.fegg-cli core:update runs it automatically after updating the core.On MySQL the YAML types are mapped to MySQL types and changed tables are altered in place. See Database configuration./cms/migrate/ in the CMS shows the same pending changes and applies them with its "Run migration" button (POST), for servers where you cannot run fegg-cli.  danger The YAML files are the single source of truth. A table that exists in the database but in no YAML file is dropped, and a column that is not in the YAML is removed with its data. Run it against a copy first when you are not sure that every table is defined.  To create a YAML file from an existing database:  ./fegg-cli migration:db2schema htdocs/_fegg/site/config/database/dump.yaml   All tables are written to the one file. Split it into one file per table if you keep it.

searchDocs.title: db:schema​
searchDocs.content: ./fegg-cli db:schema # every table ./fegg-cli db:schema cms_news # one table ./fegg-cli db:schema --json # as JSON   Lists the tables, columns (type, primary key, autoincrement, not null, default) and indexes defined in core/config/database/ and site/config/database/. It reads the YAML files, not the database, so it works without a database. It also warns when a table is missing one of the columns every table needs (valid, created, modified).  Output cms_news (htdocs/_fegg/site/config/database/cms_news.yaml) news_id INTEGER primary key, autoincrement, not null visible BOOLEAN category INTEGER title TEXT ... valid BOOLEAN post_date DATETIME created DATETIME modified DATETIME index NEWS_ID unique (news_id)

searchDocs.title: template:lint​
searchDocs.content: ./fegg-cli template:lint # every template in site/template and core/template ./fegg-cli template:lint htdocs/_fegg/site/template/main/tpl/news/detail.tpl   Checks templates without running them and reports each problem with the .tpl file and line: unknown tags, unclosed blocks or extra {{ end }}, missing include / transclude targets, undefined modifiers, and output in URL attributes, <script> or event attributes that is not escaped for that context.  Output (example) htdocs/_fegg/site/template/main/tpl/news/detail.tpl:12: unknown modifier "nosuch" (define it in site/functions/*.php) htdocs/_fegg/site/template/main/tpl/news/detail.tpl:20: {{ $page.data.url }} starts a URL: write {{ $value|feggUrl }} so javascript: URLs are refused NG: 2 problem(s) in 1 template(s)   Prints OK: <n> template(s) when there is nothing to fix. Run it after every template change.

searchDocs.title: site:create / site:list​
searchDocs.content: ./fegg-cli site:create recruit /recruit/ # NAME PATH ./fegg-cli site:list   site:create copies the starting folder core/dist/site/ (tpl/ with index.tpl, not_found.tpl and template/siteframe.tpl, a FLOCSS scss/, js/, img/ and the .htaccess) to site/template/recruit/, and adds $sites['recruit'] = array('path' => '/recruit/'); to site/config/sites.php and $route['recruit/'] = 'page/render/index'; to site/config/route.php. It refuses a name or a path that is already used. site:list prints each site's name, path and folder. See Sites.

searchDocs.title: CMS users​
searchDocs.content: ./fegg-cli user:create admin "Site administrator" # LOGIN [NAME]; NAME defaults to LOGIN ./fegg-cli user:password admin # set a new password ./fegg-cli user:list # user_id, login and name of every CMS user   Manage the CMS users (table cms_user). Passwords are asked twice without echo (never as an argument, which would stay in the shell history), must not be empty (there is no length rule), and are stored with password_hash(). From a script, or where there is no terminal, use --password-stdin:  printf '%s\n' "$CMS_PASSWORD" | ./fegg-cli user:create admin --password-stdin   user:create refuses a login that already exists; use user:password for it. With the CMS turned off, every user:* command refuses to run.  user:hash prints password_hash() of a password (asked without echo, or --password-stdin) for FEGG_CMS_INITIAL_PASSWORD_HASH in a committed environment file.  note /cms/register/ needs a CMS login and developer mode; on a production server use fegg-cli.

searchDocs.title: core:status / core:update​
searchDocs.content: core:status / core:update [vX.Y.Z] [--dry-run] [--force]: see Updating the core.  core:manifest also exists, but it is for skeleton maintainers only (it rebuilds core/manifest.json).

searchDocs.title: doctor​
searchDocs.content: ./fegg-cli doctor # check the .htaccess files on disk ./fegg-cli doctor https://example.com # also request the live site   Without a URL, it checks the files on disk:  htdocs/_fegg/.htaccess denies access,htdocs/.htaccess has the rule for _fegg/ and lets through the files of _fegg/assets/, of the site folders' css/ js/ img/ font/ and of _fegg/site/up_dir/,_fegg/assets/, each site folder (site/template/<site>/) and the upload directory site/up_dir/ have their .htaccess, which serve only their file types (see Upload).  With a URL, it also requests files under _fegg/ (a site's SCSS sources and the upload directory's .htaccess included) and the SQLite database (when it is under the document root) on the live site and reports any that can be read, and checks that /_fegg/assets/js/base.js is served.  Prints OK: https://example.com does not expose _fegg/, or NG with the list of problems (exit code 1). You can run it from your local machine against the production URL, which is the easiest check after an FTP upload.  It also prints Warning: lines, without failing, for outdated rules in htdocs/.htaccess: a <IfModule mod_php5.c> block (ignored by PHP 7 and 8), and Apache 2.2 Order / Deny from lines (an HTTP 500 on Apache 2.4 without mod_access_compat; use Require all denied). Compare the file with core/dist/htaccess.dist.

searchDocs.title: Developer commands in the skeleton​
searchDocs.content: The skeleton repository also has Composer scripts for the test suite and code checks. Composer is only used for development; the application never loads vendor/.  Command	What it doescomposer test	PHPUnit: unit and HTTP integration tests (PHP 7.4 to 8.5). test:unit and test:integration run one suite composer test:mysql	The MySQL tests, against the server given in FEGG_TEST_MYSQL_DSN, FEGG_TEST_MYSQL_USER and FEGG_TEST_MYSQL_PASSWORD (skipped without them) composer analyse	PHPStan (level 5, with a baseline) composer cs:check	PSR-12 check of core/src and the tests (composer cs:fix applies the fixes)  The integration tests run with FEGG_ENV=development and a throwaway SQLite database, so they never touch site/data/db/db.db.  The skeleton also builds the core's CMS files. Projects do not run these: the files come built with core:update.  Command	What it doesnpm run build:cms	The core's CMS CSS, the editor (assets/editor/) and the icons it uses, into htdocs/_fegg/assets/ (committed) npm run typecheck	TypeScript check of the editor's source npm run cms:vendor	Copy the CMS's libraries (SortableJS ...) from node_modules to htdocs/_fegg/assets/vendor/

searchDocs.title: Basic settings​
searchDocs.content: The defaults are in htdocs/_fegg/core/config/settings.php. Do not edit that file (it is replaced on update). Put the values for your project in htdocs/_fegg/site/config/settings.php.  The core file is loaded first, then the site file. Only the keys the site file sets are changed, so write one key per line and never reassign the whole array ($settings = array(...) would drop the defaults).  htdocs/_fegg/site/config/settings.php <?php defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; // Run mode 1: running, empty: under maintenance $settings['run_mode'] = '1'; // Maintenance page URL $settings['maintenance_page_url'] = ''; // Developer IP addresses (multiple allowed). Error details only outside production (FEGG_ENV) $settings['developer_ip'] = array('192.168.65.1', '203.0.113.10'); // Basic authentication scope (0: none, 1: whole site, 2: partial) #$settings['basic_auth_scope'] = 0; #$settings['basic_auth_user'] = ''; #$settings['basic_auth_password'] = ''; // HSTS, once the whole site is served over HTTPS #$settings['hsts'] = 'max-age=31536000';   Key	Default	Remarkscms	true	false for a site without the CMS (see A site without the CMS) run_mode	'1'	'1': running. Empty: under maintenance. During maintenance every request that does not come from developer_ip is redirected to maintenance_page_url, or gets a short maintenance message when it is empty. maintenance_page_url	''	Redirect target during maintenance developer_ip	array()	Addresses that can see error details outside production (see Developer mode) and that bypass maintenance timezone	''	Time zone of the application, set once at startup. '': FEGG_DEFAULT_TIMEZONE (Asia/Tokyo) log_level	''	Lowest level written to the application log (debug, info, notice, warning, error ...). '': warning in production, debug elsewhere. See Log log_retention_days	30	Days to keep the application log files (0: keep all) mail	array('transport' => 'sendmail', 'from' => '', 'from_name' => '')	Outgoing mail of Fegg\Tool\Mail, and the sender when send() is given none (see Sender). For SMTP see Mail security_headers	array()	Changes the default security headers: 'Header-Name' => 'value', '' removes one. See Security hsts	''	Strict-Transport-Security value sent on HTTPS responses, e.g. 'max-age=31536000'. '': not sent csp	''	Content-Security-Policy value. '': not sent csp_report_only	false	true: send the policy as Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only (reports only, blocks nothing) default_language	not set	Language code used when none is detected, e.g. 'ja'. Only for multilingual sites support_language	not set	Supported language codes, e.g. array('ja', 'en'). Only for multilingual sites basic_auth_scope	0	0: no Basic authentication. 1: every request handled by Fegg, checked before the controller runs. 2: only where the controller calls $this->basicAuth() basic_auth_user	''	Basic authentication user basic_auth_password	''	Basic authentication password (compared with hash_equals()) basic_auth_message	not set	Realm shown in the browser's login dialog basic_auth_error_message	not set	Text sent with the 401 response when the login fails (default Authorization Required) template_dir	site/template, core/template	Template directories, searched in this order. The tpl/ of the site the URL belongs to is put first (see Sites) template_ext	'tpl'	Template file extension template_cache_dir	site/data/cache/template	Compiled template cache global_config_dir	''	Optional directory searched by loadConfig() before site/config/. End it with /  Read a setting from a controller with $this->getSetting().

searchDocs.title: A site without the CMS​
searchDocs.content: htdocs/_fegg/site/config/settings.php $settings['cms'] = false;   With the CMS turned off (Fegg\Cms\Setting):  /cms/... (the core's and the project's CMS screens) and the uploads' controller (image sizes and /file/<id>/ under /_fegg/site/up_dir/) answer 404,fegg-cli migration neither creates nor drops cms_user, cms_file and cms_image (their rows are kept) and creates no first CMS user; fegg-cli db:schema leaves them out,fegg-cli user:* refuses to run.  Remove what the project itself has for the CMS: site/config/database/cms_news.yaml and the other post types (migration then drops those tables), site/controller/Cms/, site/template/cms/, the news pages if they show CMS posts, and site/config/cms_menu.php.

searchDocs.title: Database​
searchDocs.content: The connection is set in htdocs/_fegg/site/config/database_config.php, which reads FEGG_DB_DSN, FEGG_DB_USER, FEGG_DB_PASSWORD, FEGG_DB_SLAVE_DSN and FEGG_DB_PATH with feggEnv(), so the file is the same on every server. Without settings it is the SQLite file htdocs/_fegg/site/data/db/db.db; if the server allows it, move it outside the document root with FEGG_DB_PATH. For MySQL / MariaDB and master / slave, see Database configuration.  Tables are defined in YAML files (core/config/database/ for the CMS tables, site/config/database/ for the project's tables) and created or changed with ./fegg-cli migration (see fegg-cli). Every table needs the columns valid, created and modified. The files are read by Fegg\Tool\Yaml, which says what it reads.

searchDocs.title: Other files in site/config/​
searchDocs.content: File	Remarksroute.php	URL routing (see URL) sites.php	The project's sites, one line each (see Sites) site_info.php	Site title, description, OGP image, picture breakpoints, ... Loaded by the base controller and available in templates as $site. A site's 'info' in sites.php overrides it for that site category_info.php	Labels for categories and the CMS visibility states. Loaded by the base controller into $this->config['category_info'] cms_menu.php	CMS side menu. Add one block per post type env.php	Per-server settings and secrets, read with feggEnv(). Not committed; copy env.php.dist (see Environments and secrets) database_config.php	Database connection, from feggEnv() (see Database) upload_dir.php	Path and URL of the CMS upload directory (htdocs/_fegg/site/up_dir, /_fegg/site/up_dir), and the limits of images in other sizes (image_max, image_cache_max, see Trim) database/*.yaml	Table definitions for fegg-cli migration define.php	Optional. Project constants, loaded right after the core starts (web and CLI) fegg_update.php	Optional. Repository used by fegg-cli core:update (see Updating the core)  Any other file in site/config/ can be loaded with $this->loadConfig(). A file with the same name as one in core/config/ (for example validation_error_message.php) replaces the core's file.

searchDocs.title: Test servers deployed with git pull​
searchDocs.content: On the LionHeart develop server (http://p83.<project>.develop.lionheart.co.jp/, project directory /var/www/vhosts/<project>/p83) a deploy is git pull followed by fegg-cli migration. Nothing can be placed on the server by hand, so the test server's settings are committed:  htdocs/_fegg/site/config/env/paths.php return array( // project root pattern (fnmatch; * and ? do not cross /) => environment file name '/var/www/vhosts/*/p[0-9]*' => 'staging', );   htdocs/_fegg/site/config/env/staging.php return array( 'FEGG_ENV' => 'staging', // first CMS user, created by fegg-cli migration (see below) 'FEGG_CMS_INITIAL_LOGIN' => 'admin', 'FEGG_CMS_INITIAL_PASSWORD_HASH' => '$2y$10$...', // ./fegg-cli user:hash // Turnstile test keys (no host name registration needed): always pass (2x00000000000000000000AB / 2x0000000000000000000000000000000AA always fail) 'FEGG_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY' => '1x00000000000000000000AA', 'FEGG_TURNSTILE_SECRET' => '1x0000000000000000000000000000000AA', );   Both files come with the skeleton. The project root (the directory of fegg-cli) is matched against paths.php; the first match chooses site/config/env/<name>.php. Other paths (production, your machine) are unaffected.  Why the path: the host name of a request is chosen by the client. Matching it would let a request to production with Host: x.develop.lionheart.co.jp switch production to the test settings (test captcha keys that always pass, the test administrator). The path is set by the server, and fegg-cli sees the same path as the web.Check it: the first line of fegg-cli migration in the deploy log names the environment and its file (see fegg-cli).First CMS user: fegg-cli migration creates it once, while cms_user is empty (see fegg-cli). Commit the hash (./fegg-cli user:hash), not the password, and change the password after the first login.  warning Everyone who can read the repository can read these files. Put only values made for the test server there, never production keys or passwords. env.php on a server and environment variables still win over them.

searchDocs.title: Developer mode​
searchDocs.content: Fegg runs in developer mode (the constant FEGG_DEVELOPER is '1') only when both are true:  the request comes from an address in developer_ip, andFEGG_ENV is not production.  In developer mode:  PHP errors are displayed.An uncaught exception shows the message, the file and line, the template line (Template: <file>.tpl:<line>), the stack trace and $this->page. Other visitors get the error page (see Logging and errors). In both cases the error is written to the PHP error log and the application log.The 404 page shows which controller file Fegg tried to load.  developer_ip alone is not a security boundary: behind a proxy or load balancer every request may come from the same address.

searchDocs.title: Database and models​
searchDocs.content: Database errors throw Fegg\Database\QueryException (the message includes the SQL and its parameters) instead of printing and calling exit. Uncaught, it is a logged HTTP 500.updateWhere(), deleteWhere() and eraseWhere() with an empty condition throw instead of affecting every row. Pass '1 = 1' where every row was really meant.Model::order(), join() and the table / id / visible options accept only plain names. Move expressions to orderRaw().OR in conditions is bracketed: where('category = ?', 1)->where('a = ? OR b = ?', ...) is category = 1 AND (a = ? OR b = ?), and the visible flag and valid = 1 are added outside the brackets. In Fegg 4 such conditions matched rows of every category, and where('a = ?', 1)->where('b = ?', 2, 'OR') also returned unpublished and deleted rows matching b; such lists can get shorter.

searchDocs.title: Templates​
searchDocs.content: Missing templates, include targets and transclude parents throw Fegg\Template\TemplateException (HTTP 500) instead of printing "Can't Read" into the page. ./fegg-cli template:lint lists them all.Template blocks are checked: an unclosed block or an extra {{ end }} throws with the line number.Sections are passed to the parent template as closures. Code that called the global section_<name>() functions directly must be rewritten.{{ options }} escapes labels and values, and {{ hidden }} escapes values.Arrays reach modifiers: {{ $tags|feggImplode:', ' }} now prints the joined tags (it printed nothing).

searchDocs.title: Requests, sessions and security​
searchDocs.content: Actions: only a controller's own public methods can be called from a URL (see Controller). An action defined in MyApplication or a base controller is a 404: write it in each controller that uses it. An action named like a method of Fegg\Application (mail, in, redirect ...) is a 404: rename it, or map the old URL with a route.Basic authentication with basic_auth_scope = 1 is checked before the controller's __init() and action, so redirects, downloads and direct output are protected too.No more exit: Fegg ends responses by throwing Fegg\Http\Halt; rethrow it from a catch (\Throwable $e) and replace your own exit with $this->halt() (see Ending a response).Sessions and cookies: a session starts only when something is written to it (see Session). setCookie() takes SameSite as its own argument (not '/; SameSite=Lax' in the path), and unsetCookie() really deletes the cookie (Fegg 4 set an empty cookie for 7 days; see setCookie).Security headers are sent with every response; a page framed by another site calls $this->allowFraming() (see Security).HTTPS is detected from more server variables and proxy headers, and redirect() no longer sends HTTPS pages to HTTP when the detection fails (see Security).Route-only controllers: controllers that implement Fegg\Http\RouteOnly (such as the skeleton's Site\Controller\Page) are only reached through site/config/route.php. Add a route such as $route['about/'] = 'page/render/about'; for each static page that was reached as /page/render/... (see URL).htdocs/.htaccess: remove the <IfModule mod_php5.c> block and the Apache 2.2 Order / Deny from all lines (500 on Apache 2.4), and add the dotfile rules and the _fegg exceptions (the CMS's files, the site folders, the uploads) of core/dist/htaccess.dist. On nginx, use the rules of Directory structure. fegg-cli doctor warns about the old lines.Captcha keys and the database DSN move to env.php: the skeleton's database_config.php and contact/contact_config.php read them with feggEnv(). Put the project's keys there, not in committed files.

searchDocs.title: CMS​
searchDocs.content: CMS sessions need the session's user to still exist in cms_user: deleting a user ends their sessions.CMS login: logout is a POST. Copied CMS frame templates in site/template/cms/tpl/ add the class js-cms-logout to the logout link. Run fegg-cli migration for the login throttling table rate_limit. /cms/login/create/... is gone: use fegg-cli user:create (see fegg-cli).The CMS's files are in htdocs/_fegg/assets/, read at /_fegg/assets/. Copies of CMS templates in site/template/cms/tpl/ load them with {{ $site.cms_assets }} instead of {{ $site.cms_dir }} (css/, js/, img/, vendor/). _fegg/ can no longer be outside the document root. See CMS screens and the editor.No jQuery in the CMS (nor jQuery UI, Select2 or the datetimepicker). Rewrite $(...) in the project's CMS templates (site/template/cms/tpl/*/html_head.tpl) with plain JavaScript and the FeggCms helpers, or load a jQuery of your own there. Date fields become datetime-local inputs and drag & drop ordering uses SortableJS (see Dates and Drag and drop ordering).CKEditor 4 is removed. Rich text fields use FeggEditor: replace CKEDITOR.replace(...) and ckeditor/ckeditor.js with data-fegg-editor="full" on the textarea and js/editor.js, and clean the saved HTML with Fegg\Cms\HtmlSanitizer::clean(). Text written with CKEditor opens in FeggEditor. Copied cms/image/ and cms/media/ templates use the new picker scripts (js/modal/image_picker.js, file_picker.js; parameters from=wysiwyg&picker=<id>).Font Awesome 4.3 is removed. Icons are Tabler Icons: replace fa fa-… with ti ti-…: search → search, angle-right → chevron-right, image / picture-o → photo, times → x, cog → settings (pencil, trash, plus, link, check, download, upload keep their names; others: tabler.io/icons). An icon the core does not use needs a line in unique.scss (see Icons). Copies of cms/frame/sitewire.tpl and popframe.tpl load vendor/tabler-icons/icons.css instead of fonts/font-awesome.min.css.

searchDocs.title: Libraries​
searchDocs.content: Uploads check the content against the extension; add the @content message to a copied site/config/file_error_message.php (see Upload).Spyc is removed. YAML is read by Fegg\Tool\Yaml (see Yaml): replace spyc_load_file() / Spyc::YAMLLoad() in project code with Fegg\Tool\Yaml::parseFile(). Table definitions read as before; yes / no and numbers with a leading zero are now text, and anchors or tags are refused with the file and the line.getDatetime() / convertDatetime() no longer change the process-wide time zone, and convertDatetime() returns '' for a date it cannot read (it returned 1970-01-01 ...).Images in other sizes (getImageUrl) are limited by image_max and image_cache_max in site/config/upload_dir.php, and the positions lb and rb now keep the bottom left and the bottom right (see Trim).Fegg\Tool\Trim throws a \RuntimeException for a missing file, a file that is not a JPEG, PNG or GIF, or another output type (it called exit).Fegg\Tool\File methods return true / false. removeDirectory() removes symbolic links, never what they point to.Fegg\Tool\Upload::upload() for a field the form does not have is @empty (or OK when not required), and several files (name="file[]") are @failed, without PHP warnings.Fegg\Tool\Mail: the debug log is mail.log in the log directory (it was /tmp/sendmaillog). send() without a sender uses $settings['mail']['from'] / ['from_name'], or throws an \InvalidArgumentException.Fegg\Tool\RSS throws a \RuntimeException for a feed it cannot fetch or read, and keeps posts whose title contains "PR:": pass array('skip_pr' => true) to leave them out as before.

searchDocs.title: Additional work for v3 projects​
searchDocs.content: Mail (Fegg\Tool\Mail) uses PHPMailer. sendWithFile(), setInputCharset() and setSendCharset() were removed: add attachments with pushAttached() and call send(). A failed send throws PHPMailer\PHPMailer\Exception.Trailing slash: URLs without an extension are redirected (301) to the same URL with a trailing /. Check the keys in route.php and the links in templates.PHP 8: fix deprecation warnings in the project code (for example passing null to string functions).

searchDocs.title: Rewriting the PHP
searchDocs.content: Rewriting the PHP Write each controller again as a namespaced class in htdocs/_fegg/site/controller/ (cms/ becomes Cms/). The skeleton's Cms/News.php and Cms/Lab.php are the models for post types. Fegg 4: code/application/cms/News.php <?php class News extends MyApplication { public function __init() { parent::__init(); $this->_lh = $this->getClass('LH_FW', 'news'); $this->_model = new Model(true, array('table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id')); } } Fegg 5: htdocs/_fegg/site/controller/Cms/News.php <?php namespace Site\Controller\Cms; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; use Fegg\Model; class News extends Controller // Site\Controller\Cms\Controller: the CMS base { protected $_cmsSection = 'news'; // replaces new Helper('news') and the isAuth() check public function __init() { parent::__init(); $this->_model = new Model(true, array('table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id')); } public function update() { $this->requirePost(); // required: every action that changes data // ... } public function delete($id) { $this->requirePost(); // deletes are POST forms with the CSRF token // ... } } CMS screens extend Site\Controller\Cms\Controller, public pages Site\Controller\Controller. The CMS base checks the login and the CSRF token of every POST. Edit and delete forms in the project's CMS templates use method="post": delete links in list templates become POST forms (see Controller). Processing that was added to MyApplication goes into __init() or a protected method of site/controller/Controller.php. Required: requirePost() in every action that changes data Fegg 4 had no such check. Add $this->requirePost() as the first line of every action that saves, deletes, sorts or otherwise writes (update, create, delete ...). The CSRF token is only checked on POST: an action without requirePost() still runs on a GET, so a link or an image on another site can change data while a CMS user is logged in. With it, a GET answers 405. Check every action with grep -n "public function" htdocs/_fegg/site/controller/Cms/*.php. v3 / v4	Fegg 5MyApplication	Site\Controller\Controller (public pages), Site\Controller\Cms\Controller (CMS screens) Model, ModelWhere, ModelOrder, ...	Fegg\Model, Fegg\Model\Where, Fegg\Model\Order, ... DB_pdo	Fegg\Database\Pdo $this->getClass('LH_FW', 'news')	new \Fegg\Cms\Helper('news') (CMS screens get it as $this->_lh) $this->getClass('Validation')	new \Fegg\Tool\Validation() $this->getClass('Tool/Upload'), Tool/File, Tool/Mail, Tool/RSS, Tool/Trim	new \Fegg\Tool\Upload() etc. ReCAPTCHA, Turnstile	Fegg\Tool\Captcha\ReCAPTCHA, Fegg\Tool\Captcha\Turnstile Tool/Date	Removed: PHP's DateTimeImmutable (see below) Tool/OEmbed, core/config/oembed_schemes.php	Removed: Fegg\Tool\Embed (see below) $this->getClass('MyLib/Foo') (code/lib/)	new \Site\MyLib\Foo() in site/src/MyLib/Foo.php code/lib/Modifire.php	htdocs/_fegg/site/functions/modifier.php FEGG_CODE_DIR . '/config/...', '/data/...'	FEGG_SITE_DIR . '/config/...', '/data/...' FEGG_DIR . '/...'	Not needed (autoloaded) FEGG_TEST_ENVIRONMENT	FEGG_ENV !== 'production' Every file starts with namespace, defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; and use. Inside a namespace, prefix PHP's own classes with \ (new \Exception, new \DateTime, \PDO::PARAM_INT). Tool/Date: addDay($d, 3) is (new \DateTimeImmutable($d))->modify('+3 day')->format('Y-m-d H:i:s'), addMinute($d, 30) is ->modify('+30 minute'), getDiff() is ->diff(), getTheLastday() is ->format('t'), and a format in a template is feggDate (see Dates and time zone). A project that needs addMonth() (kept at the end of the month) or getSocialTime() copies the Fegg 4 class into site/src/.Tool/OEmbed: (new OEmbed($url))->media (asked of YouTube) becomes Fegg\Tool\Embed::youtubeUrl($url) (a youtube-nocookie.com URL, no request), and an <iframe> written in a template becomes {{ $page.data.youtube_url|feggYoutube|noescape }} / |feggMap|noescape, which write the whole block (see Embed). Other oEmbed services: ask them with Fegg\Http\Client in the project. grep -rn "getClass\|MyApplication\|FEGG_DIR\|FEGG_CODE_DIR\|FEGG_TEST_ENVIRONMENT" htdocs/_fegg/site must find nothing.

searchDocs.title: Routine updates​
searchDocs.content: ./fegg-cli core:status # current version, and whether core files were changed ./fegg-cli core:update --dry-run # show the difference to the latest release (changes nothing) ./fegg-cli core:update # update to the latest tag (vX.Y.Z) ./fegg-cli core:update v5.1.0 # update to a given version npm run build:scss # the project's CSS, if its SCSS changed (the CMS's comes built)   core:update option	RemarksvX.Y.Z	Version to install. The latest tag when omitted --dry-run	Show what would change without changing anything --force	Overwrite core files that were changed in the project  core:status prints the core version and compares the core files with core/manifest.json. No changes to core files. means the core is untouched and can be updated; otherwise it lists the changed files.The release is fetched with git. If you can clone from GitHub over SSH (git clone git@github.com:... works for you), no token is needed.Only core files are replaced: htdocs/_fegg/core/, htdocs/_fegg/assets/ (the CMS's CSS, JS, images and icons, already built) and htdocs/_fegg/.htaccess. There is nothing to build after an update. site/ (with the sites' templates and assets and the uploads), htdocs/index.php, htdocs/.htaccess and fegg-cli are not changed.If core files were edited in the project, the command lists them and stops. Move those changes to overrides in site/ (see Directory structure) and run it again. Add --force only if you really want to overwrite them.The replaced files are kept in htdocs/_fegg/site/data/core-backup/<old version>-<timestamp>/.After the update, the template cache is cleared and fegg-cli migration runs automatically.Finally, the core/UPGRADE.md sections for every version crossed are printed. They list what you have to change by hand (entry files, .htaccess, deprecated APIs). Read them.  Run the tests and check the site, then commit. git status should show only core files.

searchDocs.title: Changing the source repository​
searchDocs.content: By default the release is fetched from git@github.com:lionheart-group/lh-fegg-skelton.git. To use another repository (a fork, or HTTPS), set it in the project:  htdocs/_fegg/site/config/fegg_update.php <?php defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; $fegg_update['repository'] = 'https://github.com/lionheart-group/lh-fegg-skelton.git';   The environment variable FEGG_UPDATE_REPO takes precedence over this file.

searchDocs.title: When the server has no SSH (FTP-only hosting)​
searchDocs.content: Run ./fegg-cli core:update in your local working copy, then run the tests and check that everything works.Commit the changed files.Upload htdocs/_fegg/core/ and htdocs/_fegg/assets/ over FTP. Upload htdocs/_fegg/.htaccess only if it changed.fegg-cli migration cannot run on the server. For versions that change tables, either upload a database file built locally or open /cms/migrate/ in the CMS.Check the live site with ./fegg-cli doctor https://example.com.

searchDocs.title: Merging upstream with git​
searchDocs.content: You can also update by adding the skeleton repository as upstream and merging a release tag:  git remote add upstream git@github.com:lionheart-group/lh-fegg-skelton.git git fetch upstream --tags git merge v5.1.0   If the project only edited site/, there are no conflicts in the core. The skeleton's sample files in site/ (sample controllers and templates) may also have changed; in that case keep the project's version.

searchDocs.title: Versions​
searchDocs.content: Version	MeaningPatch (5.0.x)	Fixes inside the core. core:update alone is enough Minor (5.x.0)	New features. Optional work for projects is described in UPGRADE.md Major (x.0.0)	Changes that require fixes to project code  The full text, including the release procedure for skeleton maintainers, is in docs/updating.md of the skeleton repository.

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public static int Cache::clear()   Removes every cache file of the directory and returns how many were removed. fegg-cli cache:clear calls it.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: use Fegg\Tool\Cache; $count = Cache::clear();   The same from the command line ./fegg-cli cache:clear # OK: 3 value(s) removed from /path/to/htdocs/_fegg/site/data/cache/data

searchDocs.title: How to use​
searchDocs.content: The methods are static: import Fegg\Tool\Cache and call remember() with a key, the seconds to keep the value and a function that returns it.  Controller <?php namespace Site\Controller; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; use Fegg\Tool\Cache; use Fegg\Tool\RSS; class Index extends Controller { public function index() { try { // Fetched at most once every 10 minutes $this->page['posts'] = Cache::remember('blog-feed', 600, function () { return (new RSS('https://blog.example.com/feed'))->fetchAll(5); }); } catch (\RuntimeException $e) { $this->page['posts'] = array(); } $this->displayPage('index'); } }   Put everything the value depends on in the key: 'items-' . $category. Keys are any text; the file name is made from a hash of the key.

searchDocs.title: When the function fails​
searchDocs.content: When the value has expired and the function throws, remember() returns the expired value if it is still there and writes a warning with the key and the exception to the log (Cache: expired value of blog-feed used, the new one failed: ...). The page keeps working while the other service is down. Without an expired value, the exception is thrown.  The value is kept again only when the function succeeds, so the next request tries again. Fegg\Http\Halt (a redirect inside the function) is never caught.

searchDocs.title: Values​
searchDocs.content: A value can contain:  arrays, strings, numbers, booleans and null;dates: \DateTime and \DateTimeImmutable (the posts of RSS have them).  Any other object throws \InvalidArgumentException, also inside an array: a cache file can then never create an object when it is read. Keep model rows (arrays) or convert objects to arrays first.

searchDocs.title: Files​
searchDocs.content: Setting	Default	Remarks$settings['cache_dir']	site/data/cache/data	Directory of the files (created when missing)  A file is written to a temporary name and then renamed, so a request never reads a half-written file.An expired file stays until it is written again or removed with fegg-cli cache:clear; it is treated as missing (except by the fallback above).A file that cannot be read is treated as missing.When the directory or the file cannot be written, a warning goes to the log and the value is not kept: remember() still returns it.site/data/ is not tracked by git.

searchDocs.title: Clearing​
searchDocs.content: fegg-cli cache:clear removes every value, for example after a deploy that changes what a value contains:  ./fegg-cli cache:clear # OK: 3 value(s) removed from /path/to/htdocs/_fegg/site/data/cache/data   Cache::delete() removes one key, for example when the CMS saves the data the value was made from.

searchDocs.title: Errors​
searchDocs.content: A ttl below 1 second, or a value with an object other than a date, throws \InvalidArgumentException.What the function of remember() throws is thrown again when there is no expired value (see When the function fails).A directory or file that cannot be written does not throw (see Files).

searchDocs.title: Methods​
searchDocs.content: 📄️Cache::remember Return the kept value, or make it and keep it 📄️Cache::get Read a kept value 📄️Cache::has Check for a kept value 📄️Cache::set Keep a value 📄️Cache::delete Remove one value 📄️Cache::clear Remove every value 📄️Cache::directory / Cache::setDirectory The directory of the files, and replacing it in tests

searchDocs.title: How to use​
searchDocs.content: Every library is a namespaced class that is loaded by the autoloader. Import it with use and create it with new.  Controller <?php namespace Site\Controller; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; use Fegg\Tool\Mail; use Fegg\Tool\Validation; class Contact extends Controller { public function post() { $validation = new Validation(); $validation->required('mail', $this->in('mail'), array('@required', 'Email')); if (!$validation->isError()) { $mail = new Mail('Mail subject', 'Mail body'); $mail->send($this->in('mail'), 'Sender name', 'from@example.com'); } } }

searchDocs.title: Extension Libraries​
searchDocs.content: The libraries are in the Fegg\Tool\ namespace. Fegg\Model, Fegg\Database\Pdo, Fegg\Http\Client and Fegg\Log are framework classes, not in Fegg\Tool\.
