Library	Class	DescriptionValidation	Fegg\Tool\Validation	Form validation Database	Fegg\Database\Pdo	Database access (PDO) Model	Fegg\Model	Models: queries and rows File	Fegg\Tool\File	File and directory operations Upload	Fegg\Tool\Upload	Uploads and file checks Mail	Fegg\Tool\Mail	Sending mail (PHPMailer) RSS	Fegg\Tool\RSS	Reading RSS / Atom feeds Trim	Fegg\Tool\Trim	Resizing and cropping images Embed	Fegg\Tool\Embed	Embedding YouTube videos and Google Maps the way the editor does Captcha	Fegg\Tool\Captcha\ReCAPTCHA, Fegg\Tool\Captcha\Turnstile	Verifying Google reCAPTCHA / Cloudflare Turnstile responses Yaml	Fegg\Tool\Yaml	Reading and writing YAML files HTTP client	Fegg\Http\Client	Requests to other services over HTTP Log	Fegg\Log	Writing to the application log Cache	Fegg\Tool\Cache	Keeping values in files for a while CSV	Fegg\Tool\Csv	Writing and reading CSV for Excel Rate limit	Fegg\Tool\RateLimit	Limiting how often one visitor can do something Sitemap	Fegg\Tool\Sitemap	Writing sitemap.xml JSON-LD	Fegg\Tool\JsonLd	Structured data for search engines Feed	Fegg\Tool\Feed	Writing an RSS 2.0 feed of the site's posts

searchDocs.title: Project libraries​
searchDocs.content: Put your own classes in htdocs/_fegg/site/src/ with the Site\ namespace. They are autoloaded in the same way.  htdocs/_fegg/site/src/MyLib/Foo.php <?php namespace Site\MyLib; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; class Foo { }   Controller use Site\MyLib\Foo; $foo = new Foo();

searchDocs.title: External Libraries​
searchDocs.content: These libraries are bundled in htdocs/_fegg/core/vendor/ and autoloaded.  PHPMailer (7.2) Used by Mail. Namespace PHPMailer\PHPMailerA failed send throws PHPMailer\PHPMailer\Exception  JSON documents are handled with PHP's own json_encode and json_decode, YAML with Yaml.

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public static string Cache::directory() public static void Cache::setDirectory( ?string $directory )   directory() returns the directory of the cache files: $settings['cache_dir'], or site/data/cache/data when the setting is empty.  setDirectory() uses another directory for the rest of the request, for tests. null reads the setting again.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$directory	string|null Directory (a trailing / is removed), or null for the setting

searchDocs.title: Example​

When $callback throws and an expired value is still there, that value is returned and a warning is logged; without one, the exception is thrown (see When the function fails). searchDocs.content: public array Turnstile::auth( string $response )   Sends the token to https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/siteverify and returns an array:  Key	Data type	Remarkssuccess	boolean	true when the API returned success errors	array	Error messages for the API error codes  When the service cannot be reached, success is false (see When the service cannot be reached).

searchDocs.title: How to use​
searchDocs.content: Import the class and create it with new, passing the secret key. Then pass the posted token to auth().  Controller <?php namespace Site\Controller; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; use Fegg\Tool\Captcha\ReCAPTCHA; use Fegg\Tool\Captcha\Turnstile; use Fegg\Tool\Validation; class Entry extends Controller { public function confirm() { $validation = new Validation(); // reCAPTCHA (the secret comes from site/config/env.php) $recaptcha = new ReCAPTCHA(feggEnv('FEGG_RECAPTCHA_SECRET', ''), 0.5); $result = $recaptcha->auth($this->in('g-recaptcha-response')); if (!$result['success']) { $validation->setError('g-recaptcha-response', implode(',', $result['errors'])); } // Cloudflare Turnstile $turnstile = new Turnstile(feggEnv('FEGG_TURNSTILE_SECRET', '')); $result = $turnstile->auth($this->in('cf-turnstile-response')); if (!$result['success']) { $validation->setError('cf-turnstile-response', implode(',', $result['errors'])); } } }

searchDocs.title: When the service cannot be reached​
searchDocs.content: On a timeout, an outage or an answer that is not HTTP 200 JSON, auth() fails: success is false and errors has a message asking the visitor to try again later (確認サービスに接続できませんでした。…). A warning is written to the application log. A form protected by a captcha is never accepted unchecked.

searchDocs.title: Keys​
searchDocs.content: The keys differ per server, and the secret keys must not be committed. Put them in site/config/env.php (or environment variables) and read them with feggEnv():  htdocs/_fegg/site/config/env.php 'FEGG_RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY' => '...', 'FEGG_RECAPTCHA_SECRET' => '...', 'FEGG_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY' => '...', 'FEGG_TURNSTILE_SECRET' => '...',   Use different keys (or the providers' test keys) for development and production. On a test server the keys can go in the committed site/config/env/staging.php (see Test servers deployed with git pull):  	Site key	SecretTurnstile, always passes	1x00000000000000000000AA	1x0000000000000000000000000000000AA Turnstile, always fails	2x00000000000000000000AB	2x0000000000000000000000000000000AA  Test secrets accept only the dummy token of the test site keys (Cloudflare); never use them in production. reCAPTCHA v3 has no test keys: register the test server's domain, and set FEGG_RECAPTCHA_SCORE_THRESHOLD to 1.0 to see a rejection. When a captcha is enabled but a key is empty, every form is rejected and an error is logged.

searchDocs.title: Contact form​
searchDocs.content: The contact form of the skeleton supports both. Enable one in htdocs/_fegg/site/config/contact/contact_config.php with $_enable_recaptcha or $_enable_turnstile; the file reads the keys from feggEnv():  htdocs/_fegg/site/config/contact/contact_config.php $_enable_recaptcha = true; $_recaptcha_key = feggEnv('FEGG_RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY', ''); $_recaptcha_secret = feggEnv('FEGG_RECAPTCHA_SECRET', ''); $_recaptcha_score_threshold = 0.5;   The widgets are output by site/template/main/tpl/template/antispam.tpl, and site/controller/Contact.php verifies them.

searchDocs.title: Methods​
searchDocs.content: 📄️ReCAPTCHA::__construct Set the reCAPTCHA secret key and score threshold 📄️ReCAPTCHA::auth Verify a reCAPTCHA token 📄️Turnstile::__construct Set the Turnstile secret key 📄️Turnstile::auth Verify a Turnstile token

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public static void Csv::download( string $fileName, iterable $rows [, array $options = array() ] )   Sends $rows as a CSV file to save and ends the response (it throws Fegg\Http\Halt, like displayPage()). Code after it does not run.  Rows are written one at a time and the output is not buffered: pass a generator to send many rows without holding them all in memory. The response is sent with Content-Type: text/csv (charset UTF-8 or Shift_JIS) and Cache-Control: private, no-store.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$fileName	string Name in the browser's save dialog (Japanese is fine) $rows	iterable Rows, as for toString() $options	array	array()	header, encoding, escape_formulas: see toString()

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: CMS controller use Fegg\Tool\Csv; public function export() { $rows = function () { foreach ($this->_model->order('post_date', 'desc')->all() as $row) { yield array($row['title'], $row['category'], $row['post_date']); } }; Csv::download('ニュース_' . date('Ymd') . '.csv', $rows(), array( 'header' => array('タイトル', 'カテゴリー', '投稿日'), )); }   Write the same titles that the import expects in 'columns', so an exported file can be edited and sent back (see Importing a file).

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public static string Csv::field( mixed $value [, bool $escapeFormulas = true ] )   Returns $value as toString() writes it: converted to text, with a ' before a formula, then quoted when needed (see Writing). Use it to write CSV of your own, a line at a time.  Throws \InvalidArgumentException when $value is an array.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$value	mixed String, number, bool, null or date $escapeFormulas	bool	true	false: no ' before text starting with = + - @

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: use Fegg\Tool\Csv; Csv::field('Hello'); // Hello Csv::field('a,b'); // "a,b" Csv::field('say "hi"'); // "say ""hi""" Csv::field('=1+2'); // '=1+2 Csv::field('-5'); // -5 (numeric text is not escaped) Csv::field(-5); // -5 Csv::field(null); // (empty) Csv::field(true); // 1 Csv::field(new \DateTime('2026-11-15 10:00')); // 2026-11-15 10:00:00

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public static array Csv::parse( string $text [, array $options = array() [, string $source = 'CSV' ] ] )   Returns the rows of $text, keyed by their row number (see Reading). Values are strings.  Throws \RuntimeException when, with 'header', a row has another number of fields than the header or a title of 'columns' is missing. The message starts with $source.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$text	string CSV text $options	array	array()	See below $source	string	'CSV'	Name shown in error messages (a file name)

searchDocs.title: Options​
searchDocs.content: Key	Default	Remarksheader	false	true: the first row holds the titles, and each row is keyed by them columns	array()	With header: array('Title in the file' => 'key', ...). Rows are keyed by these keys, other columns are left out, a missing title is an error. Titles are compared trimmed encoding	'auto'	'auto' (UTF-8 when the text is valid UTF-8, otherwise Shift_JIS), 'utf-8' or 'sjis'. A BOM always means UTF-8

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content:
Controller use Fegg\Tool\Csv; $text = "タイトル,メモ,投稿日
Hello,,2026-11-15

\"Two
lines\",x,2026-11-16
"; $rows = Csv::parse($text, array('header' => true, 'columns' => array('投稿日' => 'post_date', 'タイトル' => 'title'))); // array( // 2 => array('post_date' => '2026-11-15', 'title' => 'Hello'), // 4 => array('post_date' => '2026-11-16', 'title' => "Two
lines"), // )   Row 3 is empty and skipped, so the keys jump from 2 to 4.

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public static array Csv::parseUpload( string $field [, array $options = array() ] )   Reads the file sent in the file input $field from PHP's temporary file and returns its rows as parse() does. Nothing is stored. Error messages start with the name of the sent file.  Only a file that PHP received as an upload in this request is read (is_uploaded_file()), with a name ending in .csv or .txt, of at most max_size bytes.  Throws \RuntimeException when:  no file was sent, or more than one in the field;the file is larger than PHP accepts (upload_max_filesize) or than max_size;the upload failed;the name does not end in .csv or .txt;a row is broken or a title of columns is missing.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$field	string Name of the file input $options	array	array()	max_size (bytes, default 5 * 1024 * 1024: 5 MB), and header, columns, encoding of parse()

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Template <form action="{{ $site.prefix }}/import" method="post" enctype="multipart/form-data"> {{ include '/cms/parts/csrf' }} <input type="file" name="csv" accept=".csv"> <button type="submit">Import</button> </form>   CMS controller use Fegg\Tool\Csv; try { $rows = Csv::parseUpload('csv', array( 'header' => true, 'columns' => array('タイトル' => 'title', '投稿日' => 'post_date'), 'max_size' => 1024 * 1024, )); } catch (\RuntimeException $e) { $this->page['error'] = array($e->getMessage()); $this->displayPage($this->page['prefix'] . '/import'); }   The whole import, with the check of every row: Importing a file.

searchDocs.title: How to use​
searchDocs.content: The methods are static: import Fegg\Tool\Csv and call them. A CMS action that downloads a list:  htdocs/_fegg/site/controller/Cms/Entry.php <?php namespace Site\Controller\Cms; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; use Fegg\Model; use Fegg\Tool\Csv; class Entry extends Controller { protected $_cmsSection = 'entry'; public function __init() { parent::__init(); $this->_model = new Model(true, array('table' => 'cms_entry', 'id' => 'entry_id')); } public function export() { // Rows are written one at a time $rows = function () { foreach ($this->_model->order('created', 'desc')->all() as $row) { yield array($row['name'], $row['mail'], $row['created']); } }; Csv::download('entries.csv', $rows(), array('header' => array('名前', 'メール', '日時'))); } }   download() sends the file and ends the response, like displayPage(). toString() returns the same text instead.

searchDocs.title: Writing​
searchDocs.content: Lines end with CRLF, and a field is quoted when it contains ,, " or a line break.  'encoding'	Written as'utf-8-bom' (default)	UTF-8 with a BOM: Excel opens it without garbled text 'utf-8'	UTF-8 without a BOM, for other programs 'sjis'	Shift_JIS (Windows characters included), for older tools  Values are written as text: null is empty, true / false are 1 / 0, dates (\DateTimeInterface) are Y-m-d H:i:s. An array as a field throws \InvalidArgumentException. Only the values of a row are written, in their order: the keys are ignored.

searchDocs.title: Formulas​
searchDocs.content: Text that starts with =, +, -, @, a tab or a CR gets a leading ', so a spreadsheet shows what a visitor typed instead of running it as a formula ("CSV injection"). Numbers are not changed: -5 (an int, or the string "-5" read from the database) is written as -5.  Written '=1+2 -5 "'=HYPERLINK(""http://example.com"",""Click"")"   'escape_formulas' => false writes the text as it is; use it only for data no visitor can type.

searchDocs.title: Reading​
searchDocs.content: parse() reads CSV text, parseFile() a file and parseUpload() a file sent with a form.  UTF-8 (with or without a BOM) and Shift_JIS are detected: the text is UTF-8 when it is valid UTF-8, otherwise Shift_JIS. 'encoding' => 'utf-8' or 'sjis' sets it.Values are strings and are not trimmed. A field in quotes can span several lines.Empty lines are skipped.  Rows are keyed by their row number, as a spreadsheet shows it: the header is row 1, and a field over several lines is one row. An error message can name the row the user sees. Since empty lines are skipped, the keys can jump: array_values($rows) makes a list.

searchDocs.title: Header and columns​
searchDocs.content: Option	Rowsnone	Lists of fields: array(2 => array('Hello', 'news'), ...) 'header' => true	Keyed by the titles of the first row: array(2 => array('タイトル' => 'Hello', 'カテゴリー' => 'news'), ...) 'header' => true, 'columns' => array('タイトル' => 'title', ...)	Keyed by your names (array(2 => array('title' => 'Hello'), ...)). Other columns are left out, the order of the columns does not matter, and a missing title is an error  With 'header' => true, a row with another number of fields than the header throws \RuntimeException naming the row (entries.csv: row 5 has 3 fields, the header has 4).

searchDocs.title: Importing a file​
searchDocs.content: A CMS form sends the file (<form method="post" enctype="multipart/form-data"> with <input type="file" name="csv"> and the CSRF token). Check every row first, and save only when all rows are right:  htdocs/_fegg/site/controller/Cms/News.php use Fegg\Tool\Csv; use Fegg\Tool\Validation; public function import() { $this->requirePost(); // The titles the export writes, and the columns they go to $columns = array('タイトル' => 'title', 'カテゴリー' => 'category', '投稿日' => 'post_date'); try { $rows = Csv::parseUpload('csv', array('header' => true, 'columns' => $columns)); } catch (\RuntimeException $e) { $this->page['error'] = array($e->getMessage()); // no file, too large, a missing column ... $this->displayPage($this->page['prefix'] . '/import'); } $errors = Csv::rowErrors($rows, function (array $row) { $validation = new Validation(); $validation->required('title', $row['title'], array('@required', 'タイトル')); $validation->datetime('post_date', $row['post_date'], array('@date', '投稿日')); return $validation->getErrorMessage(); }); if ($errors) { // "3行目: ...": nothing is saved until every row is right $this->page['error'] = array(); foreach ($errors as $line => $messages) { $this->page['error'][] = $line . '行目: ' . implode(' ', $messages); } $this->displayPage($this->page['prefix'] . '/import'); } $this->_model->insertRows(array_values($rows)); // one transaction: all rows or none $this->redirect($this->page['prefix'] . '/index/IMPORTED'); }   A file that was exported keeps the ' added before formulas: remove it (ltrim($value, "'")) in columns that can never start with '. Rich text columns go through HtmlSanitizer::clean() as in the edit form.

searchDocs.title: Errors​
searchDocs.content: A file that cannot be read, a broken row, a missing column, or an upload that is missing, failed, too large or not .csv / .txt throws \RuntimeException. The message names the file and, for a row, its number: it can be shown to the CMS user.An unknown encoding, 'columns' without 'header' => true or an array as a field throws \InvalidArgumentException (a mistake in the code).

searchDocs.title: Methods​
searchDocs.content: 📄️Csv::toString Return rows as CSV text 📄️Csv::download Send rows as a CSV download and end the response 📄️Csv::parse Read CSV text 📄️Csv::parseFile Read a CSV file 📄️Csv::parseUpload Read a CSV file sent with a form 📄️Csv::rowErrors Check every row and collect the messages by row number 📄️Csv::field One value as a CSV field

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public static array Csv::parseFile( string $path [, array $options = array() ] )   Reads the file and returns its rows as parse() does; error messages start with the path.  Throws \RuntimeException when the file cannot be read or a row is broken.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$path	string Path of the file $options	array	array()	header, columns, encoding: see parse()

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\Csv; $shops = Csv::parseFile(FEGG_SITE_DIR . '/config/shops.csv', array('header' => true)); foreach ($shops as $line => $shop) { // $shop['店名'], $shop['住所'] ... }   For a file sent from a form, use parseUpload().

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public static array Csv::rowErrors( array $rows, callable $validate )   Calls $validate for each row and returns the messages of the rows that fail, keyed by row number: array(3 => array('...', '...'), 7 => array('...')). Returns an empty array when every row is fine.  $validate takes a row and returns its messages as an array, or false, null or an empty array when the row is fine. The return value of Validation::getErrorMessage() fits directly.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$rows	array Rows from parse(), parseFile() or parseUpload(), keyed by row number $validate	callable function (array $row): returns the messages of the row

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: CMS controller use Fegg\Tool\Csv; use Fegg\Tool\Validation; $errors = Csv::rowErrors($rows, function (array $row) { $validation = new Validation(); $validation->required('title', $row['title'], array('@required', 'タイトル')); $validation->maxlength('title', $row['title'], 100, array('@maxlength', 'タイトル', 100)); return $validation->getErrorMessage(); }); foreach ($errors as $line => $messages) { $this->page['error'][] = $line . '行目: ' . implode(' ', $messages); }   Create a new Validation for each row, so the messages of one row do not carry over to the next.

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public static string Csv::toString( iterable $rows [, array $options = array() ] )   Returns the CSV text of $rows, with a BOM first for 'utf-8-bom' (see Writing).

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$rows	iterable Rows: arrays (lists or associative; only the values are written), or a generator $options	array	array()	See below

searchDocs.title: Options​
searchDocs.content: Key	Default	Remarksheader	array()	Titles written as the first row encoding	'utf-8-bom'	'utf-8-bom', 'utf-8' or 'sjis' escape_formulas	true	false writes text starting with = + - @ as it is (see Formulas)

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\Csv; $csv = Csv::toString(array( array('Hello, world', 3, true, null), array('=SUM(A1:A2)', -5, false, new \DateTime('2026-11-15 10:00')), ), array('header' => array('Text', 'Number', 'Flag', 'Date'), 'encoding' => 'utf-8'));   $csv Text,Number,Flag,Date "Hello, world",3,1, '=SUM(A1:A2),-5,0,2026-11-15 10:00:00   Use it to attach a CSV to a mail or save it to a file; download() sends it to the browser.

searchDocs.title: How to use​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Database\Pdo; $db = new Pdo(); // Raw SQL with ? placeholders $rows = $db->setQuery( 'SELECT category, count(*) AS n FROM cms_news WHERE valid = 1 GROUP BY category HAVING n > ?', array(1) )->execute()->all(); // Or build the query $rows = $db->setWhere('category = ?', 2)->setOrder('post_date DESC')->select('cms_news')->execute()->all();   A query is built with the set* methods and a build method (select, count, insert, update, delete ...), or written with setQuery. execute runs it, then all, one, getAffectedRow or getLastIndexId read the result. After execute() the built query is forgotten, so each query starts clean.

searchDocs.title: Automatic queries​
searchDocs.content: Queries built with the build methods get the automatic parts of database_regular_use_query.php (see Configuration): valid = 1 on SELECT and count, created / modified / valid on INSERT and modified on UPDATE. Queries written with setQuery() get nothing added.

searchDocs.title: Values and placeholders​
searchDocs.content: Values are always bound to ? placeholders. Integers and booleans are bound as integers, null as NULL, everything else as strings (so count(*) > ? works on SQLite).In setWhere, setHaving and setOn, an array bound to one placeholder expands it: id = ? and id IN (?) become id IN (?, ?, ...), <> / != / NOT IN become NOT IN, LIKE ? becomes (... LIKE ? OR ... LIKE ?) and NOT LIKE ? becomes (... NOT LIKE ? AND ...). An empty array matches no row (=, IN, LIKE) or every row (<>, NOT IN, NOT LIKE). An array on any other operator (<, BETWEEN ...) throws InvalidArgumentException.A ? inside a quoted string literal ('?') is not a placeholder.Table, column and ORDER BY text given to the set* methods is written into the SQL as it is: never put user input in it.

searchDocs.title: Errors​
searchDocs.content: A failed connection or query throws Fegg\Database\QueryException (a RuntimeException). Its message ends with the SQL with its values filled in, for example no such column: nope (SQL: SELECT nope FROM cms_news WHERE title = 'it''s'). getSql() returns the SQL with its ? placeholders and getParameters() the values. Uncaught, it becomes an HTTP 500 and is written to the PHP error log and the application log.  Controller use Fegg\Database\QueryException; try { $db->setQuery($sql, $params)->execute(); } catch (QueryException $e) { // e.g. a duplicate key error_log($e->getMessage()); }

searchDocs.title: Connections and transactions​
searchDocs.content: Connections are opened once per DSN and user name and shared by every Pdo instance and every model.SELECT and PRAGMA queries run on a slave, other queries on the master (see Configuration). masterServer and slaveServer choose the server for the next query.beginTransaction opens a transaction on the master. Until commit or rollBack, every query of every instance and every model runs inside it. Model::transaction does this for you.

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public array Pdo::all( [ string $index = '' ] )   Returns the rows of the last SELECT or PRAGMA run with execute, as associative arrays. With $index, the rows are keyed by that column.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$index	string	''	Column to use as the array key

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $rows = $db->setItem('news_id, title')->select('cms_news')->execute()->all(); // -> array(0 => array('news_id' => 1, 'title' => 'A'), 1 => array('news_id' => 2, 'title' => 'B'), ...) $rows = $db->setItem('news_id, title')->select('cms_news')->execute()->all('news_id'); // -> array(1 => array('news_id' => 1, 'title' => 'A'), 2 => array('news_id' => 2, 'title' => 'B'), ...)

searchDocs.title: Database connect setting​
searchDocs.content: The connection is set in htdocs/_fegg/site/config/database_config.php. The skeleton's file reads these values with feggEnv() (an environment variable, then site/config/env.php, see Settings), so the file itself is committed and the same on every server.  Name	Default	RemarksFEGG_DB_DSN	sqlite: + FEGG_DB_PATH	PDO DSN FEGG_DB_USER	''	User name (MySQL) FEGG_DB_PASSWORD	''	Password (MySQL) FEGG_DB_SLAVE_DSN	FEGG_DB_DSN	Read-only replica FEGG_DB_PATH	site/data/db/db.db	SQLite file. As an environment variable without FEGG_DB_DSN, it wins over FEGG_DB_DSN in env.php (the test suite uses it)  The file fills two entries. dsn, username and password are passed to PHP's PDO:  site/config/database_config.php (shape) $database_config['master'] = array('dsn' => ..., 'username' => ..., 'password' => ...); $database_config['slave'] = array( array('dsn' => ..., 'username' => ..., 'password' => ...), // more than one server allowed );   master is used for INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, schema changes and transactions. SELECT and PRAGMA queries use one of the slave entries, picked at random. With a single database, both use the same DSN.new \Fegg\Database\Pdo('name') reads name/database_config.php and name/database_regular_use_query.php instead, for a second database.

searchDocs.title: MySQL​
searchDocs.content: SQLite is the default. For MySQL (5.7 / 8.x) or MariaDB, set the connection in site/config/env.php (or as environment variables):  site/config/env.php 'FEGG_DB_DSN' => 'mysql:host=127.0.0.1;port=3306;dbname=example;charset=utf8mb4', 'FEGG_DB_USER' => 'example', 'FEGG_DB_PASSWORD' => '...',   Always add charset=utf8mb4 to the DSN, or emoji and other 4-byte characters are lost.The connection runs with sql_mode = ANSI_QUOTES: Fegg quotes names with ", so in raw SQL write string literals with single quotes (WHERE title = 'foo', not "foo", which is a column name). Queries are buffered../fegg-cli migration, migration:db2schema and /cms/migrate/ work on MySQL as on SQLite. Tables are created as InnoDB with utf8mb4_unicode_ci, and changed tables are altered in place (ADD / MODIFY / DROP COLUMN).  The YAML types are mapped like this (a size written in the YAML, such as VARCHAR(100), is used as written):  YAML type	MySQL typeINTEGER	INT CHAR	VARCHAR(255) TEXT	MEDIUMTEXT BOOLEAN	TINYINT(1) DATETIME	DATETIME BLOB	LONGBLOB REAL	DOUBLE  The YAML type is kept in the column comment (fegg:CHAR), so migration:db2schema writes the same YAML back. Indexes on TEXT columns use the first 191 characters.  fegg-cli migration drops the tables and columns that are not in the YAML files (see migration): give the site a database of its own, never one shared with another application.  The skeleton's MySQL tests run with composer test:mysql against the server set in FEGG_TEST_MYSQL_DSN, FEGG_TEST_MYSQL_USER and FEGG_TEST_MYSQL_PASSWORD. Each test creates and drops its own database.

searchDocs.title: Automatic append query configuration​
searchDocs.content: The queries added automatically to queries built by Fegg\Model and the build methods of Fegg\Database\Pdo are set in htdocs/_fegg/core/config/database_regular_use_query.php. To change them, copy the file to site/config/ (see Overriding the core); the whole file is replaced.  CURRENT_TABLE is replaced with the table name, and now() with the current date and time. An item that the query already sets (for example valid given to insertRow()) is not added again.  core/config/database_regular_use_query.php <?php defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; /** * Automatically appended queries * * Queries appended automatically when the "select", "insert", "update" and "delete" methods of the DB class run * (to be extended as needed). */ $database_regular_use_query = array( // Queries appended regardless of the table 'regular_use' => array( 'select' => array( 'where' => 'CURRENT_TABLE.valid = 1', 'order' => '', ), 'count' => array( 'where' => 'CURRENT_TABLE.valid = 1', 'order' => '', ), 'insert' => array( 'item' => 'modified = now(), created = now(), valid = 1', ), 'update' => array( 'item' => "modified = now()", 'where' => '', ), ), /* // Queries appended per table 'table' => array( 'table_name' => array( 'select' => array( 'where' => 'show_flag = 0', 'order' => '', ), 'insert' => array( 'item' => 'update_time = now(), create_datetime = now()', ), 'update' => array( 'item' => 'update_time = now()', 'where' => '', ), ), ), */ );   These queries are why the model needs its required columns. To skip these queries, see unsetRegularUseQuery(), unsetRegularUseQueryForTable() and disabledRegularUseQuery() (Model, Pdo).

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public void Pdo::beginTransaction()   Opens a transaction on the master database. Until commit or rollBack, every query of every Pdo instance and every model runs inside it.  Throws LogicException when a transaction is already open. With models, prefer Model::transaction(), which commits, rolls back and handles nesting for you.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Database\Pdo; $db = new Pdo(); $db->beginTransaction(); try { $db->setValues(array('title' => 'A'))->insert('cms_news')->execute(); $db->setValues(array('title' => 'B'))->insert('cms_lab')->execute(); $db->commit(); } catch (\Throwable $e) { $db->rollBack(); throw $e; }

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public void Pdo::close()   Drops the connection this instance used from the shared connections, so the next query (of any instance) opens a new one. The connection of an open transaction is kept. PHP closes connections at the end of the request, so this is rarely needed.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $rows = $db->select('cms_news')->execute()->all(); $db->close();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public static void Pdo::closeAll()   Drops every shared connection. An open transaction is rolled back. The next query opens a new connection. Useful in long-running commands and tests.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Database\Pdo; Pdo::closeAll();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public void Pdo::commit()   Commits the transaction opened with beginTransaction. Any instance can commit it. Throws LogicException when no transaction is open.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $db->beginTransaction(); $db->setValues(array('title' => 'A'))->insert('cms_news')->execute(); $db->commit();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public Pdo::__construct( [ string $env = '' ] )   Loads database_config.php and database_regular_use_query.php (see Configuration). Nothing is connected until the first query; connections are shared by every instance.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$env	string	''	Config sub directory: 'name' reads name/database_config.php and name/database_regular_use_query.php

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Database\Pdo; $db = new Pdo(); $rows = $db->setQuery('SELECT * FROM cms_news WHERE valid = 1 AND category = ?', array(2))->execute()->all();

searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::createIndex( string $table, array $field )   Builds Create [UNIQUE] Index "name" ON "table" (columns).

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$table	string Table name $field	array Index definition (below)

searchDocs.title: Index definition​
searchDocs.content: Key	Data type	Remarksname	string	Index name unique	boolean	Create a UNIQUE index target	string	Columns, separated by commas

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // Create UNIQUE Index "sample_title" ON "sample" (title) $db->createIndex('sample', array('name' => 'sample_title', 'unique' => true, 'target' => 'title'))->execute();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::count( string $table )   Builds Select Count(*) as number_of_records From (...) AS "count_temp" around the SELECT that select would build, so conditions, joins and groups are counted correctly. Read the result with one()['number_of_records'].

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$table	string Target table name

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $record = $db->setWhere('category = ?', 2)->count('cms_news')->execute()->one(); $count = (int) $record['number_of_records'];

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::compile()   Builds the query without running it or forgetting it. Read it with getQuery and getParam, or with the values filled in with getLastQuery.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $db->setWhere('category = ?', 2)->setOrder('created desc')->setLimit(10, 20)->select('cms_news')->compile(); echo $db->getQuery(); // -> Select * From "cms_news" Where category = ? And "cms_news".valid = 1 Order By created desc Limit 20, 10 print_r($db->getParam()); // -> Array ( [0] => 2 )

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::createTable( string $table, array $field )   Builds a Create Table. Tables are normally defined in site/config/database/*.yaml and created with ./fegg-cli migration.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$table	string Table name $field	array List of column definitions (below)

searchDocs.title: Column definition​
searchDocs.content: Every key must be present.  Key	Data type	Remarksname	string	Column name type	string	Column type notnull	boolean	Add NOT NULL dflt_value	mixed	Default value (null, '' or 0: no default) pk	boolean	Add PRIMARY KEY ai	boolean	Add AUTOINCREMENT

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // Create Table "sample" (id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, title TEXT DEFAULT 'none') $db->createTable('sample', array( array('name' => 'id', 'type' => 'INTEGER', 'notnull' => true, 'dflt_value' => null, 'pk' => true, 'ai' => true), array('name' => 'title', 'type' => 'TEXT', 'notnull' => false, 'dflt_value' => 'none', 'pk' => false, 'ai' => false), ))->execute();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::delete( [ string $table = '' ] )   Builds a DELETE on $table with the condition set with setWhere. This removes the rows; for a soft delete (valid = 0) use Model::delete().  Pdo does not refuse a DELETE without a condition: without setWhere() every row is removed.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$table	string	''	Target table name

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // Delete From "cms_news" Where news_id = ? $db->setWhere('news_id = ?', 3)->delete('cms_news')->execute(); $deleted = $db->getAffectedRow();
