searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::disabledRegularUseQuery()   Skips every automatic query (for every table and for the table, see Configuration) for every later query of this instance. To skip them for one query only, use unsetRegularUseQuery and unsetRegularUseQueryForTable.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $db->disabledRegularUseQuery(); // Select * From "cms_news" (also the rows with valid = 0) $rows = $db->select('cms_news')->execute()->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::execute()   Builds the query (when a build method such as select was called) or takes the one set with setQuery, and runs it. SELECT and PRAGMA queries run on a slave and their rows are read with all or one; other queries run on the master. Inside a transaction every query runs on the transaction's connection. Afterwards the query being built is forgotten (see unsetInitQueryFlag).  Throws Fegg\Database\QueryException when the connection or the query fails. Its message ends with the SQL with the values filled in.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $rows = $db->setWhere('category = ?', 2)->select('cms_news')->execute()->all(); $db->setValues(array('title' => 'Sample'))->insert('cms_news')->execute(); $id = $db->getLastIndexId();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public int Pdo::getAffectedRow()   Returns the number of rows the last query inserted, updated or deleted. After a SELECT the value depends on the driver (0 on SQLite); count the rows of all instead.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $db->setValues(array('visible' => 0))->setWhere('category = ?', 3)->update('cms_news')->execute(); $updated = $db->getAffectedRow(); // -> 4

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public string Pdo::getLastIndexId()   Returns the ID generated by the last INSERT on the connection (PDO::lastInsertId()), as a string. Call it on the same instance, right after execute.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $db->setValues(array('title' => 'Sample'))->insert('cms_news')->execute(); $id = (int) $db->getLastIndexId(); // -> 24

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public string Pdo::getLastQuery()   Returns the last query run with execute (or built with compile), with the values filled in and quoted. It is for logs and debugging only: never run the result. To get the SQL and the values separately, use getQuery and getParam.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $db->setWhere('title = ?', "it's")->select('cms_news')->execute(); echo $db->getLastQuery(); // -> Select * From "cms_news" Where title = 'it''s' And "cms_news".valid = 1

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public array Pdo::getParam()   Returns the values bound to the ? placeholders of the last query built by compile or execute, in order.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $db->setWhere('category = ? AND news_id IN (?)', 2, array(5, 6))->select('cms_news')->compile(); print_r($db->getParam()); // -> Array ( [0] => 2 [1] => 5 [2] => 6 )

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public string Pdo::getQuery()   Returns the last query built by compile or execute, with its ? placeholders. getParam returns the values.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $db->setWhere('category = ?', 2)->select('cms_news')->compile(); echo $db->getQuery(); // -> Select * From "cms_news" Where category = ? And "cms_news".valid = 1

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public array Pdo::getLastQueryDebug()   Returns array('query' => ..., 'parameter' => ...): the last query with its ? placeholders, and the values bound to them.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $db->setWhere('category = ?', 2)->select('cms_news')->execute(); print_r($db->getLastQueryDebug());   Output Array ( [query] => Select * From "cms_news" Where category = ? And "cms_news".valid = 1 [parameter] => Array ( [0] => 2 ) )

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::insert( string $table )   Builds an INSERT on $table from the values set with setValues (or setItem). created, modified and valid are added unless given (see Configuration). Run it with execute and read the new ID with getLastIndexId.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$table	string Target table name

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // Insert Into "cms_news" ("title", "category", modified, created, valid) Values (?, ?, ?, ?, ?) $db->setValues(array('title' => 'Sample', 'category' => 2))->insert('cms_news')->execute(); $id = $db->getLastIndexId(); // -> '24'

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public array Pdo::id( string $index )   Returns the values of one column of every row of the last SELECT, as a list.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$index	string Column name

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $titles = $db->setItem('title')->select('cms_news')->execute()->id('title'); // -> array('A', 'B', 'C')

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public bool Pdo::inTransaction()   Returns true while a transaction opened with beginTransaction (by any instance, or by Model::transaction()) is open.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); if (!$db->inTransaction()) { $db->beginTransaction(); }

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::masterServer()   Connects to the master database (see Configuration) and runs the next query on it, also when it is a SELECT. Use it to read a row right after writing it when the slaves may lag behind. Throws Fegg\Database\QueryException when the connection fails.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $db->setValues(array('title' => 'Sample'))->insert('cms_news')->execute(); $id = $db->getLastIndexId(); // Read it back from the master $row = $db->masterServer()->setWhere('news_id = ?', $id)->select('cms_news')->execute()->one();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public int|null Pdo::getReturnCode()   Returns the number of affected rows of the last query that was not a SELECT or PRAGMA (null before the first one). Prefer getAffectedRow. A failed query throws Fegg\Database\QueryException, so there is no error code to check.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $db->setValues(array('title' => 'Sample'))->insert('cms_news')->execute(); $code = $db->getReturnCode(); // -> 1

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public array|null Pdo::one()   Returns the first row of the last SELECT or PRAGMA, or null when it returned no row.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $row = $db->setWhere('news_id = ?', 1)->select('cms_news')->execute()->one(); if ($row === null) { // not found }

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::reset()   Forgets everything set for the next query (table, items, conditions, joins, order, limit ...), turns the reset after execute back on (see unsetInitQueryFlag) and re-enables the automatic queries unless disabledRegularUseQuery was called. The result and the last query are kept.  execute() already does this after a successful query. A query that throws keeps its state, so call reset() after catching a QueryException when you reuse the instance. Fegg\Model does this by itself.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Database\QueryException; $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); try { $db->setWhere('no_such_column = ?', 1)->select('cms_news')->execute(); } catch (QueryException $e) { $db->reset(); } $rows = $db->select('cms_news')->execute()->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::pragma( string $table, string $mode )   Builds an SQLite PRAGMA on $table. Read the rows with all after execute. SQLite only.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$table	string Table name $mode	string Pragma mode (below)

searchDocs.title: Pragma mode​
searchDocs.content: Mode	Querytable	PRAGMA table_info("table") (also any unknown mode) index_list	PRAGMA index_list("table") index	PRAGMA index_info("table")

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // Columns of cms_news: cid, name, type, notnull, dflt_value, pk $columns = $db->pragma('cms_news', 'table')->execute()->all(); // Indexes of cms_news: seq, name, unique, origin, partial $indexes = $db->pragma('cms_news', 'index_list')->execute()->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public void Pdo::rollBack()   Discards every write since beginTransaction. Any instance can roll it back. Throws LogicException when no transaction is open.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $db->beginTransaction(); try { $db->setValues(array('title' => 'A'))->insert('cms_news')->execute(); $db->commit(); } catch (\Throwable $e) { $db->rollBack(); throw $e; }

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::setGroup( string $query )   Sets GROUP BY. The text is written into the SQL as it is: never put user input in it. Another call appends its text directly, without a comma, so give every column in one call.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$query	string Columns, separated by commas

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // Select category, count(*) AS n From "cms_news" Where "cms_news".valid = 1 Group By category $rows = $db->setItem('category, count(*) AS n')->setGroup('category')->select('cms_news')->execute()->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::select( string $table )   Builds a SELECT on $table from what was set with setItem (columns, default *), setJoin / setOn, setWhere, setGroup, setHaving, setOrder and setLimit. CURRENT_TABLE.valid = 1 is added (see Configuration). Run it with execute.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$table	string Target table name

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // Select * From "cms_news" Where category = ? And "cms_news".valid = 1 Order By post_date DESC Limit 0, 10 $rows = $db->setWhere('category = ?', 2) ->setOrder('post_date DESC') ->setLimit(10) ->select('cms_news') ->execute() ->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::setIncrement( string $column, int|float $by )   Adds "column" = "column" + ? to an update, so the addition happens in the database and simultaneous requests do not lose counts. Model::increment() uses it.  Throws InvalidArgumentException when $column is not a plain name or $by is not an int or a float.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$column	string Numeric column $by	int/float Amount to add; negative to subtract

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // Update "cms_news" Set modified = ?, "view_count" = "view_count" + ? Where news_id = ? $db->setIncrement('view_count', 1)->setWhere('news_id = ?', 5)->update('cms_news')->execute();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::setHaving( string $query, [ mixed ...$parameters ] )   Adds to the HAVING clause, used with setGroup. Parameters work as in setWhere: one per placeholder, and an array expands its placeholder.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$query	string Condition with ? placeholders ...$parameters	mixed One value (or array of values) per placeholder

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // Select category, count(*) AS n From "cms_news" Where "cms_news".valid = 1 Group By category Having count(*) > ? $rows = $db->setItem('category, count(*) AS n') ->setGroup('category') ->setHaving('count(*) > ?', 3) ->select('cms_news') ->execute() ->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::setInitQueryFlag()   Turns the reset after execute back on (the default), after unsetInitQueryFlag.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // Count and fetch with the same conditions $db->unsetInitQueryFlag()->setWhere('category = ?', 2); $count = $db->count('cms_news')->execute()->one(); $db->setInitQueryFlag()->setLimit(10); $rows = $db->select('cms_news')->execute()->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::setItem( string $query, [ array $parameter = '' ] )   Sets the columns of a query.  Without $parameter: the columns of a SELECT ('news_id, title', expressions allowed).With an associative array: the values of an INSERT / UPDATE, matched to the columns in $query by name. A listed column missing from the array is written as ''.With a list: the values in the order of the columns in $query.  For INSERT and UPDATE, prefer setValues: it writes only the given columns, can store NULL and checks the column names.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$query	string Columns, separated by commas $parameter	array	''	Values (by name or by position)

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // Select news_id, title From "cms_news" Where "cms_news".valid = 1 $rows = $db->setItem('news_id, title')->select('cms_news')->execute()->all(); // Insert Into "cms_news" ("title", "category", modified, created, valid) Values (?, ?, ?, ?, ?) $db->setItem('title, category', array('title' => 'Sample', 'category' => 2))->insert('cms_news')->execute();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::setLimit( int $limit, [ int $offset = 0 ] )   Adds Limit offset, limit to a SELECT.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$limit	int Maximum number of rows $offset	int	0	Number of rows to skip

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // ... Order By post_date DESC Limit 20, 10 (rows 21 to 30) $rows = $db->setOrder('post_date DESC')->setLimit(10, 20)->select('cms_news')->execute()->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::setJoin( string|array $table, [ string $type = null ] )   Adds a JOIN. Follow it with setOn for the condition. $table is a table name or array('table', 'alias'); the names are quoted as they are.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$table	string/array Table name, or array('table', 'alias') $type	string	null	'LEFT', 'INNER' or 'RIGHT' (anything else: plain JOIN)

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // Select cms_news.title, f.org_name From "cms_news" LEFT JOIN "cms_file" AS "f" ON f.file_id = cms_news.file_id AND f.valid = ? Where "cms_news".valid = 1 $rows = $db->setItem('cms_news.title, f.org_name') ->setJoin(array('cms_file', 'f'), 'LEFT') ->setOn('f.file_id = cms_news.file_id AND f.valid = ?', 1) ->select('cms_news') ->execute() ->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::setOn( string $query, [ mixed ...$parameters ] )   Adds the ON condition of the last setJoin. The first call after setJoin() writes ON; another call appends its text after a space. Parameters work as in setWhere.  Throws LogicException when no join was set before.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$query	string Condition with ? placeholders ...$parameters	mixed One value (or array of values) per placeholder

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // ... LEFT JOIN "cms_file" ON cms_file.file_id = cms_news.file_id AND cms_file.type = ? ... $rows = $db->setJoin('cms_file', 'LEFT') ->setOn('cms_file.file_id = cms_news.file_id') ->setOn('AND cms_file.type = ?', 'pdf') ->select('cms_news') ->execute() ->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::setOrder( string $query )   Sets ORDER BY. The text is written into the SQL as it is: never put user input in it. Another call appends its text directly, so give every sort key in one call.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$query	string ORDER BY expression

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // ... Order By post_date DESC, news_id DESC $rows = $db->setOrder('post_date DESC, news_id DESC')->select('cms_news')->execute()->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::setQuery( string $query, [ array $parameter = [] ] )   Sets the SQL to run with execute, as it is.  $parameter is the list of values for the ? placeholders, in order. Arrays are not expanded here (they are in setWhere); write one ? per value.Nothing is added automatically: write valid = 1 yourself.Only queries that start with SELECT or PRAGMA return rows (all, one) and run on a slave. Any other query (including WITH ... SELECT) runs on the master as a statement; read getAffectedRow after it.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$query	string SQL with ? placeholders $parameter	array	[]	Values, in placeholder order

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $rows = $db->setQuery( 'SELECT category, count(*) AS n FROM cms_news WHERE valid = 1 GROUP BY category HAVING n > ?', array(1) )->execute()->all(); $db->setQuery('UPDATE cms_news SET visible = ? WHERE post_date < ?', array(0, '2020-01-01'))->execute(); $updated = $db->getAffectedRow();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::setWhere( string $query, [ mixed ...$parameters ] )   Adds to the WHERE clause. Give one argument per ? placeholder, after the query.  Another call appends its text after a space: write the AND / OR yourself (setWhere('AND title = ?', $title)).An array bound to one placeholder expands it (id IN (?, ?, ...)), see Values and placeholders.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$query	string Condition with ? placeholders ...$parameters	mixed One value (or array of values) per placeholder

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // ... Where category = ? AND title = ? And "cms_news".valid = 1 $rows = $db->setWhere('category = ?', 1) ->setWhere('AND title = ?', 'A') ->select('cms_news') ->execute() ->all(); // ... Where post_date >= ? AND news_id IN (?, ?, ?) ... $rows = $db->setWhere('post_date >= ? AND news_id IN (?)', '2026-01-01', array(1, 2, 3)) ->select('cms_news') ->execute() ->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::setValues( array $values )   Sets the values of an INSERT or UPDATE from column => value pairs. Unlike setItem, only the given columns are written and null is stored as NULL. Model::insertRow() and Model::updateRow() use it.  Throws InvalidArgumentException for an empty array, a column name that is not a plain name (letters, digits and _, optionally table.column), or a value that is an array or an object.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$values	array Values (column => value)

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // Insert Into "cms_news" ("title", "image_id", modified, created, valid) Values ('Sample', NULL, ...) $db->setValues(array('title' => 'Sample', 'image_id' => null))->insert('cms_news')->execute(); // Update "cms_news" Set "title"= ?, modified = ? Where news_id = ? $db->setValues(array('title' => 'New title'))->setWhere('news_id = ?', 1)->update('cms_news')->execute();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::slaveServer()   Connects to one of the slave databases, picked at random (see Configuration), and runs the next query on it. SELECT and PRAGMA queries already use a slave; this sends another query there. Throws Fegg\Database\QueryException when the connection fails.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // Same as without slaveServer(): a SELECT already uses a slave $rows = $db->slaveServer()->select('cms_news')->execute()->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public array Pdo::simpleArray( string $keyName, string $valueName )   Returns key => value pairs built from two columns of every row of the last SELECT, for example for <select> options.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$keyName	string Column to use as the key $valueName	string Column to use as the value

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $titles = $db->setItem('news_id, title')->select('cms_news')->execute()->simpleArray('news_id', 'title'); // -> array(1 => 'A', 2 => 'B', 3 => 'C')

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::truncate( string $table )   Builds Truncate "table", which removes every row. MySQL only: SQLite has no TRUNCATE (use delete without a condition there).

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$table	string Target table name

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // Truncate "sample_log" $db->truncate('sample_log')->execute();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::unsetInitQueryFlag()   Keeps what was set (items, conditions, joins, order, limit ...) after execute, so the next query can reuse it. Model::find() uses it to count and fetch with the same conditions. Turn it back on with setInitQueryFlag, or drop everything with reset.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // Count and fetch with the same conditions $db->unsetInitQueryFlag()->setWhere('category = ?', 2); $count = $db->count('cms_news')->execute()->one(); $db->setInitQueryFlag()->setLimit(10); $rows = $db->select('cms_news')->execute()->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::unsetRegularUseQuery()   For the next query only, skips the queries added for every table (regular_use in database_regular_use_query.php, see Configuration): valid = 1 on SELECT and count, created / modified / valid on INSERT and modified on UPDATE.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // Select * From "cms_news" $db->unsetRegularUseQuery()->select('cms_news')->execute(); // Select * From "cms_news" Where "cms_news".valid = 1 (the next query is back to normal) $db->select('cms_news')->execute();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::unsetRegularUseQueryForTable()   For the next query only, skips the queries configured for the table (the table section of database_regular_use_query.php, see Configuration). The queries added for every table still apply.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); $rows = $db->unsetRegularUseQueryForTable()->select('cms_news')->execute()->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Pdo::update( string $table )   Builds an UPDATE on $table from the values set with setValues (or setItem) and setIncrement, and the condition set with setWhere. modified is added unless given. Run it with execute and read the number of updated rows with getAffectedRow.  Unlike Model::updateRowsWhere(), Pdo does not refuse an UPDATE without a condition: without setWhere() every row is updated.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$table	string Target table name

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $db = new \Fegg\Database\Pdo(); // Update "cms_news" Set "title"= ?, modified = ? Where news_id IN (?, ?) $db->setValues(array('title' => 'New title')) ->setWhere('news_id IN (?)', array(1, 2)) ->update('cms_news') ->execute(); $updated = $db->getAffectedRow(); // -> 2

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public static bool Embed::isYoutubeEmbed( string $src )   Returns true when $src is a YouTube player URL that may be saved as the src of an iframe: https://www.youtube.com/embed/... or https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/..., with only simple parameters. Fegg\Cms\HtmlSanitizer keeps the iframes of the editor's text whose src this method (or Embed::isMapEmbed) accepts.  To read the URL of a video page, use Embed::youtubeUrl.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$src	string URL to check

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\Embed; Embed::isYoutubeEmbed('https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/dQw4w9WgXcQ?start=90'); // -> true Embed::isYoutubeEmbed('https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ'); // -> false

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public static bool Embed::isMapEmbed( string $src )   Returns true when $src is the URL of Google Maps' "Embed a map" (https://www.google.com/maps/embed?pb=...). Fegg\Cms\HtmlSanitizer keeps the iframes of the editor's text whose src this method (or Embed::isYoutubeEmbed) accepts.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$src	string URL to check

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\Embed; Embed::isMapEmbed('https://www.google.com/maps/embed?pb=!1m18!1m12'); // -> true Embed::isMapEmbed('https://maps.google.com/?q=Tokyo'); // -> false

searchDocs.title: In a template​
searchDocs.content: For a CMS field of its own (a "YouTube URL" or "map" input), print the block with the template modifiers feggYoutube and feggMap. They write nothing for another value. The result is HTML, so add noescape (the URL is checked and escaped by the modifier).  Template {{ $page.data.youtube_url|feggYoutube|noescape }} {{ $page.data.youtube_url|feggYoutube:'9-16':'center':50|noescape }} {{ $page.data.map|feggMap|noescape }} {{ $page.data.map|feggMap:'16-9':'center':80|noescape }}   The arguments are the ratio, the alignment and the width in % of the text (see Options). Leave one empty ('') to keep its default.  Output <div data-youtube-video class="fegg-video"><iframe src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/dQw4w9WgXcQ" width="640" height="360" allowfullscreen></iframe></div>   For feggMap, the CMS field holds the <iframe> that Google Maps gives ("Share" > "Embed a map"), or only its URL.  The styles of these blocks are those of the editor's text, under .c-entry-block (the site's scss/object/component/_wysiwyg.scss, see CMS screens and the editor). Put the block inside <div class="c-entry-block">, or style .fegg-video / .fegg-map in the project.

searchDocs.title: In PHP​
searchDocs.content: Controller <?php namespace Site\Controller; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; use Fegg\Tool\Embed; class Movie extends Controller { public function index() { // https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/xxxxxxxxxxx, or null $this->page['youtube'] = Embed::youtubeUrl('https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xxxxxxxxxxx'); $this->displayPage('movie'); } }   Template {{ if $page.youtube }} <iframe src="{{ $page.youtube|feggUrl }}" width="640" height="360" allowfullscreen class="c-youtube"></iframe> {{ end }}   For other oEmbed services, ask them with Fegg\Http\Client in the project.

searchDocs.title: YouTube URLs​
searchDocs.content: These URLs are read (also on m.youtube.com and youtube-nocookie.com, http or https):  URL	Embed URLhttps://www.youtube.com/watch?v=<id>	.../embed/<id> https://youtu.be/<id>	.../embed/<id> https://www.youtube.com/shorts/<id>	.../embed/<id> (shown 9:16) https://www.youtube.com/live/<id>, /embed/<id>, /v/<id>	.../embed/<id> https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=<list>	.../embed/videoseries?list=<list>  A start time (t= or start=, written 90, 90s, 1m30s or 1h2m3s) becomes ?start=<seconds>. Other parameters are dropped. A video ID must be 11 characters.

searchDocs.title: Options​
searchDocs.content: Embed::youtube, Embed::map and the modifiers take these options.  Option	Values	Defaultratio	Video: '16-9', '9-16'. Map: '4-3', '16-9', '1-1'	Video: '16-9' (a short: '9-16'). Map: '4-3' align	'center', 'right'	Left width	% of the text, 10 to 100	100  The ratio becomes the class is-<ratio> (none for the default one), the alignment aligncenter / alignright, the width style="width: N%". Other values are ignored.

searchDocs.title: Methods​
searchDocs.content: 📄️Embed::youtubeUrl Get the embed URL of a YouTube video or playlist 📄️Embed::isYoutubeShort Check whether a URL is a YouTube short 📄️Embed::mapUrl Get the embed URL of a Google map 📄️Embed::isYoutubeEmbed Check whether a URL is a YouTube player URL 📄️Embed::isMapEmbed Check whether a URL is a Google Maps embed URL 📄️Embed::youtube Get the HTML of a YouTube video as the editor writes it 📄️Embed::map Get the HTML of a Google map as the editor writes it

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public static bool Embed::isYoutubeShort( string $url )   Returns true when $url is a YouTube short (/shorts/<id>). Embed::youtube shows a short 9:16 unless another ratio is given.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$url	string YouTube URL

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\Embed; Embed::isYoutubeShort('https://www.youtube.com/shorts/dQw4w9WgXcQ'); // -> true Embed::isYoutubeShort('https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ'); // -> false

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public static string Embed::map( string $pasted, [ array $options = array() ] )   Returns the block the editor writes for a map, or '' when $pasted is not a Google Maps embed (the <iframe> of "Share" > "Embed a map", or its URL). The template modifier feggMap calls this method.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$pasted	string The <iframe> of Google Maps, or its URL $options	array	array()	ratio ('4-3', '16-9', '1-1'), align, width (see Options)

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\Embed; echo Embed::map('https://www.google.com/maps/embed?pb=!1m18!1m12'); // <div class="fegg-map"><iframe src="https://www.google.com/maps/embed?pb=!1m18!1m12" title="地図" loading="lazy" referrerpolicy="no-referrer-when-downgrade" allowfullscreen></iframe></div> echo Embed::map($pasted, array('ratio' => '16-9', 'align' => 'right', 'width' => 80)); // <div class="fegg-map is-16-9 alignright" style="width: 80%"><iframe ...></iframe></div>   Template {{ $page.data.map|feggMap|noescape }} {{ $page.data.map|feggMap:'16-9':'center':80|noescape }}

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public static string Embed::youtube( string $url, [ array $options = array() ] )   Returns the block the editor writes for a video, or '' when $url is not a YouTube URL. The template modifier feggYoutube calls this method.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$url	string URL of a YouTube video page $options	array	array()	ratio ('16-9', '9-16'), align, width (see Options)  A short (/shorts/) is '9-16' unless ratio is given.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\Embed; echo Embed::youtube('https://youtu.be/dQw4w9WgXcQ'); // <div data-youtube-video class="fegg-video"><iframe src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/dQw4w9WgXcQ" width="640" height="360" allowfullscreen></iframe></div> echo Embed::youtube('https://www.youtube.com/shorts/dQw4w9WgXcQ', array('align' => 'center', 'width' => 50)); // <div data-youtube-video class="fegg-video is-9-16 aligncenter" style="width: 50%"><iframe src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/dQw4w9WgXcQ" width="640" height="360" allowfullscreen></iframe></div>   Template {{ $page.data.youtube_url|feggYoutube|noescape }} {{ $page.data.youtube_url|feggYoutube:'9-16':'center':50|noescape }}

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public static ?string Embed::mapUrl( string $pasted )   $pasted is what Google Maps gives in "Share" > "Embed a map": the whole <iframe>, or only its URL. Returns the URL of the map (https://www.google.com/maps/embed?pb=...), or null when it is not a Google Maps embed (see Embed::isMapEmbed). &amp; in the URL becomes &.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$pasted	string The <iframe> of Google Maps, or its URL

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\Embed; echo Embed::mapUrl('<iframe src="https://www.google.com/maps/embed?pb=!1m18!1m12" width="600" height="450" style="border:0;" allowfullscreen="" loading="lazy"></iframe>'); // -> "https://www.google.com/maps/embed?pb=!1m18!1m12" var_dump(Embed::mapUrl('https://maps.google.com/?q=Tokyo')); // -> NULL

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public static ?string Embed::youtubeUrl( string $url )   Returns the player URL of a YouTube video or playlist (https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/<id>), or null when $url is not one of the YouTube URLs. A start time becomes ?start=<seconds>; other parameters are dropped. Nothing is asked of YouTube.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$url	string URL of a YouTube video page

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\Embed; echo Embed::youtubeUrl('https://youtu.be/dQw4w9WgXcQ?t=1m30s'); // -> "https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/dQw4w9WgXcQ?start=90" echo Embed::youtubeUrl('https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLabc123'); // -> "https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/videoseries?list=PLabc123" var_dump(Embed::youtubeUrl('https://example.com/')); // -> NULL

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public Feed Feed::add( array $item )   Adds a post and returns the feed, so calls can be chained. Posts are written in the order they are added: add the newest first.  Throws \InvalidArgumentException when the item has neither a title nor a link, or a date cannot be read.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$item	array See below

searchDocs.title: Item​
searchDocs.content: Key	Remarkstitle	Title of the post link	Path or URL of the post date	'Y-m-d H:i:s' from the database, a Unix time or a date object. Empty or '0000-00-00 00:00:00': no date content	HTML of the post, written in <content:encoded>. src="/…" and href="/…" get the domain description	Plain text. When missing, made from content (see What is written) category	A name, or a list of names guid	ID of the post. Default: the link (isPermaLink="true")

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\Feed; $feed->add(array( 'title' => $row['title'], 'link' => '/news/post_' . $row['news_id'] . '.html', 'date' => $row['post_date'], 'category' => array('お知らせ', 'イベント'), 'content' => $row['content'], ));

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public Feed::__construct( string $title, string $link [, string $description = '' [, string $feedUrl = '' ] ] )   Creates an empty feed. $link and $feedUrl become absolute URLs.  Throws \InvalidArgumentException when a path cannot be made an http(s) URL (outside a request).

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$title	string Name of the feed $link	string Path or URL of the page the feed belongs to ('/news/') $description	string	''	Description of the feed. '': the title $feedUrl	string	''	Path or URL of the feed itself ('/news/feed.xml'), written as atom:link. '': none

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\Feed; $siteName = $this->config['site_info']['name']; $feed = new Feed('ニュース | ' . $siteName, '/news/', $siteName . 'のニュース', '/news/feed.xml');   Give $feedUrl: feed validators expect the feed to name its own URL.

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public int Feed::count()   Returns the number of posts added.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\Feed; $feed = new Feed('News', '/news/'); foreach ($rows as $row) { $feed->add(array('title' => $row['title'], 'link' => '/news/post_' . $row['news_id'] . '.html')); } $feed->count(); // count($rows)

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public string Feed::toXml()   Returns the feed as XML text (see What is written). display() sends the same text.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\Feed; $feed = new Feed('News', '/news/', '', '/news/feed.xml'); $feed->add(array( 'title' => 'New shop', 'link' => '/news/post_12.html', 'date' => '2026-11-15 10:00:00', )); $xml = $feed->toXml();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public void Feed::display()   Sends the feed with Content-Type: application/rss+xml; charset=UTF-8 and ends the response (it throws Fegg\Http\Halt, like displayPage()). Code after it does not run.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\Feed; public function feed() { $feed = new Feed('News', '/news/', '', '/news/feed.xml'); foreach ($this->_model->order('post_date', 'desc')->limit(20)->all() as $row) { $feed->add(array( 'title' => $row['title'], 'link' => '/news/post_' . $row['news_id'] . '.html', 'date' => $row['post_date'], 'content' => $row['content'], )); } $feed->display(); }   Route the feed's URL to the action ($route['news/feed.xml'] = 'news/feed';) and link it from the <head> with <link rel="alternate" type="application/rss+xml"> (see How to use).

searchDocs.title: How to use​
searchDocs.content: The skeleton serves the latest news posts at /news/feed.xml with News::feed():  htdocs/_fegg/site/controller/News.php use Fegg\Tool\Feed; public function feed() { $siteName = $this->config['site_info']['name']; $feed = new Feed('ニュース | ' . $siteName, '/news/', $siteName . 'のニュース', '/news/feed.xml'); $rows = $this->_model ->order('post_date', 'desc') ->order('news_id', 'desc') ->limit(20) ->all(); foreach ($rows as $row) { $feed->add(array( 'title' => $row['title'], 'link' => '/news/post_' . $row['news_id'] . '.html', 'date' => $row['post_date'], 'category' => feggCategoryLabel($row['category'], 'news'), // Saved through HtmlSanitizer::clean(); the description is made from it 'content' => $row['content'], )); } $feed->display(); }   htdocs/_fegg/site/config/route.php $route['news/feed.xml'] = 'news/feed';   The model of the news controller is a public one (new Model(false, ...)), so hidden posts are left out. The siteframe tells browsers and feed readers where the feed is:  htdocs/_fegg/site/template/main/tpl/template/siteframe.tpl <link rel="alternate" type="application/rss+xml" title="{{ $site.name }}" href="{{ base_url }}/news/feed.xml">

searchDocs.title: What is written​
searchDocs.content: Output <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <rss version="2.0" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:content="http://purl.org/rss/1.0/modules/content/"> <channel> <title>ニュース | Example</title> <link>https://www.example.com/news/</link> <description>Exampleのニュース</description> <language>ja</language> <lastBuildDate>Sun, 15 Nov 2026 10:00:00 +0900</lastBuildDate> <atom:link href="https://www.example.com/news/feed.xml" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/> <item> <title>New shop</title> <link>https://www.example.com/news/post_12.html</link> <guid isPermaLink="true">https://www.example.com/news/post_12.html</guid> <pubDate>Sun, 15 Nov 2026 10:00:00 +0900</pubDate> <category>お知らせ</category> <description>We open a new shop in Osaka.</description> <content:encoded><![CDATA[<p>We open a <a href="https://www.example.com/shops/">new shop</a> in Osaka.</p>]]></content:encoded> </item> </channel> </rss>   Description from the content: without a description, the content's text is used: tags (and <script> / <style> with their content) removed, entities decoded, spaces joined, shortened to 240 columns (a full-width character counts 2) with ….Absolute URLs: paths (link, the feed's link and URL) become absolute with feggAbsoluteUrl() (see Absolute URLs). In the content, src="/…" and href="/…" get the scheme and host, since feed readers cannot resolve them. These paths already contain the base path (the editor writes them so), so only the domain is added.CDATA: the content is written in <content:encoded> as HTML inside a CDATA section; a ]]> in it is split between two sections. Other text is escaped.Control characters that XML does not allow are removed.lastBuildDate is the date of the newest post. The language is ja.  Pass content that is safe to show: CMS rich text saved through HtmlSanitizer::clean().

searchDocs.title: Errors​
searchDocs.content: An item without a title and without a link, a path when there is no request (in a command, FEGG_CURRENT_URL is not set: pass full URLs), or a date that cannot be read throws \InvalidArgumentException.

searchDocs.title: Methods​
searchDocs.content: 📄️Feed::__construct Create a feed 📄️Feed::add Add a post 📄️Feed::count Number of posts added 📄️Feed::toXml Return the RSS 2.0 XML 📄️Feed::display Send the feed and end the response

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public bool File::copyAll( string $fromDirectory, string $toDirectory )   Copies every file directly under $fromDirectory to $toDirectory with File::copyFile (permission 0644). Subdirectories and symbolic links are not copied, use File::copyDirectory for subdirectories.  Returns false when one of the directories does not exist or a file could not be copied.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$fromDirectory	string Source directory $toDirectory	string Destination directory (must exist)

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\File; $file = new File(); $file->copyAll('path/to/foo', 'path/to/bar');

searchDocs.title: How to use​
searchDocs.content: Import Fegg\Tool\File and create it with new.  Controller <?php namespace Site\Controller; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; use Fegg\Tool\File; class Export extends Controller { public function index() { $file = new File(); if (!$file->createDirectory(FEGG_SITE_DIR . '/data/export') || !$file->writeFile(FEGG_SITE_DIR . '/data/export/list.csv', "id,title\n", 'w')) { throw new \RuntimeException('The export could not be written'); } } }   note Every method returns true when it did its work and false when something could not be done (a missing source, a file that cannot be written, a directory that cannot be read ...). File::readFile returns the content instead, '' when the file cannot be read. Symbolic links are never followed when a directory is removed, copied or touched: a link is removed (or skipped), never what it points to.

searchDocs.title: Methods​
searchDocs.content: 📄️File::copyAll Copy all the files in a directory to another directory 📄️File::copyDirectory Copy the contents of a directory to another directory 📄️File::copyFile Copy a file 📄️File::createDirectory Create a directory 📄️File::moveFile Move (rename) a file 📄️File::output Send a file to the browser 📄️File::readFile Read a file and return its contents 📄️File::removeDirectory Remove a directory with all its contents 📄️File::removeExpiredFile Remove the files older than the specified minutes 📄️File::removeFile Remove files 📄️File::touchDirectory Change the modification time of the files in a directory 📄️File::writeFile Write data to a file

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public bool File::copyDirectory( string $fromDirectory, string $toDirectory, [ boolean $recursiveCallFlag = false ] )   Copies the files under $fromDirectory to $toDirectory. The destination directory must already exist. When $recursiveCallFlag is true, subdirectories are created in the destination and copied as well. Symbolic links are skipped.  Returns false when one of the directories does not exist or something could not be copied.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$fromDirectory	string Source directory $toDirectory	string Destination directory (must exist) $recursiveCallFlag	boolean	false	true: also copy subdirectories recursively

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\File; $file = new File(); // Only the files directly under path/to/foo $file->copyDirectory('path/to/foo', 'path/to/bar'); // Including subdirectories $file->copyDirectory('path/to/foo', 'path/to/bar', true);

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public bool File::copyFile( string $source, string $dest )   Copies $source to $dest and sets the permission of the copy to 0644 (readable by everyone). Returns false when $source is not a file or the copy fails.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$source	string Source file $dest	string Destination file

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\File; $file = new File(); $file->copyFile('path/to/foo.txt', 'path/to/bar.txt');

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public string File::readFile( string $fileName )   Returns the contents of $fileName, or an empty string when it is not a file or cannot be read. The whole file is read into memory: send a large file to the browser with File::output.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$fileName	string File to read

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\File; $file = new File(); $contents = $file->readFile('path/to/foo.txt');

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public bool File::createDirectory( string $directory, [ string|int $permission = '0755' ] )   Creates $directory and its missing parent directories with the permission $permission. Returns true when the directory exists afterwards (also when it existed already), false when it could not be created.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$directory	string Directory to create $permission	string/int	'0755'	Permission, '0755' or 0755

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\File; $file = new File(); $file->createDirectory('path/to/new_directory');

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public bool File::moveFile( string $from, string $to )   Moves $from to $to with rename(). Returns false when $from does not exist or it cannot be moved.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$from	string Source file $to	string Destination file

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\File; $file = new File(); $file->moveFile('path/to/foo.txt', 'path/to/bar.txt');

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public bool File::output( string $fileName )   Prints the contents of $fileName with readfile(), a piece at a time, so a file of any size can be sent (File::readFile reads it all into memory). Headers are not sent: send them before. Returns false when $fileName is not a file or cannot be read.  For files uploaded through the CMS, use Fegg\Http\Download, which also sends the headers.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$fileName	string File to send

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\File; $path = FEGG_SITE_DIR . '/data/export/list.csv'; header('Content-Type: text/csv; charset=UTF-8'); header('Content-Length: ' . filesize($path)); $file = new File(); $file->output($path);

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public bool File::removeDirectory( string $directory )   Deletes every file and subdirectory under $directory recursively, then removes $directory itself.  Symbolic links are never followed: a link inside the directory is removed as a link and what it points to is left alone. When $directory itself is a link, only the link is removed.  Returns false when $directory is not a directory or something could not be removed.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$directory	string Directory to remove

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\File; $file = new File(); $file->removeDirectory($this->config['upload_dir']['path'] . '/image/' . $id . '/');

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public bool File::removeExpiredFile( string $path, int $min )   Deletes the files directly under $path whose modification time is $min minutes ago or older. Subdirectories are not touched.  Returns true when every expired file was removed (also when there was none), false when $path is not a directory or a file could not be removed.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$path	string Target directory $min	int Age in minutes after which a file is deleted

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\File; $file = new File(); // Delete temporary files older than one day $file->removeExpiredFile('path/to/tmp', 60 * 24);

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public bool File::touchDirectory( string $directory, string $datetime )   Sets the modification time of every file and subdirectory under $directory (recursively) to $datetime, parsed with strtotime(). Symbolic links are skipped.  Returns false when $directory is not a directory, $datetime cannot be parsed or a time could not be changed.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$directory	string Target directory $datetime	string Date and time (any strtotime() format)

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\File; $file = new File(); $file->touchDirectory('path/to/foo', '2024-04-01 10:00:00');

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public bool File::removeFile( string $file )   Deletes the file $file. When there is no file of that exact name, $file is used as a glob() pattern (*, ?, [...]) and every matching file is deleted, so a file whose name contains [ or * is removed itself, not the files the pattern would match. Directories are not removed.  Returns false when a file could not be removed. A pattern that matches nothing returns true.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$file	string File path or glob() pattern

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\File; $file = new File(); $file->removeFile('path/to/foo.txt'); // Remove all the log files $file->removeFile('path/to/log/*.log');

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public bool File::writeFile( string $file, string $data, [ string $writeOption = 'a' ] )   Opens $file with the fopen() mode $writeOption, writes $data and sets the permission of the file to 0644 (readable by everyone). The default mode a appends to the file; use w to overwrite it.  Returns false when the file cannot be opened or written.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$file	string File to write $data	string Data to write $writeOption	string	'a'	fopen() mode (a: append, w: overwrite)

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\File; $file = new File(); // Append a line $file->writeFile('path/to/foo.log', date('Y-m-d H:i:s') . " done\n"); // Overwrite the file if (!$file->writeFile('path/to/foo.txt', 'New contents', 'w')) { // could not be written }

searchDocs.content: public Client::__construct( [ float $timeout = 10 [, float $connectTimeout = 3 [, ?string $transport = null ] ] ] )   The timeouts apply to every request made with this client.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$timeout	float	10	Seconds for the whole request $connectTimeout	float	3	Seconds to connect (cURL only; the stream wrapper has the whole $timeout) $transport	string|null	null	'curl' or 'stream'. null: cURL when the extension is installed, otherwise the stream wrapper. Set it only in tests

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Http\Client; $client = new Client(); // 10 seconds, 3 to connect $quick = new Client(3, 1); // while a visitor waits for the page

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public array Client::post( string $url, array|string $body [, array $headers = array() ] )   An array $body is sent as a form (application/x-www-form-urlencoded, the Content-Type is added). A string is sent as it is: add its Content-Type yourself, for JSON for example.  Returns array('status' => int, 'body' => string). A transport failure throws Fegg\Http\ClientException (see Errors).

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$url	string http:// or https:// URL $body	array|string Form fields, or the body as it is $headers	array	array()	Request headers, each as 'Name: value'

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Http\Client; $client = new Client(); // A form $response = $client->post('https://example.com/api/entries', array('name' => $name, 'mail' => $mail)); // JSON $response = $client->post( 'https://hooks.example.com/notify', json_encode(array('text' => 'New entry from ' . $name)), array('Content-Type: application/json') );

searchDocs.title: How to use​
searchDocs.content: Import Fegg\Http\Client, create it with new and call get(), post() or request(). Each returns an array:  Key	Data type	Remarksstatus	int	HTTP status (200, 404 ...) body	string	Response body  Controller <?php namespace Site\Controller; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; use Fegg\Http\Client; use Fegg\Http\ClientException; use Fegg\Log; class Items extends Controller { public function index() { $items = array(); try { $response = (new Client(5))->get('https://api.example.com/items?category=2', array('Accept: application/json')); if ($response['status'] === 200) { $items = json_decode($response['body'], true) ?: array(); } else { Log::warning('Items API answered {status}', array('status' => $response['status'])); } } catch (ClientException $e) { Log::warning('Items API not reachable: {message}', array('message' => $e->getMessage())); } $this->page['items'] = $items; $this->displayPage('items'); } }

searchDocs.title: Errors​
searchDocs.content: A response with an error status (404, 500 ...) is returned normally: check status.Only a transport failure (no connection, DNS, TLS, timeout) throws Fegg\Http\ClientException (a \RuntimeException). The message names the method, the URL and the cause.A URL that is not http or https throws \InvalidArgumentException before anything is sent.  The page should still work when the other service does not: catch ClientException, write it to the log and show the page without that part. Keep the timeout short for a call made while a visitor waits.

searchDocs.title: Methods​
searchDocs.content: 📄️Client::__construct Create a client with its timeouts 📄️Client::get Send a GET request 📄️Client::post Send a POST request 📄️Client::request Send a request with any method

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public array Client::get( string $url [, array $headers = array() ] )   Returns array('status' => int, 'body' => string). A response with an error status is returned normally; a transport failure throws Fegg\Http\ClientException (see Errors).

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$url	string http:// or https:// URL, with its query string $headers	array	array()	Request headers, each as 'Name: value'

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Http\Client; $query = http_build_query(array('category' => 2, 'q' => $this->in('q'))); $response = (new Client())->get('https://api.example.com/items?' . $query, array( 'Accept: application/json', 'Authorization: Bearer ' . feggEnv('ITEMS_API_TOKEN'), )); if ($response['status'] === 200) { $items = json_decode($response['body'], true); }   Keep tokens out of the code: read them with feggEnv() from env.php (see Settings).

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public array Client::request( string $method, string $url [, ?string $body = null [, array $headers = array() ] ] )   For methods other than GET and POST (PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD ...). The body is sent as it is.  Returns array('status' => int, 'body' => string). A transport failure throws Fegg\Http\ClientException; a URL that is not http or https throws \InvalidArgumentException (see Errors).

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$method	string HTTP method $url	string http:// or https:// URL $body	string|null	null	Body, sent as it is $headers	array	array()	Request headers, each as 'Name: value'

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Http\Client; $client = new Client(); $response = $client->request('PUT', 'https://api.example.com/items/42', json_encode($item), array( 'Content-Type: application/json', )); $response = $client->request('DELETE', 'https://api.example.com/items/42'); if ($response['status'] !== 204) { // ... }

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public static array JsonLd::article( array $data [, string $type = 'NewsArticle' ] )   Returns an article item. The keys below are converted; any other key is kept as it is. Empty values are left out.  Throws \InvalidArgumentException when a date cannot be read.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$data	array See below $type	string	'NewsArticle'	'NewsArticle', 'BlogPosting' or 'Article'

searchDocs.title: Data​
searchDocs.content: Key	Value	Written asheadline	The title	As it is datePublished	'Y-m-d H:i:s' from the database, a Unix time or a date object	ISO 8601 with the time zone dateModified	The same	ISO 8601 with the time zone image	A path or URL, or a list of them	A list of absolute URLs url	Path of the page	An absolute URL author	A name	{"@type": "Organization", "name": ...} (an array is kept as it is) publisher	A name	The same

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\JsonLd; JsonLd::article(array( 'headline' => $data['title'], 'datePublished' => $data['post_date'], 'dateModified' => $data['modified'], 'image' => $data['image_id'] ? FEGG_CURRENT_DOMAIN . getImageUrl($data['image_id']) : '', 'url' => '/blog/' . $data['blog_id'] . '/', 'author' => array('@type' => 'Person', 'name' => $data['writer']), 'publisher' => 'Example Inc.', ), 'BlogPosting');   getImageUrl() returns a path that already contains the base path, so only the domain is added (see Absolute URLs).

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public static array JsonLd::breadcrumb( array $items )   Returns a BreadcrumbList item. $items is name => path, from the top page to the current page; the positions are numbered from 1. Paths become absolute URLs. The current page can have '' as its path: it is then written without a URL.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$items	array array('Name' => '/path/', ...) in order

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\JsonLd; JsonLd::breadcrumb(array( 'ホーム' => '/', 'ニュース' => '/news/', $data['title'] => '', ));   Output { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "BreadcrumbList", "itemListElement": [ { "@type": "ListItem", "position": 1, "name": "ホーム", "item": "https://www.example.com/" }, { "@type": "ListItem", "position": 2, "name": "ニュース", "item": "https://www.example.com/news/" }, { "@type": "ListItem", "position": 3, "name": "New shop" } ] }   The names are array keys, so two items cannot have the same name. Write the same breadcrumbs as the page shows.

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public static array JsonLd::graph( array ...$items )   Returns array('@context' => 'https://schema.org', '@graph' => array(...)) with the items in their order. The @context of each item is removed (the graph has it once), and empty items are left out.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks...$items	array Results of the other methods, or arrays of your own with an @type

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: htdocs/_fegg/site/controller/Index.php use Fegg\Tool\JsonLd; $siteName = $this->config['site_info']['name']; $this->setSiteinfo('json_ld', JsonLd::graph( JsonLd::website($siteName, '/'), JsonLd::organization($siteName, '/') ));   An item of your own is a schema.org type as an array:  Controller $this->setSiteinfo('json_ld', JsonLd::graph( JsonLd::breadcrumb(array('ホーム' => '/', '店舗' => '/shops/', $shop['name'] => '')), array( '@type' => 'Store', 'name' => $shop['name'], 'telephone' => $shop['tel'], 'url' => feggAbsoluteUrl('/shops/' . $shop['shop_id'] . '/'), ) ));   Arrays of your own are written as they are: make URLs absolute with feggAbsoluteUrl() yourself.

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public static array JsonLd::website( string $name [, string $url = '/' ] )   Returns a WebSite item: the name search engines show for the site. Set it on the top page. $url becomes an absolute URL.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$name	string Name of the site $url	string	'/'	Path or URL of the top page

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\JsonLd; JsonLd::website('Example Inc.');   Output { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "WebSite", "name": "Example Inc.", "url": "https://www.example.com/" }

searchDocs.title: How to use​
searchDocs.content: The methods are static. A controller sets the data as the site information json_ld with setSiteinfo, usually several items in one graph():  htdocs/_fegg/site/controller/News.php use Fegg\Tool\JsonLd; public function detail($id = '') { // ... $this->page['data'] is the post $data = $this->page['data']; $siteName = $this->config['site_info']['name']; $this->setSiteinfo('json_ld', JsonLd::graph( JsonLd::article(array( 'headline' => $data['title'], 'datePublished' => $data['post_date'], 'dateModified' => $data['modified'], // getImageUrl() includes the base path: only the domain is added 'image' => $data['image_id'] ? FEGG_CURRENT_DOMAIN . getImageUrl($data['image_id']) : '', 'url' => '/news/post_' . $data['news_id'] . '.html', 'author' => $siteName, 'publisher' => $siteName, )), JsonLd::breadcrumb(array( 'ホーム' => '/', 'ニュース' => '/news/', $data['title'] => '', )) )); $this->displayPage('news/detail'); }   The skeleton's siteframe writes it in the <head> of every page that sets it:  htdocs/_fegg/site/template/main/tpl/template/siteframe.tpl {{ if $site.json_ld }} <script type="application/ld+json">{{ $site.json_ld|feggJs|noescape }}</script> {{ end }}   feggJs writes the array as JSON and encodes <, > and &, so a title containing </script> cannot end the element. Use exactly this line: noescape is required inside <script>, and the normal escaping would break the JSON.  In the skeleton, the top page (Index.php) sets the site and its organization, and the news detail page sets the article and its breadcrumbs.

searchDocs.title: The data​
searchDocs.content: Empty values (null, '', array()) are left out, so optional fields can be passed as they come from the database.Paths (url, item, image, logo) become absolute URLs with feggAbsoluteUrl(): a path of the site without the base path (see Absolute URLs).Dates ('Y-m-d H:i:s' from the database, a Unix time or a date object) are written in ISO 8601 with the time zone: 2026-11-15T10:00:00+09:00.  Output (the article above, shortened) { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@graph": [ { "@type": "NewsArticle", "headline": "New shop", "datePublished": "2026-11-15T10:00:00+09:00", "url": "https://www.example.com/news/post_12.html", "author": { "@type": "Organization", "name": "Example Inc." }, "publisher": { "@type": "Organization", "name": "Example Inc." } }, { "@type": "BreadcrumbList", "itemListElement": [ { "@type": "ListItem", "position": 1, "name": "ホーム", "item": "https://www.example.com/" }, { "@type": "ListItem", "position": 2, "name": "ニュース", "item": "https://www.example.com/news/" }, { "@type": "ListItem", "position": 3, "name": "New shop" } ] } ] }   Check a page with Google's Rich Results Test after changing its data.

searchDocs.title: How to use​
searchDocs.content: The methods are static: import Fegg\Log and call the method of the level.  Controller use Fegg\Log; Log::info('Import finished', array('rows' => $count)); Log::warning('Unknown category {id}', array('id' => $id)); try { $mail->send($to); } catch (\Exception $e) { Log::error('Mail not sent to {to}', array('to' => $to, 'exception' => $e)); }   site/data/log/fegg-2026-11-14.log [2026-11-14 13:44:54 +09:00] INFO Import finished {"rows":120} | POST /cms/import/ 203.0.113.5 [2026-11-14 13:44:54 +09:00] WARNING Unknown category 7 {"id":7} | GET /news/?category=7 198.51.100.20 [2026-11-14 13:44:54 +09:00] ERROR Mail not sent to info@example.com {"to":"info@example.com","exception":"RuntimeException: SMTP connect() failed at /path/Contact.php:88"} | POST /contact/post/ 203.0.113.5   Each line is: the date and time, the level, the message, the context as JSON, and for web requests the method, the URL and the visitor's address.  {key} in the message is replaced with $context['key'] (text, numbers, true / false and objects with __toString()).The whole context is added as JSON. An exception (\Throwable) is written as its class, message, file and line; another object as its class name.Line breaks in the message become spaces, so one entry is always one line.Never log passwords, tokens or full personal data.

searchDocs.title: Levels​
searchDocs.content: The levels are those of PSR-3, from lowest to highest:  Level	Use fordebug	Details while developing info	Something worth knowing happened (an import finished) notice	Normal but significant warning	Something unexpected that the page could handle (another service did not answer) error	Something failed (a mail was not sent, a save failed) critical	A part of the site does not work alert	Someone must act now emergency	The site is unusable  Entries below $settings['log_level'] are not written (see Settings).

searchDocs.title: Settings​
searchDocs.content: Setting	Default	Remarks$settings['log_level']	''	Lowest level written. '': warning in production, debug elsewhere $settings['log_retention_days']	30	Files older than this are removed (checked once a day). 0: keep all FEGG_LOG_DIR (env.php or environment variable)	site/data/log	Directory of the log files (created when missing)  htdocs/_fegg/site/config/settings.php $settings['log_level'] = 'info'; $settings['log_retention_days'] = 90;   site/data/ is not tracked by git and is denied to the web by htdocs/_fegg/.htaccess. When the directory or the file cannot be written, the entry goes to the PHP error log instead.

searchDocs.title: Methods​
searchDocs.content: 📄️Log::error and the other levels Write an entry at a level 📄️Log::log Write an entry at a level given as text 📄️Log::logger / Log::setLogger The logger in use, and replacing it in tests

Returns true when the entry was written, false when it is below $settings['log_level'] or could not be written (it then goes to the PHP error log).

searchDocs.content: public static Fegg\Log\FileLogger Log::logger() public static void Log::setLogger( ?Fegg\Log\FileLogger $logger )   logger() returns the Fegg\Log\FileLogger that writes the entries. It is created on first use from the settings; its file() method returns the path of today's file.  setLogger() replaces it, for tests that read what was logged. null makes the next entry create it from the settings again.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$logger	Fegg\Log\FileLogger|null new FileLogger($directory, $lowestLevel = 'debug', $retentionDays = 30), or null

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Test use Fegg\Log; use Fegg\Log\FileLogger; $dir = sys_get_temp_dir() . '/fegg-log-test'; Log::setLogger(new FileLogger($dir, 'debug', 0)); $this->importer->run($file); $this->assertStringContainsString('ERROR Import failed', file_get_contents(Log::logger()->file())); Log::setLogger(null);

searchDocs.title: How to use​
searchDocs.content: Import Fegg\Tool\Mail and create it with new. A failed send throws PHPMailer\PHPMailer\Exception, so wrap the sending in try / catch.  Controller <?php namespace Site\Controller; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; use Fegg\Tool\Mail; use PHPMailer\PHPMailer\Exception; class Contact extends Controller { public function post() { $body = $this->fetchPage('/contact/mail/to_admin'); try { $mail = new Mail('Mail subject', $body); $mail->send('admin@example.com', 'Sender name', 'from@example.com'); } catch (Exception $e) { // Failed to send: $e->getMessage() } } }   The contact form of the skeleton (htdocs/_fegg/site/controller/Contact.php) is a complete example, including Mail::setDebugFlag to write the emails to a log file instead of sending them.

searchDocs.title: Sender​
searchDocs.content: When Mail::send is given no sender address, it uses from and from_name of $settings['mail'] in site/config/settings.php. When there is no sender address in either place, send() throws an \InvalidArgumentException.  htdocs/_fegg/site/config/settings.php $settings['mail'] = array('transport' => 'sendmail', 'from' => 'info@example.com', 'from_name' => 'Example Inc.');   Controller $mail = new Mail('Mail subject', $body); $mail->send('admin@example.com'); // From: Example Inc. <info@example.com>

searchDocs.title: SMTP​
searchDocs.content: To send through an SMTP server instead of sendmail, set $settings['mail'] in site/config/settings.php, and put the password in site/config/env.php (or an environment variable) as FEGG_SMTP_PASSWORD. Every Mail object then uses it, the contact form included.  htdocs/_fegg/site/config/settings.php $settings['mail'] = array( 'transport' => 'smtp', 'host' => 'smtp.example.com', 'port' => 587, 'encryption' => 'tls', 'username' => 'user@example.com', );   htdocs/_fegg/site/config/env.php 'FEGG_SMTP_PASSWORD' => '...',   Key	Default	Remarkstransport	'sendmail'	'smtp' to use SMTP host	'localhost'	SMTP server. FEGG_SMTP_HOST in env.php overrides it port	587	Port encryption	'tls'	'tls': STARTTLS. 'ssl': SMTPS (usually port 465). '': none username	''	Login user; without it no authentication is used. FEGG_SMTP_USERNAME in env.php overrides it from	''	Sender address when send() is given none (see Sender) from_name	''	Sender name used with from  The connection times out after 10 seconds. Never write the password in settings.php, which is committed.  note The PHPMailer instance is available as $mail->_mailer when you need a setting this wrapper does not cover.

'/data/log/contact_admin.log'); // another file // Written to the log file instead of being sent $mail->send('mail@example.com', 'John Doe', 'from@example.com');

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public boolean Mail::send( mixed $to, [ string $from_name = null, string $from_ad = null ] )   Sends the email with its attachments and returns true on success. A failed send (including an invalid address) throws PHPMailer\PHPMailer\Exception.  No sender ($from_ad null or ''): $settings['mail'] (see Sender); none there throws \InvalidArgumentException.  When the debug flag is enabled with Mail::setDebugFlag, the email is not sent: the whole message is written to the log file with Mail::log instead.  note Each call sends only to the addresses given to it, so one Mail object can send the same message to several people in turn. To send one email to several recipients, pass them as an array.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$to	mixed Recipient address, or an array of addresses $from_name	string	null	Sender name (none: $settings['mail']['from_name'] when $from_ad is not given either) $from_ad	string	null	Sender address, also used as the envelope sender (none: $settings['mail']['from'])

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\Mail; use PHPMailer\PHPMailer\Exception; try { $mail = new Mail('Mail subject', 'Mail body'); $mail->send('mail@example.com', 'John Doe', 'from@example.com'); // Several recipients $mail = new Mail('Mail subject', 'Mail body'); $mail->send(array('foo@example.com', 'bar@example.com'), 'John Doe', 'from@example.com'); // The sender of $settings['mail'] $mail = new Mail('Mail subject', 'Mail body'); $mail->send('mail@example.com'); } catch (Exception $e) { // Failed to send: $e->getMessage() }

searchDocs.content: public self Model::addBindParam( string $column, string $type )   The value of the column is cast to the type before it is written by insertRow, insertRows, updateRow, updateRowsWhere, insert, update and updateWhere. null values are not cast. Reads are not affected.  Throws InvalidArgumentException for an unknown type.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$column	string Column name $type	string Bind type (case-insensitive)

searchDocs.title: Types​
searchDocs.content: Type	CastINTEGER	(int) FLOAT	(float) DATE	Y-m-d. A number is read as a Unix timestamp, anything else with strtotime() DATETIME	Y-m-d H:i:s. A number is read as a Unix timestamp, anything else with strtotime()  A DATE / DATETIME string that strtotime() cannot read is stored as 1970-01-01; validate dates before writing them.

searchDocs.content: public int Model::count()   Returns the number of matching rows. With group or having, it returns the number of groups. order and limit are ignored.
