searchDocs.title: How to use​
searchDocs.content: Controller <?php namespace Site\Controller; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; use Fegg\Model; class News extends Controller { public function __init() { parent::__init(); $this->_model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); } public function index() { $this->page['data'] = $this->_model ->where('category = ?', 2) ->order('post_date', 'desc') ->listMax(20) ->current($this->in('p')) ->find(); $this->page['pager'] = $this->_model->getPager(); $this->displayPage('news'); } }

searchDocs.title: Tables​
searchDocs.content: Tables are defined in YAML: htdocs/_fegg/site/config/database/*.yaml (project) and htdocs/_fegg/core/config/database/*.yaml (CMS core tables). ./fegg-cli migration applies them to the database.  Use ./fegg-cli db:schema to see the tables and columns (./fegg-cli db:schema cms_news for one table, --json for JSON). It reads the YAML files, so no database is needed, and it warns about tables that lack the columns below.

searchDocs.title: Required columns​
searchDocs.content: Every table used with Fegg\Model needs these columns. The model fills them by itself (see core/config/database_regular_use_query.php):  Column	Type	Set byvalid	BOOLEAN	1 on insert, 0 by delete. Reads only return rows with valid = 1 created	DATETIME	insert modified	DATETIME	insert and update

searchDocs.title: Creating a model​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', // table name 'id' => 'news_id', // primary key 'visible' => 'visible', // optional: public flag column 'bind' => array('category' => 'INTEGER', 'post_date' => 'DATETIME'), // casts on write ));   The first argument is $is_admin. With false, reads only return rows whose visible column is 1 (public pages). The CMS uses true to see unpublished rows. See Model::__construct.bind types are INTEGER, FLOAT, DATE and DATETIME (case-insensitive). Any other type throws InvalidArgumentException. See Model::addBindParam.Table and column names (table, id, visible, and the names given to order(), join(), whereIn() and the other helpers) must be plain identifiers: letters, digits and _, optionally table.column (news_id, cms_news.post_date). Anything else throws InvalidArgumentException. Never build names from user input.

searchDocs.title: Reading​
searchDocs.content: Controller $rows = $model ->where('category = ?', 2) ->whereLike('title', 'news') // contains; % and _ match literally ->whereIn('news_id', array(1, 2, 3)) ->order('post_date', 'desc') ->listMax(20)->current($this->in('p')) // page size and page number ->find(); // array of rows (associative arrays) $pager = $model->getPager(); // current_page, last_page, number_of_records ... $rows = $model->order('post_date', 'desc')->limit(5)->all(); // no paging $row = $model->id($id); // one row by primary key, or null $row = $model->where('title = ?', $title)->one(); // first match, or null $title = $model->where('news_id = ?', $id)->value('title'); // one value, or null $ids = $model->where('category = ?', 2)->column('news_id'); // array(3, 5, ...) $count = $model->where('category = ?', 2)->count(); // int $found = $model->where('title = ?', $title)->exists(); // bool   Method	Returnsfind	One page of rows; getPager has the links all	Every matching row (limit caps it) one / id	The first row, or null value	The first column of the first row, or null column	One column of every row, optionally keyed by another column count	Number of rows (of groups, with group()) exists	true when a row matches toSql	The SELECT all() would run, with the values filled in; runs nothing

searchDocs.title: find() or all()​
searchDocs.content: find() pages: set the page size with listMax and the page with current, then read the links with getPager(). all() does not page; limit caps it. Do not use listMax(9999) to get everything, and do not combine limit() with find() (it throws LogicException).

searchDocs.title: Conditions are reset after every query​
searchDocs.content: where(), order(), select(), limit() and the other chain methods only apply to the next query. After every query (find(), all(), one(), count(), insertRow() ...), failed ones included, the model forgets them, so each query starts clean. Model::reset does the same by hand.  The write methods (updateRowsWhere, deleteWhere ...) take their condition as arguments. Conditions chained with where() are not used by them (and are cleared).

searchDocs.title: Writing​
searchDocs.content: Controller $id = $model->insertRow(array('title' => $title, 'category' => 2, 'content' => null)); $n = $model->updateRow(array('title' => $title), $id); // rows updated $n = $model->updateRowsWhere(array('visible' => 0), 'category = ?', 3); $ids = $model->insertRows(array($row1, $row2)); // one transaction: all rows or none $n = $model->delete($id); // soft delete: valid = 0 $n = $model->erase($id); // removes the row   insertRow, updateRow and updateRowsWhere write only the given keys; null is stored as NULL. Do not pass created, modified or valid unless you mean to override them.Update and delete methods return the number of affected rows.delete and deleteWhere are soft deletes (valid = 0; reads no longer see the row). erase and eraseWhere remove the row.updateWhere(), deleteWhere(), eraseWhere() and updateRowsWhere() refuse an empty condition. Pass '1 = 1' to really affect every row.insert and update write '' for every listed column missing from the data and cannot store NULL: prefer insertRow() and updateRow().transaction runs several writes, of any number of models, all or nothing.

searchDocs.title: Errors​
searchDocs.content: A failed query or connection throws Fegg\Database\QueryException (see Database). Catch it only when the page can do something useful, for example with a duplicate key:  Controller try { $model->insertRow($row); } catch (\Fegg\Database\QueryException $e) { // ... }   Wrong use of the builder (an array bound to <, an invalid column name, an update without a condition) throws InvalidArgumentException with a message saying what to do instead.

searchDocs.title: Debugging​
searchDocs.content: toSql returns the SELECT a chain would run, without running it. debug prints the last query. Both fill in the values for reading.  Controller echo $model->where('category = ?', 2)->order('post_date', 'desc')->toSql(); // Select * From "cms_news" Where category = 2 AND cms_news.visible = '1' And "cms_news".valid = 1 Order By post_date DESC

searchDocs.title: Raw SQL​
searchDocs.content: For what the model cannot express, use Fegg\Database\Pdo directly. It shares the connection (and an open transaction) with the models. Raw queries get no automatic valid / created / modified handling.

searchDocs.content: public self Model::current( [ int $current = 1 ] )   Sets the page that find returns. A value that is not a number, under 1 or over the last page gives page 1, so the request parameter can be passed as it is.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$current	int	1	Current page number

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); // Page 2 of 5 rows (rows 6 to 10) $records = $model->listMax(5)->current(2)->find(); // Page from the URL (?p=3) $records = $model->listMax(5)->current($this->in('p'))->find();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public Model::__construct( [ boolean $is_admin = false, array $options = [] ] )   Throws InvalidArgumentException when table, id or visible is not a plain name, or when a bind type is unknown.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$is_admin	boolean	false	false: reads only return rows whose visible column is 1 (public pages). true: every row (CMS) $options	array	[]	Model options (below)

searchDocs.title: Options​
searchDocs.content: Key	Data type	Remarkstable	string	Table name. Same as setTableName id	string	Primary key column. Same as setPrimary visible	string	Public flag column (optional). Same as setVisible bind	array	Column types cast on write (column => type). Same as setBindParam  table, id and visible must be plain names: letters, digits and _, optionally table.column. Other keys are ignored.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Model; // For public pages (rows whose visible column is 0 are not returned) $model = new Model(false, array( // Operate on the `cms_news` table 'table' => 'cms_news', // Primary key is `news_id` 'id' => 'news_id', // Public flag is `visible` 'visible' => 'visible', // Cast these columns on insert and update 'bind' => array( 'category' => 'INTEGER', 'image_id' => 'INTEGER', 'file_id' => 'INTEGER', 'post_date' => 'DATETIME', ), )); // For CMS pages (every row, visible or not) $admin = new Model(true, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', ));

searchDocs.content: public void Model::create( array $fields )   Creates the model's table. Tables are normally defined in site/config/database/*.yaml and created with ./fegg-cli migration; use this only for tables made at run time. Throws Fegg\Database\QueryException when the query fails.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$fields	array List of column definitions (below)

searchDocs.title: Column definition​
searchDocs.content: Every key must be present.  Key	Data type	Remarksname	string	Column name type	string	Column type notnull	boolean	Add NOT NULL dflt_value	mixed	Default value (null, '' or 0: no default) pk	boolean	Add PRIMARY KEY ai	boolean	Add AUTOINCREMENT

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(true, array( 'table' => 'sample', )); // Create Table "sample" (sample_id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, title TEXT DEFAULT 'none', valid BOOLEAN, created DATETIME, modified DATETIME) $model->create(array( array('name' => 'sample_id', 'type' => 'INTEGER', 'notnull' => true, 'dflt_value' => null, 'pk' => true, 'ai' => true), array('name' => 'title', 'type' => 'TEXT', 'notnull' => false, 'dflt_value' => 'none', 'pk' => false, 'ai' => false), array('name' => 'valid', 'type' => 'BOOLEAN', 'notnull' => false, 'dflt_value' => null, 'pk' => false, 'ai' => false), array('name' => 'created', 'type' => 'DATETIME', 'notnull' => false, 'dflt_value' => null, 'pk' => false, 'ai' => false), array('name' => 'modified', 'type' => 'DATETIME', 'notnull' => false, 'dflt_value' => null, 'pk' => false, 'ai' => false), ));

searchDocs.content: public void Model::debug()   Prints (echo) the last query of this model with its values filled in. The values are quoted for reading only: never run the result. To see a SELECT without running it, use toSql.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); $model->where('category = ?', 1) ->listMax(5) ->current(2) ->find(); $model->debug(); // -> Select * From "cms_news" Where category = 1 AND cms_news.visible = '1' And "cms_news".valid = 1 Limit 5, 5

searchDocs.content: public int Model::delete( mixed $id )   Soft-deletes the row whose primary key is $id: sets valid = 0 (and modified), so reads no longer return it. Returns the number of updated rows. To remove the row from the table, use erase.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$id	mixed Deleting target Primary ID

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(true, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); $deleted = $model->delete(1); // -> 1

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public int Model::deleteWhere( string $where, mixed $data )   Soft-deletes every row matching $where (sets valid = 0) and returns the number of updated rows. $data is one value, or an array with one value per placeholder.  The condition is required: an empty $where throws InvalidArgumentException. Pass '1 = 1' to really delete every row.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$where	string Condition with ? placeholders $data	mixed Values for the placeholders

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(true, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); $deleted = $model->deleteWhere('category = ?', 1); // Every row $deleted = $model->deleteWhere('1 = 1', array());

searchDocs.content: public self Model::disabledRegularUseQuery()   Skips every automatic query (for every table and for this table, see Configuration) for every later query of this model instance: reads also return rows with valid = 0, and inserts and updates no longer fill created, modified and valid. To skip them for one query only, use unsetRegularUseQuery.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller // A table without valid / created / modified columns $model = new Model(true, array( 'table' => 'sample_log', 'id' => 'log_id', )); $model->disabledRegularUseQuery(); $records = $model->all(); $model->insertRow(array('message' => 'Hello'));

The condition is required: an empty $where throws InvalidArgumentException. Pass '1 = 1' to really delete every row.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​

searchDocs.content: public array Model::find( [ array $options = [] ] )   Returns one page of matching rows (an array of associative arrays; an empty array when nothing matches). The page size is set with listMax (default 10) and the page with current. find() counts the matching rows first, so getPager can return the page links afterwards.  To get every row without paging, use all. find() throws LogicException when limit was set.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$options	array	[]	Overrides select, list_max and current

searchDocs.title: Options​
searchDocs.content: Key	Remarksselect	Same as select list_max	Same as listMax current	Same as current  Any other key throws an Exception.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); $this->page['data'] = $model ->where('category = ?', 2) ->order('post_date', 'desc') ->listMax(20) ->current($this->in('p')) ->find(); $this->page['pager'] = $model->getPager(); // Same as listMax(20)->current($this->in('p')) $records = $model->find(array('list_max' => 20, 'current' => $this->in('p')));

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public array Model::getPager()   Returns the page links of the latest find on this model (an empty array before the first find()). Each find() replaces them.  Key	Remarkscurrent_page	Page returned by find() page_min	First page number to show (up to 4 before the current) page_max	Last page number to show (up to 4 after the current) previous_page	Previous page. Only set when there is one next_page	Next page. Only set when there is one last_page	Number of pages number_of_records	Number of matching rows

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); // 23 rows, 5 per page, page 2 $records = $model->listMax(5)->current(2)->find(); $pager = $model->getPager(); print_r($pager);   Output Array ( [current_page] => 2 [page_min] => 1 [page_max] => 5 [previous_page] => 1 [next_page] => 3 [last_page] => 5 [number_of_records] => 23 )

searchDocs.content: public self Model::group( string $group )   Adds GROUP BY. Several calls are joined with commas. The text is written into the SQL as it is: never put user input in it. With group(), count counts the groups.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$group	string Group column(s)

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); // Select category, count(*) AS n // From "cms_news" // Where ... // Group By category $records = $model->select('category, count(*) AS n')->group('category')->all(); // Number of categories that have news $categories = $model->group('category')->count();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Model::havingClose()   Closes the bracket opened with havingOpen.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); $model->select('category, count(*) AS n, max(post_date) AS latest')->group('category'); $model->having('n > ?', 5); $model->havingOpen(); $model->having('category = ?', 1); $model->having('latest >= ?', '2026-01-01', 'OR'); $model->havingClose(); // ... Group By category // Having n > 5 AND (category = 1 OR latest >= '2026-01-01') $records = $model->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Model::having( string $query, [ mixed $data = [], string $andOr = 'AND' ] )   Adds a HAVING condition, used with group. $data works as in where: one value, or an array of values in placeholder order. With having(), count counts the groups that match.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$query	string Condition with ? placeholders (never put user input in it) $data	mixed	[]	One value, or an array of values in placeholder order $andOr	string	'AND'	How it joins the previous condition: AND or OR

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); // Categories with more than 5 news // Select category, count(*) AS n From "cms_news" Where ... Group By category Having n > 5 $records = $model ->select('category, count(*) AS n') ->group('category') ->having('n > ?', 5) ->all();

searchDocs.title: Complex HAVING query​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); $model->select('category, count(*) AS n, max(post_date) AS latest')->group('category'); $model->having('n > ?', 5); $model->havingOpen(); $model->having('category = ?', 1); $model->having('latest >= ?', '2026-01-01', 'OR'); $model->havingClose(); // ... Group By category // Having n > 5 AND (category = 1 OR latest >= '2026-01-01') $records = $model->all();

searchDocs.content: public array|null Model::id( mixed $id )   Returns the row whose primary key (see setPrimary) is $id, or null when there is none. A public model ($is_admin = false) also returns null for a row that is not visible, and deleted rows (valid = 0) are never returned. Conditions chained before it with where also apply.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$id	mixed Target primary ID

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); $record = $model->id($this->in('id')); if ($record === null) { // 404 }

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public int Model::increment( string $column, mixed $id, [ int|float $by = 1 ] )   Adds $by to $column of the row whose primary key is $id, in the UPDATE itself ("column" = "column" + ?), and returns the number of updated rows. Simultaneous requests do not lose counts, as they would when reading, adding and writing back.  Like every update, it also sets modified. Call unsetRegularUseQuery first to leave modified alone (for example for a view counter).  Throws InvalidArgumentException when $column is not a plain name or $by is not a number.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$column	string Numeric column $id	mixed Target primary ID $by	int/float	1	Amount to add; negative to subtract

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller // The table has a view_count INTEGER column $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); // Update "cms_news" Set "view_count" = "view_count" + 1 Where news_id = 24 $model->unsetRegularUseQuery()->increment('view_count', 24); // Subtract 2 (modified is updated) $model->increment('view_count', 24, -2);

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public int|string Model::insertRow( array $row )   Inserts one row from column => value pairs and returns the new ID (an int for integer keys).  Only the given columns are written; null is stored as NULL.created, modified and valid are filled automatically. Give them only to override them.bind types are applied.Throws InvalidArgumentException for an empty array, a column name that is not a plain name, or a value that is an array or an object. A failed insert (for example a duplicate key) throws Fegg\Database\QueryException.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$row	array Values (column => value)

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(true, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); $id = $model->insertRow(array( 'title' => $this->in('title'), 'category' => 2, 'post_date' => '2026-01-15 10:00:00', 'image_id' => null, )); // -> 24

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public string Model::insert( string $item, array $data )   Inserts one row and returns the new ID as a string. For new code, use insertRow: insert() writes '' for every column listed in $item that is missing from $data, and cannot store NULL.  $data is an associative array (values matched to $item by name) or a list (values in the order of $item). created, modified and valid are filled automatically and bind types are applied.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$item	string Columns, separated by commas $data	array Values

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(true, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); $item = 'title, content'; $data = array( 'title' => 'Sample title', 'content' => 'Sample content', ); // Returns the new ID $insertedId = $model->insert($item, $data); // -> '24'

searchDocs.content: public self Model::join( string|array $table, [ string $type = 'INNER', string $on = null, mixed $data = [] ] )   Joins another table. $table is a table name, or array('table', 'alias'); both must be plain names, or InvalidArgumentException is thrown. $on takes ? placeholders and $data works as in where.  The automatic valid = 1 and visible conditions only apply to the model's own table. Add them to $on for the joined table when you need them.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$table	string/array Table name, or array('table', 'alias') $type	string	'INNER'	'INNER', 'LEFT' or 'RIGHT' (anything else: INNER) $on	string	null	ON condition with ? placeholders $data	mixed	[]	Values for the ON placeholders

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); // Select cms_news.*, f.org_name // From "cms_news" // LEFT JOIN "cms_file" AS "f" ON f.file_id = cms_news.file_id AND f.valid = 1 // Where ... $records = $model ->select('cms_news.*, f.org_name') ->join(array('cms_file', 'f'), 'LEFT', 'f.file_id = cms_news.file_id AND f.valid = ?', 1) ->find();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public array Model::insertRows( array $rows )   Inserts each row with insertRow inside one transaction and returns the new IDs in order. When one row fails, none is inserted and the exception is rethrown. Throws InvalidArgumentException when an element of $rows is not an array.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$rows	array List of rows (column => value arrays)

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(true, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); $ids = $model->insertRows(array( array('title' => 'First', 'category' => 1), array('title' => 'Second', 'category' => 2), )); // -> array(25, 26)

searchDocs.content: public self Model::limit( int $count, [ int $offset = 0 ] )   Adds LIMIT to all, column and toSql; one, value and exists use the offset. count ignores it. find pages with listMax and current instead and throws LogicException when limit() was set.  Throws InvalidArgumentException when $count is under 1 or $offset under 0.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$count	int Maximum number of rows $offset	int	0	Number of rows to skip

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); // The 5 newest $records = $model->order('post_date', 'desc')->limit(5)->all(); // The next 5 (rows 6 to 10) $records = $model->order('post_date', 'desc')->limit(5, 5)->all();

searchDocs.content: public self Model::listMax( [ int $listMax = 10 ] )   Sets the number of rows per page of find. Without it, find() returns 10 rows. A value under 1 is treated as 1. Only find() uses it: use limit with all instead of a large listMax() to get every row.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$listMax	int	10	Rows per page

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); // First page, 5 rows $records = $model->listMax(5)->find();

searchDocs.content: public array|null Model::one( [ array $options = [] ] )   Returns the first matching row as an associative array, or null when nothing matches. order decides which row is first; the offset of limit is used.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$options	array	[]	array('select' => ...) overrides select

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); // The newest news, or null $latest = $model->order('post_date', 'desc')->one(); $record = $model->where('title = ?', $title)->one(); if ($record === null) { // not found }

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Model::order( string $order, [ string $duration = 'ASC' ] )   Adds a column to ORDER BY. Call it again for a second sort key.  $order must be a column name (post_date or cms_news.post_date); anything else, such as 'post_date desc' or an expression, throws InvalidArgumentException. Use orderRaw for expressions.$duration is DESC (case-insensitive) or anything else for ASC, so it is safe to pass a sort direction from the request.order('random') sorts in random order (ORDER BY RANDOM(), an SQLite function).

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$order	string Column name, or 'random' $duration	string	'ASC'	'ASC' or 'DESC'

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); // ... Order By post_date DESC,news_id DESC $records = $model->order('post_date', 'desc')->order('news_id', 'desc')->find(); // 3 random news $records = $model->order('random')->limit(3)->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Model::orderRaw( string $expression )   Adds an ORDER BY expression as it is. Use it for what order does not accept: CASE, functions, several keys in one string. The expression is written into the SQL unchanged: never put user input in it.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$expression	string ORDER BY expression

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); // Category 1 first, then the newest // ... Order By CASE WHEN category = 1 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, post_date DESC $records = $model->orderRaw('CASE WHEN category = 1 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, post_date DESC')->find();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Model::reset()   Forgets the conditions set with the chain methods: where, having, order, join, group, select, listMax, current and limit. The model does this by itself after every query, failed ones included, so call it only to drop a chain you built but did not run. The table, primary key, visible flag, bind types and the pager are kept.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(true, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', )); $model->where('category = ?', 1)->order('post_date', 'desc'); // Changed our mind: start again $model->reset(); // Select * From "cms_news" Where 1 = 1 And "cms_news".valid = 1 $records = $model->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public array Model::pragma( string $mode )   Runs an SQLite PRAGMA on the model's table and returns its rows. SQLite only.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$mode	string Pragma mode

searchDocs.title: Pragma mode​
searchDocs.content: Mode	Querytable	PRAGMA table_info("table") (also any unknown mode) index_list	PRAGMA index_list("table") index	PRAGMA index_info("table")

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(true, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', )); // PRAGMA table_info("cms_news") $columns = $model->pragma('table'); print_r($columns[0]);   Output Array ( [cid] => 0 [name] => news_id [type] => INTEGER [notnull] => 1 [dflt_value] => [pk] => 1 )

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Model::select( string $select )   Sets the columns of the next SELECT (default *). The text is written into the SQL as it is: never put user input in it. Like every chain method, it is reset after the query.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$select	string Columns or expressions, separated by commas

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); // Get the `news_id` and `title` columns $records = $model->select('news_id, title')->find(); // Expressions work too $records = $model->select('category, count(*) AS n')->group('category')->all();

searchDocs.content: public self Model::setPrimary( string $id )   The primary key is used by id, updateRow, delete, erase and the other methods that take an ID. Throws InvalidArgumentException when $id is not a plain name.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$id	string Primary key column name

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(); $model->setPrimary('news_id'); // Same as the following $model = new Model(false, array( 'id' => 'news_id', ));

searchDocs.title: Example​

searchDocs.content: public self Model::setVisible( string|null $visible )   When the model was created with $is_admin = false, reads only return rows whose visible column is 1. null or '' removes the flag. Throws InvalidArgumentException when $visible is not a plain name.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$visible	string/null Public flag column name

searchDocs.content: public self Model::unsetRegularUseQuery()   For the next query only, skips the queries added for every table (regular_use in database_regular_use_query.php, see Configuration): the valid = 1 condition of reads, created / modified / valid on insert and modified on update. disabledRegularUseQuery skips them for good.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(true, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', )); // Include the rows deleted with delete() (valid = 0) $records = $model->unsetRegularUseQuery()->all(); // Count a view without changing "modified" (the table has a view_count column) $model->unsetRegularUseQuery()->increment('view_count', 1);

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public mixed Model::transaction( callable $callback )   Runs $callback in a transaction and returns what it returns. The transaction is committed when the callback returns and rolled back when it throws; the exception is then rethrown.  The callback receives this model.Every query inside the callback takes part, whatever model (or Fegg\Database\Pdo) runs it.A transaction() call inside another one joins the outer transaction.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$callback	callable Receives this model

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Model; $news = new Model(true, array('table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible')); $labs = new Model(true, array('table' => 'cms_lab', 'id' => 'lab_id', 'visible' => 'visible')); $id = $news->transaction(function (Model $news) use ($labs) { $id = $news->insertRow(array('title' => 'A')); $labs->insertRow(array('title' => 'B')); // another model joins the same transaction return $id; });

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public string Model::toSql()   Returns the SELECT that all would run with the conditions set so far, with the values filled in, without running it. Like after a query, the conditions are cleared afterwards. The values are quoted for reading only: never run the result.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); echo $model ->where('category = ?', 2) ->whereIn('news_id', array(1, 2)) ->order('post_date', 'desc') ->limit(5) ->toSql();   Output Select * From "cms_news" Where category = 2 AND news_id IN (1, 2) AND cms_news.visible = '1' And "cms_news".valid = 1 Order By post_date DESC Limit 0, 5

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Model::unsetRegularUseQueryForTable()   For the next query only, skips the queries configured for this table (the table section of database_regular_use_query.php, see Configuration). The queries added for every table still apply; see unsetRegularUseQuery.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(true, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', )); $records = $model->unsetRegularUseQueryForTable()->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public int Model::updateRow( array $row, mixed $id )   Updates the row whose primary key is $id and returns the number of updated rows (0 when there is no such row). Only the given columns are written; null is stored as NULL. modified is set automatically, and bind types are applied.  Throws InvalidArgumentException like insertRow.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$row	array Values (column => value) $id	mixed Target primary ID

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(true, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); // Only title (and modified) are written; the other columns keep their value // Update "cms_news" Set "title"= 'New title', modified = '2026-11-09 17:40:25' Where news_id = 1 $updated = $model->updateRow(array('title' => 'New title'), 1); // -> 1

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public int Model::updateRowsWhere( array $row, string $where, [ mixed $params = [] ] )   Updates every row matching $where and returns the number of updated rows. Columns are written as in updateRow. $params works as in where: one value, or an array of values in placeholder order (an array on a single IN (?) placeholder expands it).  The condition is required: an empty $where throws InvalidArgumentException. Pass '1 = 1' to really update every row. Conditions chained with where are not used.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$row	array Values (column => value) $where	string Condition with ? placeholders $params	mixed	[]	One value, or an array of values in placeholder order

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(true, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); // Hide every news of category 3 $updated = $model->updateRowsWhere(array('visible' => 0), 'category = ?', 3); $updated = $model->updateRowsWhere(array('category' => 1), 'news_id IN (?)', array(4, 5, 6)); // Every row $updated = $model->updateRowsWhere(array('visible' => 1), '1 = 1');

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public int Model::updateWhere( string $item, array $data, string $where, mixed $wh_data )   Updates every row matching $where and returns the number of updated rows. For new code, use updateRowsWhere: updateWhere() writes '' for every column listed in $item that is missing from $data, and cannot store NULL.  $wh_data is one value, or an array with one value per placeholder. The condition is required: an empty $where throws InvalidArgumentException. Pass '1 = 1' to really update every row.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$item	string Columns, separated by commas $data	array Values $where	string Condition with ? placeholders $wh_data	mixed Values for the placeholders

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(true, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); $item = 'title, content'; $data = array( 'title' => 'Sample title', 'content' => 'Sample content', ); $updated = $model->updateWhere($item, $data, 'category = ? AND news_id > ?', array(2, 10));

searchDocs.content: public int Model::update( string $item, array $data, mixed $id )   Updates the row whose primary key is $id and returns the number of updated rows. For new code, use updateRow: update() writes '' for every column listed in $item that is missing from $data, and cannot store NULL. modified is set automatically and bind types are applied.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$item	string Columns, separated by commas $data	array Values $id	mixed Target primary ID

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(true, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); $item = 'title, content'; $data = array( 'title' => 'Sample title', 'content' => 'Sample content', ); $updated = $model->update($item, $data, 1); // -> 1

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public mixed Model::value( string $column )   Returns the first column of the first matching row, or null when nothing matches. $column may be an expression such as 'max(post_date)'; it is written into the SQL as it is, so never put user input in it.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$column	string Column name or SQL expression

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); $title = $model->where('news_id = ?', 5)->value('title'); // -> 'News 5', or null $latest = $model->where('category = ?', 2)->value('max(post_date)'); // -> '2026-01-23 10:00:00'

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Model::whereBetween( string $column, mixed $from, mixed $to, [ string $andOr = 'AND' ] )   Adds column BETWEEN ? AND ?. Both ends are included. Throws InvalidArgumentException when $column is not a plain name.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$column	string Column name $from	mixed Lowest value $to	mixed Highest value $andOr	string	'AND'	How it joins the previous condition: AND or OR

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); // News of January 2026 // ... Where post_date BETWEEN '2026-01-01 00:00:00' AND '2026-01-31 23:59:59' AND ... $records = $model->whereBetween('post_date', '2026-01-01 00:00:00', '2026-01-31 23:59:59')->find();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Model::where( string $query, [ mixed $data = [], string $andOr = 'AND' ] )   Adds a condition with ? placeholders. Values are always bound, never written into the SQL. Several calls are joined with AND (or OR with $andOr).  A query without placeholders ('note IS NULL') needs no $data.An array bound to one placeholder expands it (id IN (?, ?, ...)), see Values and placeholders. An array that cannot be expanded throws when the query runs.An empty $query ('') adds nothing, which is handy for optional search conditions.  A query with its own OR outside brackets is put in brackets when it is joined to other conditions: where('category = ?', 1)->where('title = ? OR summary = ?', array($q, $q)) is category = 1 AND (title = ? OR summary = ?). The conditions the model adds by itself (the visible flag and valid = 1) are joined with AND after yours, with yours in brackets when they have an OR (Where (a = ? OR b = ?) AND ...), so hidden and deleted rows never match. having works the same way. To group conditions inside your own, use whereOpen and whereClose.  For common cases there are helpers that also check the column name: whereIn, whereNotIn, whereLike, whereNull, whereNotNull and whereBetween.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$query	string Condition with ? placeholders (never put user input in it) $data	mixed	[]	One value, or an array of values in placeholder order $andOr	string	'AND'	How it joins the previous condition: AND or OR

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); $records = $model->where('category = ?', 2)->find(); // Select * From "cms_news" Where category = 2 AND cms_news.visible = '1' And "cms_news".valid = 1 ... // Several placeholders: an array in placeholder order $records = $model->where('category = ? AND post_date >= ?', array(2, '2026-01-01'))->find(); // An array on one placeholder: IN (...) $records = $model->where('news_id IN (?)', array(1, 2, 3))->find(); // ... Where news_id IN (1, 2, 3) AND ...

searchDocs.title: Complex WHERE query​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); $model->where('category = ?', 2); $model->whereOpen(); $model->where('title = ?', 'foo'); $model->where('post_date <= ?', '2021-01-01', 'OR'); $model->whereClose(); // Select * // From "cms_news" // Where category = 2 // AND (title = 'foo' OR post_date <= '2021-01-01') // AND cms_news.visible = '1' And "cms_news".valid = 1 $records = $model->find();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Model::whereClose()   Closes the bracket opened with whereOpen.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); $model->where('category = ?', 2); $model->whereOpen(); $model->where('title = ?', 'foo'); $model->where('post_date <= ?', '2021-01-01', 'OR'); $model->whereClose(); // Select * // From "cms_news" // Where category = 2 // AND (title = 'foo' OR post_date <= '2021-01-01') // AND cms_news.visible = '1' And "cms_news".valid = 1 $records = $model->find();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Model::whereIn( string $column, array $values, [ string $andOr = 'AND' ] )   Adds column IN (?, ?, ...). An empty array matches no row (1 = 0), so an empty selection returns nothing instead of failing. Throws InvalidArgumentException when $column is not a plain name.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$column	string Column name (news_id or cms_news.news_id) $values	array Values to match $andOr	string	'AND'	How it joins the previous condition: AND or OR

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); // ... Where news_id IN (1, 2, 3) AND ... $records = $model->whereIn('news_id', array(1, 2, 3))->all(); // ... Where 1 = 0 AND ... (no rows) $records = $model->whereIn('news_id', array())->all();

searchDocs.content: public bool RateLimit::attempt( string $key )   Stores an attempt for $key, then counts the attempts of the window including it. Returns true when there are more than $max: the attempt is refused and its row removed again. Returns false when it is allowed; the attempt then counts until the window has passed, unless undo() takes it back.  Without the table rate_limit it always returns false (see The table).

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$key	string Who is counted: an IP address, a login ID ...

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Log; use Fegg\Tool\RateLimit; $ip = isset($_SERVER['REMOTE_ADDR']) ? (string) $_SERVER['REMOTE_ADDR'] : ''; if ((new RateLimit('contact', 5, 3600))->attempt($ip)) { Log::warning('Contact form: more than 5 mails an hour from {ip}', array('ip' => $ip)); $this->redirect('/contact/error.html'); }   Call it where the work is done (just before sending the mail, when checking the password), not when the form is shown.

searchDocs.content: public self Model::whereOpen( [ string $andOr = 'AND' ] )   Opens a bracket in the WHERE clause; close it with whereClose. The first condition inside the bracket is not prefixed with AND / OR.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$andOr	string	'AND'	How the bracket joins the previous condition: AND or OR

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); $model->where('category = ?', 2); $model->whereOpen(); $model->where('title = ?', 'foo'); $model->where('post_date <= ?', '2021-01-01', 'OR'); $model->whereClose(); // Select * // From "cms_news" // Where category = 2 // AND (title = 'foo' OR post_date <= '2021-01-01') // AND cms_news.visible = '1' And "cms_news".valid = 1 $records = $model->find();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public void RateLimit::clear( string $key )   Removes every attempt of $key in this bucket, for example after a successful login, so earlier failures do not count any more.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$key	string Who is counted

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\RateLimit; $limit = new RateLimit('member-login', 5, 900); if ($limit->attempt($loginId)) { $this->redirect('/member/login/?locked=1'); } if ($this->_checkPassword($loginId, $password)) { $limit->clear($loginId); // ... log in }

searchDocs.title: How to use​
searchDocs.content: Import Fegg\Tool\RateLimit, create it with a bucket name, the attempts allowed and the window, and call attempt(). It returns true when the attempt is refused.  Controller <?php namespace Site\Controller; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; use Fegg\Tool\RateLimit; class Entry extends Controller { public function post() { $this->requirePost(); // 5 entries an hour from one address $limit = new RateLimit('entry', 5, 3600); if ($limit->attempt((string) $_SERVER['REMOTE_ADDR'])) { $this->redirect('/entry/error.html'); } // ... check and save the entry } }   The bucket names the limit: the same key is counted apart in each bucket.

searchDocs.title: How attempts are counted​
searchDocs.content: An attempt counts for $window seconds from the moment it was made (a sliding window, not fixed hours).attempt() stores the attempt first, then counts. Requests sent in parallel cannot all pass the check before any of them is stored.A refused attempt removes its own row, so a client that keeps trying does not extend its lock: it can try again once its oldest counted attempt is older than the window.The key itself is not stored: each row holds the bucket and a sha256 hash of the bucket and the key, so the table holds no addresses or login IDs.Now and then (on about one allowed attempt in 20), rows older than one day, or than the window when it is longer, are removed.

searchDocs.title: The table​
searchDocs.content: rate_limit is a core table (core/config/database/rate_limit.yaml), created by fegg-cli migration (see fegg-cli).  Without the table nothing is limited: every attempt is allowed, so the page keeps working, and one line per request goes to the PHP error log:  Fegg: rate limiting is off (...). Run `fegg-cli migration` to create the table rate_limit.   Run fegg-cli migration after deploying a project that uses RateLimit for the first time.

searchDocs.title: In the skeleton​
searchDocs.content: Where	Bucket	Key	LimitCMS login (core/controller/Cms/Login.php)	cms-login	Login ID + address	5 in 15 minutes CMS login	cms-login-address	Address	20 in 15 minutes Contact form (site/controller/Contact.php)	contact:<template>	Address	rate_limit_per_hour an hour  The CMS login takes back the attempt of the address when the per-login limit refuses (undo()), and after a successful login forgets the failures of that login (clear()) and takes back the attempt of the address. A locked login shows a message on the login page.  The contact form counts sent mails, checked just before sending. Its limit is $_RATE_LIMIT_PER_HOUR in site/config/contact/contact_config.php (5 by default; 0 turns it off):  htdocs/_fegg/site/config/contact/contact_config.php // Mails one visitor (IP address) can send per hour (Fegg\Tool\RateLimit); 0 = no limit $_RATE_LIMIT_PER_HOUR = 5;   note The skeleton uses $_SERVER['REMOTE_ADDR'] as the address. Behind a reverse proxy or a CDN that does not pass the visitor's address to PHP there, every visitor has the proxy's address and shares one limit.

searchDocs.title: Errors​
searchDocs.content: A bucket name that is empty or longer than 64 characters, or $max / $window below 1, throws \InvalidArgumentException.A missing table does not throw (see The table).

searchDocs.title: Methods​
searchDocs.content: 📄️RateLimit::__construct Create a limit 📄️RateLimit::attempt Record an attempt and check the limit 📄️RateLimit::isLimited Check whether the next attempt would be refused 📄️RateLimit::remaining Attempts left in the window 📄️RateLimit::undo Take back the last allowed attempt 📄️RateLimit::clear Forget the attempts of a key

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public RateLimit::__construct( string $bucket, int $max, int $window )   Creates a limit of $max attempts in $window seconds. Keys are counted apart in each bucket.  Throws \InvalidArgumentException when $bucket is empty or longer than 64 characters, or $max or $window is below 1.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$bucket	string Name of the limit (1 to 64 characters): 'contact', 'cms-login' $max	int Attempts allowed in the window $window	int Seconds

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\RateLimit; $perHour = new RateLimit('entry', 5, 3600); // 5 an hour $perDay = new RateLimit('entry-day', 20, 86400); // and 20 a day

Use it to show a message before the visitor fills in a form. To enforce the limit, use attempt(): two requests can both see isLimited() return false.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​

searchDocs.content: public RSS::__construct( string $url, [ array $options = array() ] )   Loads and parses an RSS 1.0, RSS 2.0 or Atom feed. The entries can then be read with RSS::fetch or RSS::fetchAll.  An http:// or https:// URL is fetched with Fegg\Http\Client; any other value is read as a local file.  Throws a \RuntimeException when:  the URL cannot be fetched (connection error, timeout, or an HTTP status other than 200);the file does not exist or cannot be read;the document is not XML, or is not an RSS or Atom feed.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$url	string Feed URL, or the path of a file $options	array	array()	Options (see below)  Key	Data type	Default	Remarksskip_pr	boolean	false	true: leave out the posts whose title contains PR: (advertisements of some blog services) timeout	int	10	Seconds for the whole request (the connection: 3 seconds)

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\RSS; try { $rss = new RSS('https://example.com/feed', array('skip_pr' => true, 'timeout' => 5)); } catch (\RuntimeException $e) { // cannot be fetched, or not a feed: $e->getMessage() } // A local file $rss = new RSS(FEGG_SITE_DIR . '/data/feed.xml');

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public void RateLimit::undo()   Removes the attempt stored by the last allowed attempt() of this object, when it turned out not to count. Nothing happens when the last attempt was refused or undo() was already called.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: The CMS login checks two limits. When the second refuses, the attempt of the first is taken back, and a successful login does not count against the address:  htdocs/_fegg/core/controller/Cms/Login.php $perAddress = new RateLimit('cms-login-address', 20, 900); $perLogin = new RateLimit('cms-login', 5, 900); if ($perAddress->attempt($ip)) { $this->redirect($this->page['prefix'] . 'login/index/LOCKED'); } if ($perLogin->attempt($loginKey)) { $perAddress->undo(); $this->redirect($this->page['prefix'] . 'login/index/LOCKED'); } // ... password checked $perLogin->clear($loginKey); $perAddress->undo();

searchDocs.title: How to use​
searchDocs.content: Import Fegg\Tool\RSS and create it with new, passing the feed URL. The constructor throws a \RuntimeException when the feed cannot be fetched or read, or is not RSS or Atom, so catch it when the feed may be unavailable.  Controller <?php namespace Site\Controller; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; use Fegg\Tool\RSS; class Index extends Controller { public function index() { try { $rss = new RSS('https://example.com/feed'); $this->page['posts'] = $rss->fetchAll(10); } catch (\RuntimeException $e) { $this->page['posts'] = array(); } $this->displayPage('index'); } }

searchDocs.title: Entry data​
searchDocs.content: Each entry returned by RSS::fetch and RSS::fetchAll is an array with these keys. A field the feed does not have is '' (an empty array for category and tag).  Key	Data type	Remarkstitle	string	Title pubDate	string	Date as written in the feed (RSS 2.0: pubDate, or dc:date; RSS 1.0: dc:date; Atom: published, or updated) datetime	DateTime/null	pubDate as a DateTime object, null when there is no date or it cannot be read link	string	Link URL (Atom: the href of <link rel="alternate">) description	string	Description (RSS: HTML entities decoded; Atom: summary) content	string	content:encoded (HTML entities decoded); Atom: content author	string	dc:creator (RSS 2.0: or author; Atom: author > name) category	array	Category names (RSS 2.0: category; RSS 1.0: dc:subject; Atom: the term of category) tag	array	Always an empty array (not implemented)

searchDocs.title: Methods​
searchDocs.content: 📄️RSS::__construct Load RSS feed 📄️RSS::fetch Fetch the next entry of RSS feed 📄️RSS::fetchAll Fetch all entries or specified number of entries of RSS feed

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public mixed RSS::fetch()   Returns the next entry as an array (see Entry data), or false when there are no more entries.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\RSS; $rss = new RSS('https://example.com/feed'); while ($post = $rss->fetch()) { // $post['title'], $post['link'], $post['datetime'] ... }

searchDocs.content: public Sitemap::__construct( [ string $baseUrl = '' ] )   $baseUrl is the root URL that paths are added to. '' uses the URL of the current request (FEGG_CURRENT_URL: the scheme, the host and the base path).

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$baseUrl	string	''	Root URL of the site, with the base path. '': the current request

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\Sitemap; $sitemap = new Sitemap(); // URLs of the current host $sitemap = new Sitemap('https://www.example.com'); // always the production host   Pass the root URL when the sitemap is written outside a request (a command that saves it as a file).

searchDocs.title: How to use​
searchDocs.content: The skeleton serves /sitemap.xml with Site\Controller\Sitemap: the pages listed in site/config/sitemap.php, then every published news post.  htdocs/_fegg/site/controller/Sitemap.php <?php namespace Site\Controller; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; use Fegg\Model; use Fegg\Tool\Sitemap as SitemapXml; class Sitemap extends Controller implements \Fegg\Http\RouteOnly { public function index() { $sitemap = new SitemapXml(); foreach ($this->loadConfig('sitemap') as $path) { $sitemap->add($path); } // Published posts only: new Model(false, ...) leaves out the hidden ones $news = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); foreach ($news->select('news_id, modified')->order('post_date', 'desc')->all() as $row) { $sitemap->add('/news/post_' . $row['news_id'] . '.html', $row['modified']); } $sitemap->display(); } }   htdocs/_fegg/site/config/sitemap.php $sitemap = array( '/', '/news/', '/contact/', );   htdocs/_fegg/site/config/route.php $route['sitemap.xml'] = 'sitemap/index';   The controller is route-only: it answers /sitemap.xml and nothing else.  For a new project:  Add the project's pages to site/config/sitemap.php, and add the posts of other CMS sections in the controller as for the news.Leave out pages that are not for search results: form steps, thank-you pages, the CMS.Give no date to the pages of sitemap.php: the dates of their files change on every deploy. Give the posts their modified date.  Tell search engines where the sitemap is with a line in htdocs/robots.txt (an absolute URL):  htdocs/robots.txt Sitemap: https://www.example.com/sitemap.xml   Output <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <urlset xmlns="http://www.sitemaps.org/schemas/sitemap/0.9"> <url> <loc>https://www.example.com/</loc> </url> <url> <loc>https://www.example.com/news/post_12.html</loc> <lastmod>2026-11-15T10:00:00+09:00</lastmod> </url> </urlset>   Only <loc> and <lastmod> are written: search engines ignore <changefreq> and <priority>. A sitemap lists at most 50,000 URLs.

searchDocs.title: Absolute URLs​
searchDocs.content: Paths are made absolute with feggAbsoluteUrl(), a function you can also call yourself (it is used by JSON-LD and Feed too):  feggAbsoluteUrl('/news/'); // https://www.example.com/news/ feggAbsoluteUrl('https://other.example.com/'); // returned as it is feggAbsoluteUrl('/x/', 'https://example.org'); // https://example.org/x/   string feggAbsoluteUrl( string $path [, string $baseUrl = '' ] )   $path is a path of the site without the base path: FEGG_CURRENT_URL (the scheme, the host and the base path, like {{ base_url }}) is put before it. When the site is installed in /sub/, '/news/' becomes https://example.com/sub/news/.http:// and https:// URLs are returned as they are; //host/... gets the scheme of the request.$baseUrl replaces FEGG_CURRENT_URL, for example in a command, where there is no request.  The URLs use the host of the request: on a test server, the sitemap lists the test server's URLs.  A URL that already contains the base path, such as the result of getImageUrl(), only needs the domain: FEGG_CURRENT_DOMAIN . getImageUrl($id).

searchDocs.title: Errors​
searchDocs.content: A URL that is not http or https, or contains spaces or control characters, throws \InvalidArgumentException. So does a date that cannot be read.A 50,001st URL throws \LengthException.

searchDocs.title: Methods​
searchDocs.content: 📄️Sitemap::__construct Create an empty sitemap 📄️Sitemap::add Add a page 📄️Sitemap::count Number of URLs added 📄️Sitemap::toXml Return the sitemap XML 📄️Sitemap::display Send the sitemap and end the response

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public Sitemap Sitemap::add( string $loc [, string|int|\DateTimeInterface|null $lastmod = null ] )   Adds a page and returns the sitemap, so calls can be chained. A path is made absolute (see Absolute URLs). A URL added twice is listed once, with the date of the last call.  $lastmod is written as a W3C date with the time zone (2026-11-15T10:00:00+09:00). null, '' and '0000-00-00 00:00:00' write no date.  Throws \InvalidArgumentException for a URL that is not http or https or a date that cannot be read, and \LengthException for more than 50,000 URLs.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$loc	string Path of the site without the base path ('/news/'), or an http(s) URL $lastmod	string|int|DateTimeInterface|null	null	When the page last changed: 'Y-m-d H:i:s' from the database, a Unix time or a date object

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\Sitemap; $sitemap = new Sitemap(); $sitemap->add('/') ->add('/about/') ->add('/news/post_12.html', '2026-11-15 10:00:00');

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public int Sitemap::count()   Returns the number of URLs in the sitemap (a URL added twice counts once).

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\Sitemap; $sitemap = new Sitemap(); $sitemap->add('/')->add('/news/')->add('/'); $sitemap->count(); // 2

searchDocs.content: public void Sitemap::display()   Sends the sitemap with Content-Type: application/xml; charset=UTF-8 and ends the response (it throws Fegg\Http\Halt, like displayPage()). Code after it does not run.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\Sitemap as SitemapXml; public function index() { $sitemap = new SitemapXml(); foreach ($this->loadConfig('sitemap') as $path) { $sitemap->add($path); } $sitemap->display(); }   Inside a controller named Sitemap, import the library under another name (as SitemapXml), as the skeleton does.

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public string Sitemap::toXml()   Returns the sitemap as XML text, in the order the URLs were added. display() sends the same text.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: use Fegg\Tool\Sitemap; $sitemap = new Sitemap('https://www.example.com'); $sitemap->add('/')->add('/news/post_12.html', '2026-11-15 10:00:00'); file_put_contents(FEGG_HTML_DIR . '/sitemap.xml', $sitemap->toXml());   Output <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <urlset xmlns="http://www.sitemaps.org/schemas/sitemap/0.9"> <url> <loc>https://www.example.com/</loc> </url> <url> <loc>https://www.example.com/news/post_12.html</loc> <lastmod>2026-11-15T10:00:00+09:00</lastmod> </url> </urlset>

searchDocs.content: public bool Trim::create()   Saves the resized image to the output path given to Trim::setImage. Missing directories are created. JPEG images are saved with quality 90.  The image is written next to the output path first and then renamed, so a request at the same time never reads half a file. Returns false when it could not be saved.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\Trim; $trim = new Trim(); $trim->setImage('path/to/image.jpg', 'path/to/converted.jpg'); $trim->resizeTrim(300, 300, 'm'); if (!$trim->create()) { // could not be saved }

searchDocs.title: How to use​
searchDocs.content: Import Fegg\Tool\Trim and create it with new. Set the source image and the output path with Trim::setImage, resize it with one of the resize* methods, then save it with Trim::create or send it without saving with Trim::output.  Controller <?php namespace Site\Controller; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; use Fegg\Tool\Trim; class Thumbnail extends Controller { public function index() { $trim = new Trim(); try { $trim->setImage('path/to/image.jpg', 'path/to/thumbnail/300_300.jpg'); } catch (\RuntimeException $e) { http_response_code(404); $this->halt('Not Found'); } $trim->resizeTrim(300, 300, 'm'); if ($trim->create()) { // Output the saved image to the browser $trim->view(); } $this->halt(); } }

searchDocs.title: Images of the CMS in other sizes​
searchDocs.content: The images uploaded in the CMS are shown in other sizes through URLs such as /_fegg/site/up_dir/image/12/i-300_200.jpg, built by the getImageUrl modifier ({{ $page.data.image_id|getImageUrl:300:200 }}).  /_fegg/site/up_dir/image/{id}/{type}-{width}_{height}.{jpg|png|gif} /_fegg/site/up_dir/image/{id}/{type}-{width}.{jpg|png|gif} /_fegg/site/up_dir/image/{id}/{type}.{jpg|png|gif}   Fegg\Controller\Up_dir::image() makes a missing size with this class and saves it at that path; later requests get the saved file.  type	Method	Resulti	Trim::resize	Within the size, keeping the ratio c	Trim::resizeFill	Exactly the size, the empty area white or transparent f	Trim::resizeForce	Stretched to the size lt t rt l m r lb b rb	Trim::resizeTrim	Fills the size, keeping that part of the image  A missing width or height is the original one. A name that is not one of these (x-10.jpg, I-10.JPG), an unknown image ID or a file that is not an image is a 404.  Two settings of htdocs/_fegg/site/config/upload_dir.php keep anyone from filling the disk or the memory with sizes:  Key	Default	Remarksimage_max	2000	Largest width or height that can be asked for. A larger one is a 404 image_cache_max	50	How many sizes of one image are saved. Past that, new sizes are made for each request (Trim::output) and not saved  htdocs/_fegg/site/config/upload_dir.php $upload_dir['image_max'] = 2000; $upload_dir['image_cache_max'] = 50;

searchDocs.title: Methods​
searchDocs.content: 📄️Trim::setImage Set target image and output file path 📄️Trim::getSize Get the width and height of the loaded image 📄️Trim::resize Resize the image to fit in the specified size with keeping ratio 📄️Trim::resizeFill Resize the image with keeping ratio and filling the empty area (Like object-fit: contain) 📄️Trim::resizeForce Resize the image to the specified size ignoring ratio 📄️Trim::resizeTrim Resize the image with keeping ratio and trimming the overflow (Like object-fit: cover) 📄️Trim::create Save the image to the output path 📄️Trim::output Output the image to the browser without saving it 📄️Trim::view Output the saved image to the browser

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public array Trim::getSize()   Returns array(width, height) of the image loaded by Trim::setImage, after its Exif orientation (a photo taken upright gives the upright size).

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\Trim; $trim = new Trim(); $trim->setImage('path/to/image.jpg', 'path/to/converted.jpg'); list($width, $height) = $trim->getSize(); if ($width > $height) { $trim->resize(600, 0); } else { $trim->resize(0, 600); } $trim->create();

searchDocs.title: Arguments​

searchDocs.content: public void Trim::resizeFill( int $w, int $h )   The output is exactly $w x $h. The image is scaled down to fit in it, keeping its aspect ratio, and placed in the center. The empty area is transparent for PNG output (and for GIF output from a PNG or GIF source), white otherwise. Images smaller than the specified size are not enlarged.

searchDocs.content: public void Trim::resizeTrim( int $w, int $h, string $cp )   The output is exactly $w x $h. The image is scaled to cover the whole area, keeping its aspect ratio, and the overflow is cut off. $cp decides which part of the image is kept.

searchDocs.content: The positions are listed in Trim::POSITIONS.  $cp	Kept partlt	Top left t	Top center rt	Top right l	Middle left m	Center r	Middle right lb	Bottom left b	Bottom center rb	Bottom right  Any other value is lt.

searchDocs.content: public void Trim::setImage( string $org_path, string $cnv_path )   Loads the source image. The output format is decided by the extension of $cnv_path: jpg (or jpeg), png or gif. A JPEG photo is turned the way its Exif orientation says.  Throws a \RuntimeException when:  $org_path is not a file;the extension of $cnv_path is not jpg, jpeg, png or gif;$org_path is not a JPEG, PNG or GIF image, or cannot be read.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$org_path	string Source image path $cnv_path	string Output image path (.jpg, .jpeg, .png or .gif)

searchDocs.title: Other languages​
searchDocs.content: When a language code is passed to the constructor (new Upload('en')), the messages are read from config/en/file_error_message.php (searched in site/config/ first, then core/config/).

searchDocs.title: How to use​
searchDocs.content: Import Fegg\Tool\Upload and create it with new. Set the upload directory, then call Upload::upload with the name of the input[type="file"].  Controller <?php namespace Site\Controller; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; use Fegg\Tool\Upload; class Entry extends Controller { public function post() { $this->loadConfig('upload_dir'); $upload = new Upload(); $upload->setUploadDir($this->config['upload_dir']['path'] . '/entry'); $upload->setMaxFileSize(5); $upload->setFileType(array('jpg', 'jpeg', 'png', 'pdf')); if ($upload->upload('file', uniqid('f_'), 'Attachment')) { $data = $upload->getUploadedData('file'); // $data['name'], $data['org_name'], $data['type'], $data['size'] ... } else { $errors = $upload->getErrorMessage('file'); } } }   $this->loadConfig('upload_dir') reads site/config/upload_dir.php (path htdocs/_fegg/site/up_dir and url /_fegg/site/up_dir) into $this->config['upload_dir']. The CMS screens (Fegg\Controller\Cms\Image, Media, Multi) use this class in the same way.  Error messages are defined in file_error_message.php, see Configuration.

searchDocs.title: What is checked​
searchDocs.content: Upload::upload checks, in order:  Upload errors and the size (@empty, @size, @failed).The extension must be allowed by setFileType. Script extensions (php, phtml, phar, cgi ...) are refused even when listed (@type).The content must match the extension (@content): images (jpg, jpeg, png, gif, webp) must be readable by getimagesize(), and for the extensions of Upload::MIME_TYPES the MIME type reported by finfo must be one of the types listed for the extension. A PHP file renamed to .jpg, or a text file named .pdf, is refused.  When the file is saved:  Files are saved under the name you give (uniqid('f_'), ...), never under the visitor's file name. Keep the original name (org_name) in the database only.Directories are created with mode 0755 and files saved with 0644.

searchDocs.title: MIME types​
searchDocs.content: Upload::MIME_TYPES is the one table of types by extension (jpg, png, gif, webp, pdf, the Office formats such as docx, xlsm, pptx, and zip, txt, csv). For each extension:  every type listed is accepted from finfo when the file is uploaded;the first type is the one the stored file is sent with (Upload::mimeType).  Upload::MIME_TYPES['docx']; // array('application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document', 'application/zip', 'application/octet-stream')   An extension that is not in the table is checked by its extension only, and sent with the type finfo reads from it.

searchDocs.title: Protecting the upload directory​
searchDocs.content: The upload directory htdocs/_fegg/site/up_dir/ is inside _fegg/, which is denied; the root .htaccess lets /_fegg/site/up_dir/ through and sends a file that is not there (an image size not made yet, /file/<id>/) to PHP. When the upload directory is below the document root, setUploadDir writes an .htaccess into it (Upload::HTACCESS, an existing file is left alone) that serves only the file types that can be uploaded and runs no script, so an uploaded file can never run as code. The CMS dashboard also writes it when it opens, and the skeleton ships the file.  fegg-cli doctor and the CMS dashboard report a missing site/up_dir/.htaccess or a missing root rule (see fegg-cli). Remember it when you upload over FTP: many FTP clients skip dotfiles. On nginx, .htaccess is ignored: use the location ^~ /_fegg/site/up_dir/ block of Directory structure.

searchDocs.title: Sending stored files​
searchDocs.content: The CMS sends stored files (/_fegg/site/up_dir/file/<id>/, the media and image screens) with Fegg\Http\Download::sendHeaders(). It sends X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, a valid Cache-Control, and an RFC 6266 Content-Disposition with the original name escaped (an ASCII fallback plus the UTF-8 name). HTML, SVG, XML and JavaScript files are always sent as attachments, never shown inline. Use it when your own controller sends a stored file:  Controller use Fegg\Http\Download; Download::sendHeaders(array( 'type' => $file['type'], 'size' => filesize($path), 'org_name' => $file['org_name'], ), false); // false: browser cache only (private); true: public $this->halt(file_get_contents($path));

Key	Remarksname	Saved file name ($up_name + extension) org_name	Original file name type	MIME type: from getimagesize() for images, otherwise Upload::mimeType size	File size (bytes) up_time	Upload time (Unix timestamp) width	Image width (images only) height	Image height (images only) attr	width="..." height="..." string (images only)

searchDocs.content: public static string Upload::mimeType( string $path, string $extension )   Returns the first type of Upload::MIME_TYPES for $extension (case does not matter). For an extension that is not in the table, returns the type finfo reads from the file $path, or application/octet-stream when it cannot be read.  Upload::upload uses it for the type of a file that is not an image (Upload::getUploadedData).

searchDocs.title: Arguments​

Returns true when the directory is writable, otherwise false and the directory is not set.  When the directory is below the document root and has no .htaccess, Upload::HTACCESS is written there: it serves only the file types that can be uploaded and runs no script (see Introduction). An existing .htaccess is left alone.

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public boolean Upload::setFileType( array $type )   Replaces the list of allowed extensions. The extensions are compared in lower case. Returns false when $type is not an array. The default is array('jpg', 'jpeg', 'png', 'gif').  Extensions a web server may run as code (php, php5, phtml, phar, pht, phps, cgi, pl, py, rb, sh, asp, aspx, jsp, shtml, htaccess, htpasswd) are always refused, even when listed here. The file's content must also match its extension (see Upload::upload).

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$type	array Allowed extensions, without the leading dot

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\Upload; $upload = new Upload(); $upload->setFileType(array('pdf', 'docx', 'xlsx'));

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public boolean Upload::upload( string $name, string $up_name, [ string $label = 'ファイル', boolean $required = true ] )   Checks the file posted as $_FILES[$name] and moves it to {upload directory}/{$up_name}.{extension} with mode 0644. The extension is the lower-cased extension of the original file name.  The size, the extension and the content are checked first (see What is checked).  Returns true on success. On failure it returns false and the error messages are available with Upload::getErrorMessage.  No file selected, or a field that the form does not have (no $_FILES[$name]): @empty, or true without saving anything when $required is false.Several files in one field (name="file[]") are not handled by this method: the result is @failed. Give each file its own field.  Neither case writes a PHP warning.  Set the upload directory with Upload::setUploadDir before calling this method.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$name	string name attribute of the input[type="file"] $up_name	string File name to save, without extension $label	string	'ファイル'	Item label used in the error messages $required	boolean	true	false: no error when no file is selected

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\Upload; $upload = new Upload(); $upload->setUploadDir($this->config['upload_dir']['path']); if ($upload->upload('image', uniqid('i_'), 'Image')) { $data = $upload->getUploadedData('image'); } else { $errors = $upload->getErrorMessage('image'); } // Optional file $upload->upload('attachment', uniqid('a_'), 'Attachment', false);
